sections.title: 2. Who the exam is for
sections.html:
As a candidate for this Microsoft Certification, you’re a contact center engineer or solutions pro who designs, implements, and supports AI-powered contact center solutions by using Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center and service-oriented autonomous agents. Your role involves translating business and service requirements into scalable, well-governed contact center solutions that include human representatives and AI-driven capabilities.

In this role, you’re responsible for:

  • Configuring workstreams and engagement channels.
  • Designing, managing, and implementing routing strategies.
  • Configuring service representative profiles and experiences.
  • Enabling productivity tools, including Microsoft Copilot–assisted guidance.
  • Implementing and managing agents for customer self-service.
  • Identifying implementation opportunities for and managing service-oriented autonomous agents.
  • Working with Dynamics 365 Contact Center tools for continuous improvement.
  • Monitoring and resolving operational issues identified in the contact center.
  • Configuring proactive engagement capabilities, including outbound dial modes and journey orchestration.
  • Configuring workforce management capabilities, including demand forecasting, scheduling, and skills alignment.

You typically collaborate with customer service leaders, contact center managers, IT teams, and legal and compliance stakeholders to help ensure that solutions align with operational goals, organizational policies, and responsible AI principles, including security, data protection, transparency, and accountability.

For this exam, you should have:

  • Experience implementing or planning to implement contact center as a service (CCaaS) solutions.
  • An understanding of how voice, social, and digital channels are used and orchestrated in a contact center.
  • Familiarity with contact center personas, such as representatives, supervisors, and administrators.
  • A fundamental understanding of agents, along with AI self-service and AI-assisted experiences.
  • Experience working in or supporting business environments that focus on agent productivity, routing, service performance.
  • Familiarity with the supervisor role and related activities.

Additionally, you should have experience with Microsoft Power Platform, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Foundry. You should know how to use automation, integrations, and AI capabilities to extend and optimize service workflows. You also need to understand how to design modern contact centers, where human representatives, AI agents, and autonomous AI agents work together within secure, compliant, and well-governed systems.

Source: Official study guide (audience profile), updated 2026-10-19.

sections.title: 4. How to read the skills measured
sections.html:
• The bullets illustrate how a skill is assessed; related topics may appear (Microsoft's own note in the study guide). Treat each bullet as a heading for everything around it.
  • Most questions cover generally available (GA) features, but Preview features can appear when they are commonly used. Where the documentation labels something preview, retired or renamed, this guide says so.
  • Expect scenario questions (pick the right setting, path, role or sequence for a requirement) and decision questions (X versus Y). Exact names, menu paths and limits matter.
  • Case studies present a business scenario followed by several questions. Read the requirements and constraints once, then answer every question against them. Microsoft's break rules differ inside case-study and problem/solution sets.

sections.title: What this means for your preparation
sections.html:
• If you studied or hold MB-240: treat AB-250 as a fresh exam. Microsoft’s retirement FAQ says: “To earn the new Certification, you need to pass the new exam, since the new exam and the old one don’t measure the same skill sets.” Your MB-240 certification stays valid until it expires; retirement does not revoke it.
  • If you hold MB-230: you already cover much of §1.3, §3.1, §4.1, §4.2 and §5.1 to §5.3. Put your time into Implement channels (30–35%), voice agents (§3.2), workforce management and proactive outbound (§2.3), and the supervisor and analytics domain (10–15%).
  • Plan by weight: Implement channels is the largest AB-250 domain. Its third group, Configure channel features (§2.3), alone lists 26 skills, including workforce management, proactive outbound, and design, best-practice and total-cost topics.
  • Watch for edits: the AB-250 study guide shows no “skills measured as of” date and no change log, so a change would appear only as an edit to the live page. Recheck it shortly before you sit the exam.

sections.title: 1.1 Implement Dynamics 365 Contact Center
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure the Copilot Service workspace • Configure and extend connectors for Dynamics 365 Contact Center • Configure embedded Dynamics 365 Contact Center mode • Configure Copilot for third-party CCaaS solutions • Enable agent simulation to evaluate journeys • Enable the Health Agent to proactively investigate issues • Enable agents to perform transformation, environment migration, and configuration. Build it in a trial or sandbox: open the workspace as a representative, create and assign an experience profile, run the Salesforce connector wizard, add the widget to a CRM, run the contact center health check and try Conversational Setup.

Configure the Copilot Service workspace

Copilot Service workspace (CSW, formerly Customer Service workspace) is the representative-facing app in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. It is installed automatically in every Contact Center organization; reps open it from the Dynamics 365 apps page and need the Omnichannel agent role. You configure it in Copilot Service admin center (formerly Customer Service admin center / Omnichannel admin center) with System Administrator or System Customizer (every site-map entry), App Profile Manager administrator + Basic User (experience profiles) or Omnichannel administrator + Basic User (chat, voice, queues, workstreams).

  • Sessions and tabs: up to nine sessions, and up to 10 tabs within a session. Opening a case from the Home session, accepting a conversation, global search, a Quick Create notification or creating a record starts a new session; a record opened from the timeline, a form lookup, or a site-map view or dashboard opens as a new tab in the focused session.
  • Multisession works only in the out-of-the-box CSW app, not in a custom app or a copy of CSW. The inbox (turned on per profile) holds asynchronous work such as SMS, persistent chat, WhatsApp and Teams; the productivity pane uses Smart Assist; session restore is no longer a preview feature (an administrator turns it on under Miscellaneous > New and upcoming features > Manage), and without it a browser refresh reloads only the home page.
  • Client requirements: the latest three major releases of Edge or Chrome, 4 GB RAM, latency of 150 ms or less within a country/region (300 ms or less across regions), throughput of at least 4 Mbps. Keep the CSW tab from being discarded when inactive so unified routing works. CSW isn't supported on mobile devices or Unified Service Desk.

Experience profiles tailor CSW for a team and are the alternative to building custom apps (they bundle session templates, conversation channels and productivity tools). A user with no profile gets the out-of-the-box default profile; the three out-of-box profiles can't be modified, deleted or made the default.

TaskHow
Create (needs App Profile Manager Administrator + Basic User)Support experience > Workspaces > Experience profiles > New: Name, Unique name (<prefix>_<name>), Description, then Create
ConfigureAdd Users; Add entity session template; Productivity pane On with options (Copilot, Knowledge search, Agent scripts, Smart assist, Teams chats and others); Inbox > Edit; Channel providers > Edit (All active channels, third-party voice providers)
Give everyone a custom experienceSet as default on one custom profile (use Remove Default first to switch); users with a specific profile keep theirs
Assign by security roleSet rank and roles: a user with several mapped roles gets the profile with the higher rank (rank 1 beats rank 2); assignment by team membership isn't allowed; making a profile the default removes its role mappings
AuditSearch by user shows the assignment method: Default, Role-based or Direct

Order of work: create users and assign roles (Customer Service Representative or Omnichannel agent), build workstreams, queues, session templates and productivity tools, then create and assign experience profiles; an existing org needs only the last two steps. A new organization can use the Home page Create your contact center wizard (live chat, voice, a default profile and recommended AI features in one click; new organizations only). Roles and users: §1.3.

Exam traps
  • Nine sessions and 10 tabs per session: candidates swap the numbers, and no setting raises them.
  • Copying the CSW app (or building a custom app) to remove tools loses multisession; use an experience profile instead.
  • Out-of-box profiles are read-only. To change what a team sees, create a custom profile; to apply it by role, set a rank and roles, not a team.

Configure and extend connectors for Dynamics 365 Contact Center

Connectors let Contact Center work with a non-Microsoft CRM by copying Contact and Account data into Dataverse, so incoming customers are recognized. The copy is one-way: edits made to synced rows in Dataverse are not written back to the CRM, so change the data in the CRM only.

CRMMechanismWhere you configure it
SalesforceBuilt-in wizard, no flowsCopilot Service admin center > Support experience > Workspaces > Data synchronization from external CRMs > Manage > New (or Home > CRM connection wizard > Open)
ServiceNow, ZendeskPower Automate flows downloaded from GitHub, plus webhooks or business rules for incremental syncPower Automate and the CRM
Any other CRMYour own flows: a Power Automate connector, HTTP action (Basic authentication, JSON), webhooks, business rules, or Apex triggersPower Automate
  • Salesforce prerequisites: System administrator in both Contact Center and Salesforce, a Contact Center license, and a Salesforce license for change data capture. Recommended: back up the Dataverse Contact and Account tables first and keep the data under 10 GB.
  • Salesforce wizard, in order: New, then Create a CRM connector > Salesforce (signs in through a Power Apps connection), agree to share connector permissions, Enable salesforce permissions (do the listed steps in Salesforce and tick the box), Choose tables to sync (Contacts and Accounts; select both to keep the relationship), Column mapping (only compatible data types appear), Teams permissions, review, Create, tick the activate box, Done.
  • Teams permissions means a Dataverse team whose ID is used to write the data. It needs read and write permission on the selected tables, otherwise synchronization fails. Dataverse doesn't support the Virtual and EntityName data types.
  • Power Automate connectors (ServiceNow, Zendesk, any CRM) need a Power Platform System administrator, a Contact Center license that includes Power Apps and Power Automate, the same environment for both, the msdyn_ContactCenterCRMConnector connector, and the Source CRM, Source CRM ID and Source CRM URL columns on the Account and Contact tables.
  • ServiceNow order: configure View-In-CRM (a calculated Base URL field, u_base_url); import the flows (My flows > Import > Import Package (legacy); imported flows are disabled by default, so select Turn on); configure incremental sync (create the REST message first, then the business rule; it needs the ServiceNow Customer Service plugin, and the endpoint is the HTTP URL from the flow's Manual trigger); run the flow.
  • Any CRM: run an initial sync with manual triggers (use pagination, because Power Automate connectors limit the records returned per call), then an incremental sync with automated triggers on create, update and delete.

Configure embedded Dynamics 365 Contact Center mode

In the embedded experience the Contact Center conversation widget runs inside a non-Microsoft CRM (or any web page or app that supports HTML and JavaScript), so reps chat and take calls without leaving it. In the standalone experience reps work in Copilot Service workspace. Learn pages state in an "Applies to" line whether they cover Contact Center embedded, Contact Center standalone or Customer Service.

Common prerequisites: the system requirements are met; omnichannel capabilities are enabled (provision channels, §1.2); the provisioning user has System Administrator permissions in the CRM; and you have the widget URL: Copilot Service admin center welcome page > Open under Your default contact center > Conversation widget tab > Integration into third-party systems.

SalesforceServiceNow
Extra prerequisiteCall-center definition file Dynamics365CallCenter.xml from the Microsoft GitHub repo (GitHub sign-in needed)OpenFrame plugin installed (System Definition > Plugins)
Register the widgetIn the file, replace the CTI Adapter URL with the widget URL; Setup > Call Center > Continue > Import the file; Manage Call Center Users > Add more users > SaveAll > OpenFrame > Configurations > New: Name and Title Dynamics 365 Contact Center, URL = widget URL
DisplaySoftphone Layouts: Is Default Layout ticked; App Manager > edit Service Console > Utility Items > Open CTI Softphone, width 400, height 600Width 400, height 700
  • To connect Copilot to Salesforce data, create the non-Microsoft CRM connection with the right sign-in URI and v58.0 as the Salesforce API version.
  • Copilot feature differences (Learn comparison table): Copilot analytics and trusted webpages as knowledge sources are not available in the embedded experience (they are in standalone); resolution notes are generated in the embedded experience only; auto and proactive prompts based on case data are not available in standalone. Ask a question, write an email and conversation summaries work in both.
Exam traps
  • "Teams permissions" in the Salesforce wizard is a Dataverse team, not Microsoft Teams. The wizard syncs only Contacts and Accounts, and changes in Dataverse never flow back.
  • Imported ServiceNow flows are off until you turn them on, and incremental sync needs the REST message before the business rule plus the Customer Service plugin.
  • Salesforce softphone is 400 x 600; ServiceNow OpenFrame is 400 x 700. The widget URL comes from the Conversation widget tab in Copilot Service admin center.
  • Embedded mode keeps the CRM as the rep's desktop and adds Contact Center to it; it is not the Customer Service product and it needs System Administrator rights in the CRM.

Configure Copilot for third-party CCaaS solutions

No Learn page carries this exact title. The topic is covered by Microsoft's contact center reference architectures plus the Copilot admin settings. Start with the decision: which parts of the stack does the customer keep?

Customer wantsMicrosoft product
Add generative AI to the existing CCaaS and existing CRM (self-service and agent productivity)Copilot (named Copilot for Service on the architecture page) and Copilot Studio
Replace the CCaaS, keep the CRMDynamics 365 Contact Center (embedded in the CRM, or standalone)
Replace the CRM, keep the CCaaSDynamics 365 Customer Service Enterprise
Consolidate vendors on one AI-infused platformDynamics 365 Customer Service Premium

In the "keep both" architecture customers still reach you through your CCaaS channels and telephony; Copilot embeds within your existing CRM; Copilot Studio builds the self-service digital and voice bots (IVR); routing stays with your CRM or CCaaS; follow-up, supervision and reporting stay with those providers; consult and transfer to Teams users needs a Microsoft 365 license. The page dates from 2024 and uses older product names, so take the pattern, not the labels.

  • Enable Copilot (System Administrator): in Copilot Service admin center open the Copilot for questions and emails or Summaries page and select Opt in (opting out erases the training data). Reps get Copilot through experience profiles: the default profiles include it; in a custom profile turn on Productivity pane > Copilot for questions and emails, then Copilot AI features > Edit (Ask a question, Write an email, Case summary, Live conversation summary).
  • Help pane: Support experience > Productivity > Copilot settings > Manage offers Copilot immersive Preview and Copilot help pane - Ask a Question. Filters (preset, representative, automated) can use only String, Whole Number, Option Set and Two Options Set fields.
  • Roles: by default only users with the Customer Service Representative role can use Copilot; custom roles need the msdyn_copilot* privileges listed on the page, plus prvIntelligenceUsage for case summary.
  • Region: the question, email and summary features are generally available only in North America and are in preview in other supported regions; outside North America, Bing web search also needs data movement across regions enabled in the Power Platform admin center.

Enable agent simulation to evaluate journeys

Agentic simulations Preview let administrators test and validate configurations, AI agents and routing flows before they go live by describing the simulation in a natural-language prompt. Learn labels the article prerelease documentation, and preview features aren't meant for production use. In preview the scope is inbound workstreams of the voice channel only, English only, and no DTMF.

  • Prerequisites: the System administrator and Omnichannel administrator roles, a provisioned voice channel, and a phone number configured for simulation.
  • Cost: each three-minute simulation consumes about 40 Copilot Studio AI credits (it varies with the dialogue). Consumption appears as D365 Contact Center Agentic Simulation in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Run one: Copilot Service admin center Home > Launch on the Agentic Simulation tile; enter a prompt or pick one from the prompt library (suggested, saved, recent) and include the phone number tied to the workstream that receives the call; watch the Ongoing conversation report; review Simulation Run History; open transcripts and recordings in the closed conversation form.
LimitValue
Conversations per promptUp to five
Concurrent simulated callsUp to two
Simulations running at onceOne per organization
Call lengthAccepted simulated calls last at most five minutes; unaccepted calls end after five minutes

Configure representatives and routing rules so the simulated calls can be handled; the notification timer follows the notification template, and the simulated caller number is a regional default handled by the simulation agent.

Enable the Health Agent to proactively investigate issues

What the docs nameThe Contact Center Agents page in Copilot Service admin center lists three agents: Customer Assist Agent, Quality Assurance Agent and Service Operations Agent. The Learn pages reviewed in October 2026 do not describe an agent named "Health Agent". Proactive health investigation is documented through the four capabilities below, so know how to enable and use each.
CapabilityWho and what it needsWhat it does
Contact center health checkerSystem AdministratorHome > Contact center health > Run health check; results are Errors, Warnings, Suggestions with counts; open the link to the faulty setting, fix it and re-run until errors and warnings reach zero. Background checks also send proactive notifications of emerging issues.
Service Operations AgentOmnichannel administrator; for troubleshooting, Application Insights configured and connected to Contact CenterValidates setup after configuration changes, finds misconfigurations and missing dependencies, troubleshoots runtime issues through conversational queries, gives diagnostics for supported channels.
Conversation diagnostics (Application Insights)Managed environment, license with premium use rights; one export configuration per environmentPower Platform admin center > Manage > Data export > App Insights tab > New data export: name, Dynamics Customer Service, environment, subscription, resource group, instance > Create. Logs every conversation lifecycle event.
Diagnose dashboardOmnichannel supervisor or CSR Manager; real-time analytics enabled; Application Insights configuredOmnichannel real-time analytics > Diagnose opens the Debug page: non-assignment reasons, time to assign, assignment events, conversation timeline. Supports only out-of-the-box assignment methods (presence, capacity, skills); data takes about 24 hours to sync fully and can lag up to 15 minutes; no transfer or consult data.

Example health-check findings: errors for an inactive default queue, a queue with no representatives, a workstream with no intake rules, a queue with no valid assignment method, and stopped SLA monitoring (restart the cloud flow SLAInstanceMonitoringWarningAndExpiryFlow); warnings for web-client automatic record creation or SLA rules (use the migration tool).

Enable agents to perform transformation, environment migration, and configuration

Service Operations Agent (SOA) is a self-service AI agent for administrators in Dynamics 365 Contact Center only, in English only. It handles conversational setup, validation and troubleshooting. Open it with Launch on the Conversational Setup tile in Copilot Service admin center; the Contact Center Agents page is where you view and manage the AI agents. The SOA articles carry no Preview label; industry templates and simulation are Preview.

PrerequisiteWhy
Omnichannel administrator roleAccess to the agent
System Administrator roleManage Power Apps connections and Model Context Protocol (MCP) connections
Power Platform pay-as-you-go planAn Azure subscription is charged when the agent runs; set up consumption-based billing
Application Insights (troubleshooting only)Configured and connected with Contact Center
  • Connect: Launch Conversational Setup, the agent asks to connect to Dataverse through the MCP server, select Allow once. To repair it: make.powerapps.com > the right environment > Connections > delete D365 Contact Center MCP Connection; then open Admin Copilot in Copilot Service admin center, start a new conversation and select Allow to create D365 Contact Center Admin MCP.
  • Configures: channels and workstreams (including syncing phone numbers with Azure Communication Services and Teams), queues (out-of-the-box assignment methods; a default is applied if you name none; custom assignment isn't supported), route-to-queue rules (several rules, without conditions only; workstream and queue must be for the same channel; hit policy All or First), operating hours, capacity profiles, skills (only a skill with no assignments can be deleted) and users.
  • Configure manually instead: classification rulesets, assignment rules, overflow rules, percentage-based or multi-queue distribution, and any rule conditions.

Transformation = industry templates Preview (the "agentic transformation" flow). Templates exist for Retail and Telecom and set up workstreams, knowledge, real-time voice agent capabilities and simulation readiness. Prerequisites: voice channel provisioned, System administrator and Omnichannel administrator roles, a configured phone number and pay-as-you-go billing; each setup run uses up to eight Copilot Studio AI credits. Stages: select a template, choose a phone number, start transformation, track setup status, validate with simulation. In the UI: Home > Launch on Industry template (default prompt "Setup my contact center using default configurations"), choose the template > Continue, choose the number > Submit. The setup creates a new workstream and moves the number from its existing workstream to it. On the error LatestPublishedVersionNotFound, republish the Transformation Agent Chat Bot in Copilot Studio.

Environment migration is done with Power Platform admin center operations (reset, restore, recover and tenant-to-tenant moves; Learn lists Omnichannel for Customer Service as not supported in tenant-to-tenant migration, and geo-to-geo migration is limited and requested through your account manager or Technical Support) and the copy-environment steps in §1.2. The Learn pages reviewed do not describe an AI agent that performs them, so know the manual procedures.

Exam traps
  • SOA cannot add rule conditions or create classification, assignment or overflow rules, and its route-to-queue rules are unconditional; do those manually.
  • Role split: Omnichannel administrator opens SOA, System Administrator manages the connections; simulation and industry templates need both roles.
  • Credits: simulation is about 40 per three-minute run, a template setup up to eight. SOA itself bills through a pay-as-you-go Azure subscription.
  • Pick the right health tool: health checker = configuration (System Administrator); diagnose dashboard = why work isn't assigned (supervisor, Application Insights); Application Insights export needs a managed environment.
  • Keeping a third-party CCaaS means routing, supervision and reporting stay there; replacing it means Contact Center.

sections.title: 1.2 Deploy Dynamics 365 Contact Center
sections.html:
Skills measured: Manage and roll out agents by using the Agent hub • Create solutions for Dynamics 365 Contact Center deployments • Configure application lifecycle management (ALM) for Dynamics 365 Contact Center deployments • Manage an omnichannel environment. Build it: create a rollout plan, package a live chat widget and its workstream into a solution and import it as managed into a second environment, then copy an environment and work through the post-copy checklist.

Manage and roll out agents by using the Agent hub

Agent hub (in Dynamics 365 Contact Center and Customer Service) is where admins and supervisors adopt autonomous AI agents safely and monitor their impact. Open it from Copilot Service admin center Home > Open in the Agent hub tile. Its sections are Learn, Rollout manager, Agent insights, Security (trust center), Architecture and Privacy and compliance.

Rollout manager is a wizard for phased, controlled adoption. Prerequisite: the autonomous agents must already be enabled. Steps: Home > Open in Agent hub, Create a rollout plan, then on the Rollout manager page select Create and follow the guided steps. Make one plan per agent or one plan for several agents.

Agent in a rollout planWhat it does / what the wizard asks
Customer Intent AgentSuggested responses based on customer intent; you select a line of business
Case Management AgentCreates and updates cases; you configure case update and closure
Customer Knowledge Management AgentKnowledge-base articles based on customer queries
Quality Evaluation AgentChecks that human and AI interactions are compliant, ethical and on-brand
  • Manage a plan: Edit; Deactivate or activate; Delete; Schedule a future date and time at which it is enabled automatically.
  • The rollout manager reuses the agent's existing settings, which you configure on that agent's admin settings page. Deactivating or deleting a plan for the Customer Intent Agent or Customer Knowledge Management Agent does not deactivate or delete the agent setting; for the Case Management Agent only, the corresponding rules are deactivated or deleted too.
  • Agent insights: enable it at Operations > Insights > AI feature settings > Agent insights > Manage, turn on Enable Agent insights and save; supervisors then open the dashboard in Copilot Service workspace. The autonomous rate is the share of conversations engaged by AI agents only (not routed to a representative). Other KPIs: quality score, sentiment score, active and closed conversations, and days to close for cases. You can set goals for autonomous rate and days to close; the quality score goal reads the Quality Evaluation Agent settings.
Admin-center pageWhat it manages
Agent hub (Home > Open)Rollout and monitoring of the autonomous service agents above, plus Learn, Security and insights
Contact Center Agents (site map)The three contact center agents: Customer Assist, Quality Assurance and Service Operations
AI Agents (Customer support)Copilot Studio agents connected to workstreams: Add > Create new bot or Connect existing bot
Exam traps
  • Enable autonomous agents before you create rollout plans. Deleting or deactivating a Customer Intent or Customer Knowledge Management plan leaves the agent setting unchanged, so turn the agent off on its own settings page; Microsoft's page does not say that a plan can never switch an agent on.
  • Only the Case Management Agent plan takes its rules with it when deactivated or deleted.
  • Quality Evaluation Agent (rollout plans, insights) is not the Quality Assurance Agent (Contact Center Agents page).
  • Agent insights is a separate switch under Operations > Insights; the dashboard stays empty until it is enabled.

Create solutions for Dynamics 365 Contact Center deployments

Solutions transport apps and components between environments and are the Power Platform mechanism for ALM. Contact Center guidance combines solutions (component definitions such as templates and channel configuration) with the Configuration Migration tool (relational reference data such as new capacity profiles and queues).

Create one: make.powerapps.com > Solutions > New solution. Display Name can change later; Name is unique (letters, numbers and underscores; generated from the display name) and can't be changed once saved; Publisher should be one you create for your organization and reuse in every environment; Version matters only on export and appears in the file name; Set as your preferred solution, Configuration Page and Description are optional. A new solution is empty: use New, or Add existing (available only in unmanaged, non-default solutions). Remove from this solution keeps the object in the environment; Delete from this environment can't be undone.

ChannelStarting table to Add existing
Live chatChat widget msdyn_livechatconfig
VoiceVoice channel setting msdyn_ocvoicechannelsetting
SMSSMS number settings msdyn_ocsmschannelsetting
WhatsApp / WeChat / Apple Messages for Businessmsdyn_ocwhatsappchannelnumber / msdyn_ocwechatchannelconfig / msdyn_ocapplebusinessaccount
Facebook, Google Business Messages, LINE, Microsoft Teams, custom channelWorkstream msdyn_liveworkstream
  • Added automatically with any channel: the workstream, capacity profile and workstream capacity profile, context variable, decision contract and ruleset, routing configuration and step, and language (except voice and custom channels). Caveat: new capacity profile records must be migrated with the Configuration Migration tool; once a profile exists in the target, updates can travel in solutions. Workstreams that share a capacity profile are pulled in together.
  • Templates: add session templates, notification templates, agent scripts, agent script steps, application tab templates, notification fields, macros and template parameters to a solution, export it, then import it.
  • Reconfigure after import: records that reference Azure Communication Services, third-party channels, Copilot Studio agents or Customer Voice surveys. Survey columns can't be migrated. Out of scope: account, channel provider, agent configuration, and AI and analytics settings.
  • Privileges: export and import solutions; read on all source tables and full permission on all destination tables used with the Configuration Migration tool. Custom tables, columns, relationships, choices and lookup values that are referenced must already exist in the target.
  • Uninstall: uninstalling Contact Center doesn't remove the omnichannel solutions. Turn off channels first, then delete the managed solutions one at a time in the order the page lists (Advanced Settings > Solutions > Managed tab > Delete). Don't remove shared preinstalled solutions such as UnifiedRouting that Customer Service unified routing depends on.

Configure application lifecycle management (ALM) for Dynamics 365 Contact Center deployments

Contact Center ALM practiceRule
Managed vs unmanagedPackage configuration in an unmanaged solution in the source environment, export it as managed, and import it into the target (for example development to production)
Environment parityKeep source and target aligned, with installed solutions at the same version
Don't edit managed records in the targetAn edit creates an active (unmanaged) layer that always wins over the managed layer: it blocks later updates from the source and can make deleting the managed solution fail. Ship changes in the next managed import
DeletingManaged configuration records can't be deleted in the target; delete the managed solution that brought them in
  • Tool choice: solutions carry components; the Configuration Migration tool is best suited to relational configuration data, and environment variables are recommended for non-relational parameters. Other ALM tools: Power Platform admin center, Power Apps, PowerShell, pipelines and DevOps build tools.
  • Channel configurations are environment-specific: exporting and importing complete configurations as-is won't work, so create them in Copilot Service admin center where you can. Omnichannel entities have internal dependencies (rulesets and decision contracts must exist before workstreams and queues import; context variables imported twice can fail). Don't export msdyn_analytics, which holds organization-specific data.
  • Pipelines in Power Platform: admins configure them, makers deploy with a few clicks, and every deployment is prevalidated against the target (for example missing dependencies); developers can use pac pipeline. The pipelines host should be a production environment (it needn't be managed); all other environments used in pipelines must be managed environments (Developer environments are exempt), with licenses that grant premium use rights. From October 2026 the admin deployment page warns about unmanaged target environments: admins have 30 days to approve enabling managed environments (one 30-day extension per environment) before further deployments to that target are blocked.
MigrationDo it in this order
Channels (solutions + Configuration Migration tool)1 session and notification templates, 2 skill-based routing rulesets, 3 new capacity profiles, 4 queues, 5 channel workstreams and channel settings, 6 verify
Records based on unified routing (Configuration Migration tool)1 FetchXML filter, 2 solution with session and notification templates, 3 skill-based rulesets, 4 capacity profiles, 5 queues, 6 intake rules and record workstreams (the record-routing article lists steps 2 to 6)

Not migrated with record routing: the intelligent skill finder, effort estimation for routing (preview), sentiment prediction for routing (preview), role persona mapping, presence and queue membership. Recreate these in the target.

Exam traps
  • A managed record edited in production hides every later change you import from the source (the active layer wins). The fix is to change it in the source and re-import, never to patch production.
  • Export unmanaged configuration as managed for downstream environments; managed records can't be deleted, only removed by deleting the managed solution.
  • New capacity profiles go through the Configuration Migration tool; updates to an existing profile can use solutions. A solution Name can't change after you save it.
  • Skill-based routing rulesets migrate, but intelligent skill finder, effort estimation and sentiment prediction settings, presence, queue membership and role persona mapping do not.

Manage an omnichannel environment

Provision and turn off channels: the channels are Chat, Voice, SMS, Social and Microsoft Teams. Prerequisites: the channel licensing, the system requirements, and the System Administrator role on the root business unit. In Copilot Service admin center go to Customer Support > Channels > Manage (Manage channels), tick the channels and Save; provisioning runs in the background for several minutes, check boxes for unlicensed channels are disabled, and in the trial every channel is on and grayed out. To turn one off, clear its check box and select Turn off. If you turn off all channels, previous configurations won't work for a channel you enable later.

NeedOperation (Power Platform admin center)Afterwards
Same-configuration sandbox or UATCopy environment: full copy = everything; minimal copy = schemas and customizations only (turn channels off and on, then create channels and workstreams in the target)Post-copy checklist below
Start over, free storage, remove personal dataResetProvision channels or enable unified routing again
Return to an earlier stateRestore from a backup or restore pointProvision channels or enable unified routing again
Environment deleted recentlyRecoverRestored to its previous state
Move to another tenantTenant-to-tenant migrationProvision channels or enable unified routing again
Move to another geoGeo-to-geo migration (the contact center is recreated)Post-move steps below

After a full copy, channels, workstreams, queues, security roles, queue memberships and capacity settings are copied. Review users, role assignments, queue memberships and capacity profiles, test routing, then fix what is environment-specific:

  • Voice with Azure Communication Services (ACS): the ACS resource is copied too, but one resource can be used in one environment only. Disconnect it in the target, connect the target's own ACS resource, assign a phone number and associate it with the workstream. For Teams Phone, configure a target-specific number and integration identifiers, associate it with the copied workstream and test inbound calls.
  • Chat: a new widget configuration is generated, so replace the source widget snippet on your site. Microsoft Teams channel: delete or disconnect the copied messaging account, create a new account and channel configuration, associate it with the workstream, configure the target agent and add it to Teams.
  • Copilot agents: confirm capabilities and connections, fix anything that still references the source, confirm the workstream association, then publish and test escalation and routing.
  • Analytics: turn Enable Omnichannel real-time analytics off and on again, and do the same for Enable Omnichannel historical analytics report.
  • Record routing configuration isn't copied; configure and validate it separately.

After a geo-to-geo move: remove the organization from administration mode; get the new organization URL; copy the updated chat widget code and re-embed it; for voice, copy the Recording, SMS and Incoming call Web Hook Endpoint values (Channels > Phone numbers > Advanced > Manage Azure Communication Services) into the Azure event grid subscriptions. Record routing needs no extra steps.

Exam traps
  • A copied ACS resource is still attached in the target. Leave it and voice breaks in both environments, so disconnect it and connect the target's own resource.
  • Reset, restore and tenant-to-tenant migration all end with provisioning channels (or enabling unified routing) again; a geo move instead needs the new chat widget code and updated ACS webhook endpoints.
  • Copy skips record routing configuration, while after a geo move record routing needs nothing extra.
  • Turning off all channels discards earlier channel configuration, and provisioning needs System Administrator on the root business unit.

Sources: Agent hub overview · Create rollout plans · Enable Agent insights · View Agent insights · Manage your agents · Contact center agents · Create a solution · Migrate channel configurations · Migrate record routing configurations · Data migration for records · Uninstall omnichannel solutions · ALM best practices · Export and import configuration data · ALM tools and apps · Pipelines in Power Platform · Provision channels · Copy an environment with omnichannel · Manage Contact Center environments

sections.title: 1.3 Manage users
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure user settings • create user accounts • manage security roles, including custom security roles and personas • manage capacity profiles. Practise by creating a user in the Microsoft 365 admin center, giving the user a role directly and through a Microsoft Entra group team, setting skills, queues and capacity in Enhanced user management, mapping a copied custom role to a persona, and building a capacity profile with a custom limit.

Configure user settings

Rep settings live in Copilot Service admin center > Customer support > User management. The Contact center users view lists users who have the representative, supervisor or admin persona; All users lists every Customer Service user. For bulk changes select Manage for Enhanced user management, tick the users and choose Update user attributes.

OptionActionsRemember
Update skillsAdd to all • Activate for all / Deactivate for all • Remove from allFor different proficiencies add one skill and proficiency at a time. A deactivated skill is ignored in assignment when a work item requires it.
Update queuesAdd to all • Remove from allUnified-routing queues (§4.1); do not add reps to queues that route records.
Update capacity profilesAdd to all • Remove from all • Custom limitProfile details are in the capacity topic below.
Update conversation limitEnter 1–100, then Update to allDocs tip: start with the limit equal to capacity (capacity 4, limit 4), then raise the limit above capacity for selected reps.
  • Limits. One step updates up to 200 users and five attributes; save, then update the next set. The service quotas page separately lists 25 users per bulk update as a recommended, adjustable limit.
  • Classic experience. User management > Manage for Users > Omnichannel Users > open a user > Omnichannel tab: Capacity (when capacity units are used), Default Presence (the status the rep logs in with, for example Available), New Bookable Resource (name, Save, then the Work Hours tab opens), New Bookable Resource Characteristic (Skill Name plus Rating Value) and Add Existing Capacity Profile.
  • Bookable resource. A user must be a bookable resource to be assigned work by unified routing. Work hours need universal resource scheduling (included with Field Service, Project Service or Service Scheduling); apply a bookable resource calendar to assign by schedule.
  • Capacity units. A rep's capacity must be a multiple of the workstream's capacity unit (§4.2): unit 1 and three simultaneous conversations = 3; unit 5 and three simultaneous conversations = 15. Use either capacity units or capacity profiles.
  • Changes to skills, capacity profile and calendar can take up to 15 minutes to reach the user experience.
Exam traps
  • Capacity (units on the user, a multiple of the workstream unit) and conversation limit (1–100, Enhanced user management) are different settings.
  • A rep with the right role and skills who gets no work usually lacks a bookable resource, a capacity profile or capacity units, or the right presence.
  • Deactivate for all keeps the skill on the user but the user is not considered for work that requires it; Remove from all deletes the skill.

Create user accounts

Create every account in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The account registers the user with Microsoft Online Services, and a license must be assigned before the user can use the service. Assigning the global administrator or service administrator role automatically gives the user the System Administrator security role. Creating the user and assigning a license also creates the user in Dataverse after a sync that can take a few minutes, but the user has no access to the apps until a security role is assigned, directly or through a group team. Force a sync by signing out of the app and the Microsoft 365 admin center, closing all browsers and signing in again.

Assign roles directlyMicrosoft Entra security group team
HowSettings > Advanced Settings > Settings > Security > Users > select users > Manage security roles > select roles > SaveCreate the group in Microsoft Entra and add the reps, then create a team in Power Platform admin center: Team type = Microsoft Entra ID Security Group, Group name = your group; assign Basic User, Customer Service Representative and Omnichannel agent; Save
Use whenA few users, or roles that must be mapped to personasMany reps with identical roles, such as seasonal hiring; add or remove members in the group instead of editing each user
Speed-upNone neededOptional Power Automate flow that runs the SyncGroupMembersToTeam action to sync with the group immediately
  • Enable a user in an environment with a Dataverse database: sign-in allowed, a license assigned, and membership of the security group associated with the environment. Disable by removing the license or removing the user from that group. Removing all roles also blocks access, but the docs say not to use that to remove access. Global, Power Platform and Dynamics 365 admins need no license and run in administrative access mode.
  • Troubleshoot: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > the environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > the user. Run diagnostics checks access problems; Refresh user resyncs from Microsoft Entra ID.
  • Limits and types: role attachment provisions about 500 users per 15 minutes (recommended, adjustable); at most seven non-interactive users per instance. Agent users (Microsoft Entra Agent ID) and users without licenses are Preview.
Exam traps
  • Accounts are created in the Microsoft 365 admin center; User management in Copilot Service admin center configures users that already exist.
  • Signing in to Microsoft 365 does not prove app access: with no role (direct or through a group team) the user cannot use the apps.
  • Do not strip roles to disable a user; remove the license or the environment security-group membership.
  • The Omnichannel administrator role alone cannot manage user roles; it also needs System Administrator.

Manage security roles, including custom security roles and personas

RoleUse
Basic UserRequired by all Contact Center users
Omnichannel administratorAdministrator tasks; also needs System Administrator to manage user roles and privileges
Omnichannel supervisorMonitor, assign and transfer conversations; can view but not edit operating hours
Omnichannel agentRepresentative tasks; view lists and quick replies
Customer Service RepresentativeRequired to work with cases
Productivity tools user / administratorRead, or create/read/write/append/delete, on agent scripts, steps and macro actions

Do not assign Omnichannel API access to a supervisor or rep. App Profile Manager Administrator (creates app profiles, §5.1) is built into Omnichannel administrator but assigned manually in Customer Service; App Profile User privileges are built into Omnichannel agent, Omnichannel supervisor, Customer Service Representative and CSR Manager.

Personas (Admin, Supervisor, Agent) are archetypes that roles map to for unified routing. Map them in Copilot Service admin center > Customer support > User management > Role persona mapping > Manage (needs System Administrator): select a persona, tick or clear roles in the Edit roles pane, then Save and Close.

EnvironmentAdminSupervisorAgent
Customer Service EnterpriseCSR ManagerCSR ManagerCustomer Service Representative
Dynamics 365 Contact CenterOmnichannel AdministratorOmnichannel supervisorOmnichannel agent

With both services enabled both sets apply. Customized mappings are not reset if a service is added later.

A custom role becomes functional only after these steps, in order:

  1. Create the role at organization or business unit level. Copy a predefined role (Omnichannel Administrator, Omnichannel supervisor, Omnichannel agent, CSR Manager or Customer Service Representative) so you do not under-grant, trim access, keep the prvAgent, prvSupervisor or prvAdmin privilege that fits the persona, and use a recognisable name (the docs' example: "seasonal service rep", copied from Omnichannel agent).
  2. Map the role to a persona. The role must be assigned to users directly, not through team membership.
  3. Enable access to the application: Apps page > ellipsis on the tile > MANAGE ROLES > select the role > Save.
  4. Enable access to forms and dashboards: Advanced Settings > Settings > Customizations > Customize the system > Default Solution > Entities > the table > Forms > open the active form > Enable security roles > select the role > OK.

To open the Omnichannel Agent dashboard from Power Apps with custom roles, add the role to the Agent persona. The Personas and privileges page lists each persona's table privileges with recommended access levels; custom plug-ins and workflows break unless their privileges are granted to the personas. Admins who configure workstreams, authentication settings, Azure Communication Services or WhatsApp also need a column security profile for the secret columns.

Exam traps
  • Mapping a role to a persona does not grant access to the app, forms or dashboards; steps 3 and 4 do.
  • A role that reaches a user only through a team (for example the Entra group team) is not picked up by persona mapping; assign it directly.
  • Omnichannel supervisor can only view operating hours; editing them needs Omnichannel administrator.

Manage capacity profiles

A capacity profile defines the type and amount of work a rep can take: the work item limit, whether capacity is concurrent or daily, and whether other channels are affected. Reps can hold several profiles. Supervisors can override capacity and assign work manually, so capacity can show a negative value. Configure either capacity profiles or capacity units, not both.

NeedUse
Simple concurrent limit per rep in one workstreamCapacity units
A phone call must block chat; daily caps; limits by work type or experienceCapacity profiles
Counter resets after the shift even if conversations stay openReset frequency End of day
One rep needs a different limit on the same profileCustom limit

Create: Copilot Service admin center > Customer support > User management > Manage for Capacity profile > Create new. On the Details tab:

  • Profile name and Work item limit (units of work the rep can be assigned).
  • Reset frequency: Immediate, or End of day (resets after the rep's shift even if conversations are still open; those do not count against the next shift). It cannot be changed later: recreate the profile. You can edit everything else, add or remove users, and delete an unused profile.
  • Assignment blocking = Yes: when the limit is met the rep gets no automatic work, even unit-based items, and presence becomes Busy-DND.
  • On the Users tab choose Add user; users must be bookable resources.

Custom limit for selected reps: Enhanced user management > Contact center users > select reps > Update user attributes > Update capacity profiles > pick the profile > Custom limit > Add to all > Save and close; leave the field empty to reset. It applies to new assignments only, and reps with no custom limit keep the default. By OData set msdyn_maxunits (null resets):

Xrm.WebApi.updateRecord("msdyn_bookableresourcecapacityprofile", "<id>", { msdyn_maxunits: 5 });

Apply to work: set the profile in the workstream's work distribution settings (applies to every item routed through it) and/or as a classification ruleset output that appends a profile to the work item. Assignment then needs a rep with capacity in both profiles and consumes both; no queue-level rule is needed. Docs example: High-priority 2/day, Normal-priority 4/day and Total 5/day, all End of day; Total is the workstream default, classification appends High or Normal, and each rep holds all three.

Work typeCapacity is released when
ConversationThe rep ends the conversation and closes the session
CaseThe rep resolves or cancels it, or clears their name from Worked By on Queue Item details
Other records and activities, such as email through record routingNot automatic: deactivate the queue item, or clear Worked By to keep the record open

The out-of-box escalation profile cannot be edited; it blocks new chat or voice work while a chat escalated to a voice or video call lasts, and follows the call on transfer. Capacity-update history sits in Dataverse; at 50–60% storage consumption consider moving or deleting it (irreversible).

Exam traps
  • Reset frequency is the one setting you cannot edit; the fix is a new profile.
  • A custom limit does not reassign work already given to the rep; it affects new assignments only.
  • Email and other activities under record routing keep the rep "full" until you deactivate the queue item or clear Worked By.

Sources: Manage users · Assign roles, enable users · User management overview · Create users · Personas and custom security roles · App profile roles · Personas and privileges · Capacity profiles · Service quotas
