sections.title: 2.1 Configure chat and digital channels
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure the chat channel • Configure the record-based channel • Configure digital channels • Configure and embed a chat widget • Configure proactive chat • Configure pre-chat surveys • Manage quick replies • Extend the chat experience using the live chat SDK • Configure authentication settings for chat • Manage chat in native mobile apps by using the Messaging SDK for Dynamics 365 Contact Center • Configure a custom messaging channel by using messaging APIs • Enable real-time translation of conversations • Configure customer settings, including location and self-service settings. Build it: in a trial environment create a chat workstream with a Modern widget (pre-conversation survey, authentication setting, proactive invitation) on a test page, then add a Twilio SMS channel and a messaging-API custom channel and switch on real-time translation.

Configure the chat channel

Chat is a first-party channel: a live chat widget on your portal that a workstream routes to queues. The workstream is the container that enriches, routes and assigns work; its Type is Messaging (live chat, SMS, social, Teams), Record (case, email, activity) or Voice. For chat create Customer support > Workstreams > New workstream with Type = Messaging and Channel = Chat. You must be a system administrator or hold permissions on the secure columns.

Workstream fieldRule
Work distribution modePush (the system alerts a representative) or Pick (representatives pick from Open work items). It cannot be edited later; voice supports push only.
Fallback queueCreate new (add users afterwards) or Choose existing (defaults to the out-of-the-box queue for the channel type). Used when no route-to-queue rule picks a queue.
NeedSetting
Customers resume one thread over several daysPersistent chat: tick Make chats persistent when you create the workstream and select Keep same representative for entire conversation in Work distribution. It requires the widget's authentication settings, needs its own workstream (live and persistent widgets cannot share one), shows no default wait-time or queue-position messages, and only representatives can end the conversation. A representative can set an unresponsive conversation to waiting, which frees capacity.
Customer drops and comes backReconnect to previous chat (Chat widget tab): set a Time limit (capacity stays blocked, then the conversation moves to wrap-up), a Portal URL and an optional Redirect URL (empty = a new chat starts). It works only if the customer returns inside the limit, the representative did not select End and the customer did not close the window.
Show chat only in business hoursCreate the operating-hours record (Operations > Calendars > Operating Hours > Manage, see §4.1), then switch on Show widget during operation hours on the widget.
Name the customer seesRepresentative display name: Full name (default), First name, Last name or Nick name (falls back to the full name when empty). Consult and transfer always show the full name.
Let people send filesFile attachments under User features. Default limit 5 MB (5,120 KB), changed in Advanced Settings > System > Email Configuration > Email Settings > Maximum file size for attachments (KB).
Exam traps
  • Push or Pick is fixed at creation; the only fix is a new workstream.
  • Persistent chat is not Reconnect to previous chat: persistent needs authentication, Make chats persistent and a dedicated workstream, while reconnect works only inside its time limit.
  • Wait-time and queue-position messages are not available for persistent chat.
  • Never add .txt to the blocked file extensions (System > Administration > General > Set blocked file extensions for attachments): transcripts of closed conversations would become unavailable.

Configure the record-based channel

The record channel sends Dataverse records (cases, emails, activities or a custom table) to representatives through unified routing. It uses a workstream with Type = Record and is configured under Customer support > Routing > Record routing. Prerequisites: unified routing is provisioned for the environment; the table is enabled for queues; you hold the System Administrator role; representatives are set up as bookable resources.

  1. Enable the table: Power Apps > Tables > the table > Properties > Advanced options > Can be added to a queue. This cannot be undone. Clear the table option that moves new or assigned rows to the owner's default queue, otherwise rows are not distributed.
  2. Customer support > Routing > Manage (Record routing) > Add > pick the Record type > Add.
  3. Workstreams > New workstream: Name, Work distribution mode (Push or Pick), Type = Record, Record type > Create.
  4. Intake rules > Create rule: conditions reach up to two levels of related records and attributes; map the rule to a workstream or an active basic routing rule; reorder rules in the Decision list (See more on the workstream page).
  5. Add routing rules (work classification and route-to-queue; §4.2), then Work distribution: capacity (Unit based or Profile based), Allowed presences and the Default skill matching algorithm (Exact Match or Closest Match).

Emails follow the same pattern: a dedicated mailbox with server-side synchronization creates the email record and queue item, a flow routes the work item, and an intake rule identifies the Record workstream.

Exam traps
  • After unified routing is enabled, the active basic routing rule does not route records until intake rules exist.
  • Upgrading with Contact Center installed: recreate existing record-routing workstreams in the admin center before provisioning unified routing.
  • To route records in Customer Service Hub, add every required presence to Allowed presences; record-routing notifications appear only in Copilot Service workspace.

Configure digital channels

Provision first: Customer support > Channels > Manage channels, tick the channels you need (Chat, Voice, SMS, Social, Microsoft Teams) and save. You need the System Administrator role on the root business unit; provisioning runs in the background. Every digital channel then follows the same four steps: (1) create the account, page or app with the provider; (2) create a Messaging workstream; (3) create the channel in the admin center and attach it to the workstream; (4) exchange the handshake values (tokens, secrets, callback URL) in both places.

The messaging account lives at Customer support > Channels > Accounts > Messaging accounts > Manage > New account (channel details, account details, numbers or pages, Callback information). On the workstream choose Set up <channel>, pick the account or number, then Language, Behaviors, User features and Summary > Finish; routing rules and work distribution follow.

ChannelWhat to remember
SMS via TwilioTwilio Account SID, Auth token and a purchased number; US phone numbers only. Number format <country_code><phone_number> with no spaces (for example 14252306549); Type = Long code, Short code or Toll free. Paste the admin-center callback into the number's Messaging settings in Twilio; opt-out and consent are configured with the provider.
SMS via InfobipAn API key with the message:send scope plus the API Base URL. The Infobip application ID must be your Dynamics organization ID (not the environment or tenant ID).
WhatsApp via TwilioSandbox (shared number, recipients send join <code>, no custom templates) or production number. 24-hour session rule: free-form replies only within 24 hours of the customer's latest message; afterwards only a WhatsApp-approved template, identified by its Content template SID (one language per template). Enter the number with a leading +.
FacebookFacebook Page with Messenger and a Business app; App Review for pages_messaging (until approved only users with an app role can message). Paste the Callback URL and Verify token into Meta and subscribe the page to Messages. Facebook message tag lets representatives reply after 24 hours.
LINEChannel ID, Channel secret and a long-lived Channel access token; paste the callback URL as the webhook URL and keep Use webhook on.
Microsoft TeamsFor internal support (IT, HR): employees chat with support staff. The Teams app's Application (client) ID must equal the Bot ID shown in the admin center.

Deprecated SMS via Azure Communication Services (ACS) and WhatsApp via ACS are deprecated as of September 23, 2026, with removal on September 30, 2028; existing channels keep working until then, but customers without an ACS resource can no longer provision new SMS numbers and new ACS customers cannot acquire or port numbers. For new deployments the docs point to SMS via Twilio or Infobip and WhatsApp through Twilio. Apple Messages for Business onboarding is deprecated (July 17, 2026) and its configuration leaves the admin center on September 30, 2026. Older training content still shows ACS, so know both.

Exam traps
  • Twilio SMS takes US numbers only; Infobip needs the organization ID as the application ID.
  • WhatsApp after 24 hours: an approved template only. Facebook uses the message tag instead.
  • The Teams channel serves employee-facing support; it is not Teams collaboration between representatives.
  • Messaging accounts are under Channels > Accounts > Messaging accounts; voice numbers are under Channels > Phone numbers.

Configure and embed a chat widget

A widget needs a chat workstream. Create it at Customer support > Channels > Manage (Chat) > Chat channels > Add chat channel and choose Modern (live preview) or Classic. The Modern wizard runs: General Configuration → Workstream details → Color Settings → Chat button (icon, or a custom icon URL that must be a publicly hosted .png or .svg) → Header → Intro page → Chat Widget (expand, size, representative display name and the toggles Proactive chat, Reconnect to previous chat, Show widget during operation hours, Only show widget on the provided domains) → Behaviors (automated messages, surveys, authentication settings, customer wait time, customer location detection) → User features (file attachments, customer notifications, transcripts, voice and video, screen sharing, co-browse) → Notifications (Azure Notification Hub details for mobile push) → Create channel. Screen sharing and co-browse need a non-Microsoft provider from Microsoft Marketplace, one of each per widget.

TaskWhereEffect
Add the Modern widget to a live Classic channelWorkstreams > a workstream with Channel = Chat > Add Modern UIKeeps the workstream configuration. Behaviors and User features are shared and editable only in the active version.
Test one version⋮ next to Classic or Modern > Copy testing scriptA script that always loads that version, unlike the general script tag.
Go live or roll back⋮ > Set as activeThe general script tag already on your site now serves that version; make Classic active to roll back.

Embed the snippet:

  1. Channels > Chat, select the instance, Edit, open the Chat widget tab and copy the code snippet.
  2. Website: paste it inside the HTML <body>.
  3. Power Pages: Portal Management app > Portal > Content Snippets > Chat Widget Code > General tab > Value (HTML) > Save.
  4. Mobile: use the native SDK (below); the snippet in a WebView is the fallback.

Web engagement orchestration deploys one script tag for many workstreams or sites: Channels > Web Engagement > Manage > Engagement Rulesets > New, then Copy Live Chat Widget Script (one tag per ruleset). Rules live in versions numbered #.#; only one version is published at a time and the published one cannot be edited. Conditions: Site Area (a regex on the URL), Custom Context, Custom Client Function. Actions: Show Chat Button, Open Chat Widget, Do Nothing. Rules start inactive, run in ascending Priority, stop at the first true rule, and changes take about 10–15 minutes. It is web only (not the mobile SDKs or custom Chat SDK widgets). Per-widget snippets suit small deployments; orchestration suits many workstreams or rules managed in the admin center.

Exam traps
  • Modern and Classic are two versions of one channel; Add Modern UI is on the Workstreams page, not on Chat channels.
  • Copy testing script never changes the live site; Set as active does.
  • Screen sharing and co-browse are not built in: install a Marketplace provider first.
  • The Power Pages snippet is the Chat Widget Code content snippet, not a web template.

Configure proactive chat

Proactive chat invites a visitor to chat instead of waiting for the visitor to open the widget. The page's banner reads Customer Service and Contact Center — standalone only, and an invitation can appear only on pages where the chat widget is embedded. Two parts are needed: switch on Proactive chat on the Chat widget tab of Chat channel settings (workstream > edit the widget), then add page script that decides when to invite.

window.addEventListener("lcw:ready", function () {
  setTimeout(function () {
    Microsoft.Omnichannel.LiveChatWidget.SDK.startProactiveChat(
      { message: "Need help with your order?" },  // notificationUIConfig (required)
      false,                                      // showPrechat (optional, default true)
      { inNewWindow: false });                    // options object
  }, 20000);                                      // after 20 seconds on the page
});
  • notificationUIConfig is a required object; without a message the invitation reads "Hi! Have any questions? I'm here to help". showPrechat defaults to true; false skips the pre-conversation survey. The method returns nothing.
  • The visitor can accept or close the invitation. If ignored, it closes automatically after one minute, and that timer cannot be configured.
  • When the visitor accepts, the representative gets a notification and accepts it; the Active conversation loads if the customer's details match stored data. Context such as time on page and page URL appears on the Additional details tab when you configured that tab and the context variables.
NeedUse
Invitation logic in page JavaScript (time on page, visit count, case status)Proactive chat toggle + startProactiveChat
No-code, admin-managed rules (site area, custom context) that show the button or open the widgetWeb engagement orchestration (above)
Outbound AI-led voice or SMS campaignsProactive outbound engagement (§2.3), a different feature
Exam traps
  • The one-minute auto-close is fixed; there is no setting to lengthen it.
  • No widget snippet on the page, no invitation: proactive chat cannot start on pages without the embedded widget.
  • showPrechat defaults to true, so the survey is shown unless you pass false.
  • Proactive chat (widget invitation), web engagement orchestration (rules) and proactive engagement (outbound campaigns) are three different things.

Configure pre-chat surveys

The preconversation survey asks the customer questions before the chat starts; the post-conversation survey is a separate Behaviors setting that runs after the conversation closes. Path: Customer support > Workstreams > the chat workstream > choose the channel instance in the dropdown > Edit > Chat channel settings > Behaviors tab > set Pre-conversation survey to On > Survey questions > Add.

Field or limitRule
Survey question nameInternal name.
Question textAt most 512 characters.
Answer typeSingle line, Multiple lines, Option set (drop-down; type the options separated by a semicolon, for example North;South;East;West) or User consent (a checkbox next to the text; link format [link text](link URL); Required must be Yes).
RequiredMakes the answer mandatory. Validation is supported for mandatory fields only.
Count and orderUp to 10 questions; the order can be changed.

Adding questions creates matching context variables under the workstream's Advanced settings > Context variables, so routing rules can use the answers and representatives see them. Answers can also identify the customer record. Use these question names with the Single line type:

RecordQuestion name (context key)Searched attribute
AccountName, Email, Phonename, emailaddress1, telephone1 (Business Phone)
ContactName, Email, Phonefullname, emailaddress1, mobilephone
Case (incident)CaseNumberticketnumber

Only records with the active status code are searched (custom status codes break identification), a search that returns more than one match links nothing, and a single active case on the identified customer is linked automatically. Identification uses what the customer types; it is not authentication.

Exam traps
  • Know the limits: 10 questions, 512 characters per question; options are semicolon-separated; User consent must be Required.
  • The survey is configured per chat channel instance on the workstream (Behaviors tab), not in a global survey area.
  • A pre-conversation answer identifies a record; only a signed JWT authenticates (see authentication below).

Manage quick replies

Quick replies are predefined messages that representatives insert into a conversation. Create them at Support experience > Productivity > Manage (Quick replies) > New, with a Title, a Locale and a Message. The admin center does not localize quick replies: create one quick reply per language and set each Locale.

Dynamic text (slug)Inserts
{FullName{Customer}}, {FirstName{Customer}}, {LastName{Customer}}The customer's name parts
{FullName{Agent}}, {FirstName{Agent}}, {LastName{Agent}}, {Nickname{Agent}}The assigned representative's name parts and nickname
{OCContext.contextKey1}A custom context value, for example {OCContext.OrderID}; the context key must already be defined
  • Tags: select two or more quick replies > Edit > Tags (type a name, or + to create it) > Close. Tags group replies into conversational stages for representatives.
  • Scope to workstreams: open the quick reply > Workstreams > Add Existing Work Stream > pick > Add > Save. With no workstream associated, the quick reply is available to all representatives.
  • What a representative sees depends on three parameters: the language mapped to the channel instance (widget or Facebook page), the language in the representative's personal settings and the workstream the reply is mapped to.
  • Personal quick replies belong to one representative: Personalization > Personal quick replies tab > New in Copilot Service workspace; they can take up to 15 minutes to appear and are not localized either.
Exam traps
  • No workstream association means everyone sees the reply, not nobody.
  • Localization is manual: one record per language and Locale.
  • Admin quick replies are under Support experience > Productivity, not Channels; personal ones are created by the representative.
  • Slugs use double braces, {FirstName{Customer}}; {OCContext.key} needs a defined context key.

Extend the chat experience using the live chat SDK

Pick the lowest customization level that meets the requirement:

LevelUse whenHow
Data tags (low)Hide buttons, change the font, open in a windowAttributes on the copied script tag, for example data-hide-chat-button, data-hide-minimize-button, data-open-in-window, data-font-family-override (default Segoe UI; web-safe fonts only), data-render-mobile.
Customizable widget 2.0 (medium)Restyle the standard widget, keep admin-center behaviorChat workstream > Copy Live Chat Widget 2.0 Script; write a function with component styling (CSS); add v2 after the script attribute; add data-customization-callback pointing at the function. It changes the UI only; the Config Override JSON of web engagement orchestration is the admin-center equivalent.
Your own widget (high)Fully custom UI, extra features or React NativeThe open-source headless Omnichannel Chat SDK (npm @microsoft/omnichannel-chat-sdk) plus the Live Chat Widget UI Components library (React on Fluent UI).

The live chat SDK is the browser object Microsoft.Omnichannel.LiveChatWidget.SDK of the standard widget. Methods include setContextProvider, setAuthTokenProvider, startChat, startProactiveChat, closeChat and getAgentAvailability. Events are raised on window: lcw:ready, lcw:error, lcw:startChat, lcw:closeChat, lcw:chatQueued, lcw:chatRetrieved, lcw:onMessageReceived, lcw:threadUpdate (the agent ended the conversation) and more. Call SDK methods only after lcw:ready.

window.addEventListener("lcw:ready", function () {
  Microsoft.Omnichannel.LiveChatWidget.SDK.setContextProvider(function () {
    return { orderId: { value: "A-1001", isDisplayable: true } };
  });
});
// or pass the context when you start the chat:
// Microsoft.Omnichannel.LiveChatWidget.SDK.startChat({ inNewWindow: true,
//   customContext: { orderId: { value: "A-1001", isDisplayable: true } } });
  • setContextProvider is for unauthenticated chat only and accepts at most 100 custom context variables per chat. isDisplayable: true shows the item on the third tab of the conversation summary. A key with no matching workstream context variable is created at run time as a String.
  • When you pass customContext to startChat you do not need setContextProvider; customContext overrides it.
Exam traps
  • Methods called before lcw:ready fail; always wrap them in the listener.
  • Widget 2.0 restyles the UI only; it does not change functional settings in the admin center.
  • lcw:threadUpdate means the agent ended the conversation, so the host page calls closeChat to finish on the client.
  • Signed-in customers: context goes in the JWT lwicontexts claim, not in setContextProvider.

Configure authentication settings for chat

Authentication proves who the customer is: the signed-in customer's site passes a signed JWT to the widget and the system validates it with the public key you registered. Customer identification only matches a contact or account from what the customer typed and never authenticates. Authentication lets you separate anonymous from authenticated customers (separate queues, priority by cart value); the representative sees Authenticated = Yes/No in the Conversation summary. It is supported for Chat (and the deprecated Apple Messages for Business). Prerequisites: working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and JWTs, and permissions on the secure columns.

  1. Customer support > Customer settings > Authentication settings > Manage > New Authentication Settings: Name, Owner, Authentication type (OAuth 2.0, not editable), Public key URL (validates the JWT), Javascript client function (extracts a token from the token endpoint) > Save.
  2. Attach it: edit the chat widget in the workstream > Behaviors tab > Authentication settings box > choose the record. The record works only once it is added to a channel instance in a workstream.
Portal typeValues
Power Pages (Power Apps portal)Public key URL <portal_base_URL>/_services/auth/publickey; function auth.getAuthenticationToken; upload a custom certificate to get a valid public key URL. The out-of-the-box token carries sub = the contact ID, which links the contact automatically.
Custom portalThe developers build the plumbing below and give the administrator the public-key URL and the function name.

Custom-portal developer work: (1) generate an RSA256 key pair (for example openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -out private_key.pem -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048); (2) expose an endpoint that returns the public key (one PEM, or an array of {kid, publicKey (base64), expiry} items for several keys, in which case the JWT header carries kid); (3) build a service that signs the JWT with the private key; (4) write a JavaScript function that takes a callback and returns the JWT within 10 seconds.

// header
{ "alg": "RS256", "typ": "JWT" }
// payload: iss, iat, exp and sub are the minimum claims
{ "sub": "aaaaaaaa-0000-1111-2222-bbbbbbbbbbbb",
  "iss": "contosohelp.com", "iat": 1542622071, "exp": 1542625672,
  "lwicontexts": "{\"msdyn_cartvalue\":\"10000\", \"msdyn_isvip\":\"false\"}" }
  • sub: Microsoft recommends the GUID of the contact or account record (only active records are found). lwicontexts carries context variables for routing or display; the keys must match the workstream's context variables exactly.
  • An expired or invalid token raises an error event. setAuthTokenProvider(fn), called after lcw:ready, is the SDK hook that supplies the token.
Exam traps
  • The minimum claims are iss, iat, exp and sub; lwicontexts is optional and kid is a header field.
  • Keys use RSA256, and the token function must return within 10 seconds.
  • Authentication settings sit under Customer settings, not under Channels; a pre-conversation survey never authenticates.

Manage chat in native mobile apps by using the Messaging SDK for Dynamics 365 Contact Center

A native app has two options: the native Messaging SDKs for iOS and Android or the web widget inside a WebView. Microsoft strongly recommends the native SDKs for superior feature support and performance. The SDKs and their documentation are hosted on GitHub (Contact Center Messaging SDK for Android and for iOS). They contain a sample app, a configurable out-of-the-box messaging interface, a full set of messaging lifecycle functions for a bespoke UI, and support for push notifications with Azure Notification Hub.

SDK componentUse when
Messaging WidgetA pre-built native UI with the least development effort; its options mirror the web live chat widget. Recommended for most programs.
Core Messaging FrameworkYou build your own UI; the functions call the Omnichannel Messaging APIs.
  • Microsoft recommends authenticated, persistent chat with the SDKs; the app passes an auth token (signed by your identity provider) that identifies the customer, for example by Dynamics record ID.
  • Setup: create a chat workstream; the widget values from the workstream page (organization ID, URL, widget ID) go into the app. For push, turn on Notifications in the widget wizard and enter the Azure Notification Hub details.
  • The out-of-the-box mobile UI is styled through code in your app, not through the admin center.

WebView fallback (when the SDK does not meet your requirements or timelines; expect reduced performance, limited mobile usability and unavailable features): load the widget script with data-render-mobile="true" (hides the header and the Close button) and data-hide-chat-button="true", optionally data-color-override. On Android enable local storage with webSettings.setDomStorageEnabled(true). Add your own end-chat button that calls closeChat, and listen for lcw:threadUpdate to call closeChat when the agent ends the chat. Escalation to voice or video and transcript download are not supported in a WebView.

Exam traps
  • WebView is the fallback, not the recommendation; it loses voice/video escalation and transcript download.
  • Branding the native chat UI is done in app code, not in Copilot Service admin center.
  • The Messaging SDK is for native apps; the live chat SDK (JavaScript) is for the web widget and the Messaging APIs are for back-end services.

Configure a custom messaging channel by using messaging APIs

Messaging APIs are RESTful, service-to-service endpoints that let you integrate a custom channel without client-side SDKs or UI. Use them for end-to-end customization, strict network or data-compliance environments, or a bring-your-own channel that omnichannel does not support. They are intended for back-end integrations and not recommended for mobile or web client apps that call them from the user's device; use the native SDKs or chat widgets there.

ItemValue
ProtocolHTTPS; GET and POST. Base URL https://m-{org_id}.{geo}.omnichannelengagementhub.com
Required headersAuthorization (OAuth 2.0 bearer token from Microsoft Entra), channel-id (GUID of the custom channel), organization-id. A missing authentication header returns 401 Unauthorized.
EndpointsPOST /conversation/create, POST /conversation/{id} (message, typing, end), GET /conversations, GET /conversation/{id}/messages, GET /conversation/{id}/context, and the webhook POST /v3/conversations/{id}/activities
Create payloadcustomercontext (email and phone drive record matching), conversationcontext (up to 100 context variables, each with isDisplayable and value), startmessage (sent to the representative only), skipdeflectionbot (true = the AI agent is not engaged). An active conversation with the same customerid returns the existing conversation.
WebhookRetried three times, 10-second timeout each; payloads follow the Bot Framework Activity Schema; activity type is message, typing or event (event names such as AgentAccepted, ConversationClose).
  1. Prerequisites: System Administrator role, a messaging workstream with routing rules, an active Azure subscription.
  2. Register a confidential client app in Microsoft Entra ID and copy its Application (client) ID (it becomes msdyn_appid). Tokens use the client-credentials flow with the scope https://{organization_id_without_dash}-c.{zone}.dynamics.com/.default.
  3. Host an HTTPS webhook at {webhook_url}/v3/conversations/{conversationId}/activities with a valid certificate (not self-signed).
  4. Optional managed identity for webhook authentication: create a managedidentity record (credentialsource 2, subjectscope 1), link it with managedidentityid@odata.bind, call GetComponentManagedIdentityFIC to get the FICSubject and add a federated credential to the Entra app (scenario Other issuer, type Explicit subject identifier). Any webhook change generates a new FIC, so repeat the Azure update.
  5. Create the channel record. There is no form: in Copilot Service admin center open Workstreams, press F12 and run the call below in the Console; list records at {org_url}/api/data/v9.2/msdyn_occustommessagingchannels.
  6. Add the channel to a messaging workstream (the Channel field lists the Messaging API channel you created).
Xrm.WebApi.createRecord("msdyn_occustommessagingchannel", {
  "msdyn_occustomchannelid": 192350005,   // MessagingAPI
  "msdyn_name": "Litware gateway",
  "msdyn_appid": "{azure_app_id_guid}",
  "msdyn_tenantid": "{azure_tenant_id_guid}",
  "msdyn_webhookurl": "https://gateway.litware.example"
});
NeedUse
Your back end bridges an in-house messaging platform over RESTMessaging APIs custom channel
Bot Framework based channel through Azure Bot ServiceCustom messaging account with method Azure bot framework (Direct Line connector sample)
Customer-facing web page / native appChat widget and live chat SDK / Messaging SDK
Exam traps
  • The msdyn_occustommessagingchannel record is created with the Dataverse Web API (Xrm.WebApi), not a wizard.
  • A 401 means the bearer token or Authorization header is missing or invalid; the webhook certificate cannot be self-signed.
  • Messaging APIs call from servers; Microsoft does not recommend calling them from the customer's device.

Enable real-time translation of conversations

Real-time translation translates messages between the customer and the representative and between representatives who consult or collaborate, such as supervisors and subject-matter experts. It is implemented as a plug-in that exposes APIs for third-party translation services and also provides a native implementation. It is not supported on Unified Service Desk. Prerequisites: add a web resource and configure the translation service, and enable call recording and transcription so translated voice-call transcripts display (§2.2).

  1. Admin center Operations > Insights > Real-time translation section > Manage. Other articles word the menu path differently, so look for the Real-time translation tile.
  2. On Omnichannel Configuration · Real Time Translation Settings set Turn on to Yes.
  3. Default input language: the language representatives converse in; the default is English (en-us).
  4. Web resource URL: use two forward slashes before WebResources, for example https://example.crm.dynamics.com//WebResources/new_rtt_translator. Save.
  • The developer builds the web resource from the sample webResourceV2.js (methods initializeNewConversation and translateMessage), uploads it as a Script (JScript) web resource in a solution, publishes it and hands over its URL.
  • Azure Translation Services as the provider: configure the resource to use the "global" endpoint.
  • Score-based language detection keeps one-off messages from switching or stopping translation: set enableLanguageDetectionWithHistoryMessages: true, in the web resource file. The language used most often (by weight) wins.
Exam traps
  • The web resource, not the widget language setting, defines the provider and the translation behavior.
  • The default input language is the representative's language, not the customer's.
  • Voice transcripts translate only when call recording and transcription are on.

Configure customer settings, including location and self-service settings

Customer support > Customer settings groups customer-facing configuration: Authentication settings (above), Geo location, Self service, Customer feedback (survey agents; §2.2) and voice items such as blocked numbers and phone music.

GoalSettingWhere
Representative sees where the visitor isGeo location provider record + Customer location detectionCustomer settings > Geo location; widget Behaviors tab
Representative sees what the visitor did on the portalSelf service = Yes + page code that calls setContextProviderCustomer settings > Self service
Separate signed-in from anonymous customersAuthentication settings recordCustomer settings > Authentication settings

Location. The visitor's browser prompts for permission when the chat starts; if approved, latitude and longitude go to the representative, and if location sharing is off in the browser nothing is detected. You need permissions on the secure columns. (1) Get a Bing Maps API key. (2) Customer settings > Geo location > Manage > Active Geo Location Providers > New: Name and Bing Maps API key > Save and Close. (3) On the chat widget, Chat channel settings > Behaviors tab > Customer location detection On > pick the provider > Save. Deprecated Bing Maps for Enterprise is deprecated: it remains available to existing Bing Maps for Enterprise customers until June 30, 2028 and is not available to new customers or customers using Azure Maps.

Self-service. The page applies to Customer Service and Contact Center standalone only. It shows the customer's recent self-service actions before the chat. Prerequisite: a developer adds a snippet to the self-service portal that passes the history as context with setContextProvider (key SelfService; items carry msdyn_displaytitle, msdyn_starttime and msdyn_type: 192350000 page visited, 192350001 phrase searched, 192350002 knowledge article viewed, 192350003 custom action). Then Customer settings > Self service > Manage > Omnichannel Configuration · Self service settings > Self service = Yes > Save; representatives then see a Self service tab when a customer starts a chat. Each action is stored in the Self service table (msdyn_visitorjourney) once the conversation closes.

Exam traps
  • Location detection needs a Bing Maps key, not an Azure Maps key, and the customer must approve the browser prompt.
  • The location toggle sits on the widget's Behaviors tab, but the provider record is created under Customer settings > Geo location.
  • The Self service tab stays empty unless the portal code passes the history with setContextProvider.

sections.title: 2.2 Provision and manage the voice channel
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure the voice channel • Integrate a non-Microsoft interactive voice response (IVR) system with voice channel • Manage phone numbers • Configure inbound and outbound calling profiles • Configure call recording, transcription, and real-time translation • Configure agent feedback • Manage voice calls via the CCaaS SDK API. Build it: start with a trial number or connect an Azure Communication Services resource, create a voice workstream and queue, turn on transcription and recording with its Event Grid subscriptions, then add an outbound profile with a capacity profile.

Configure the voice channel

The voice channel is PSTN calling inside Dynamics 365, built on Azure Communication Services (ACS) and routed by unified routing like chat. Provision it first (turn on Voice and accept the Voice and SMS terms), then connect ACS: create a new resource (Channels > Phone numbers > Manage > Get started > Create new resource: subscription, resource group, resource name with letters, numbers and hyphens; the subscription must be in the same tenant and you need Contributor rights; that page is marked standalone and Customer Service only), use an existing resource, import numbers, or bring your own carrier. Map one application instance to one ACS resource; numbers bought through a resource linked to an environment cannot be moved to another environment.

  1. Prerequisites: voice provisioned, unified routing enabled, a phone number acquired.
  2. Workstreams > New: Name and Type = Voice. Owner and Channel are preset and only Push is available. Create.
  3. Queues > New: Name, Type = Voice, Group number > Create > Add users. Only users configured for unified routing can be added, and representatives must refresh their dashboards, which can take 20 minutes after they are added.
  4. Open the workstream > Set up voice > Phone number (only numbers with inbound enabled that are not on another workstream) > Language > Behaviors > Summary > Save and close.
  • Language: the primary language is the first language the representative uses to greet the customer. One number can serve several languages, each with its own settings, hold and wait music, and a Voice profile (voice, style, speed, pitch).
  • Behaviors: Customer wait time (notify position in queue, average wait), Channel operating hours, Transcription and recording, custom automated messages, transfer and consult toggles, Post-call survey. Anonymous inbound calls work only on numbers configured through ACS direct routing.
  • Voicemail: up to five minutes, always transcribed; the AI agent cannot offer it (the call must escalate to a representative). It needs voice, unified routing, working presence, the Event Grid call recording and SMS services, and the voice workstream's Channel operating hours turned off (otherwise the system plays a message and disconnects). It is offered on queue overflow (calls waiting, after hours, wait too long) or when a direct call to an inbound profile number is missed. Voicemails are records, so they cannot be routed to voice queues; the out-of-the-box Default Group Voicemail Workstream and Default Individual Voicemail Workstream handle them.
Transfer to an external number or Teams userUse bridged transfers selectedNot selected
Caller ID on the new legThe Dynamics numberThe customer's number
The original callContinues (transfer message, then hold music)A new call begins (transfer message, then ringing)
Recording and transcriptionContinueStop
Customer DTMF to the external partyNot possiblePossible
Post-conversation surveyTriggered when the external party hangs upNot sent

To answer calls with a Copilot Studio AI agent first, add the agent to the voice workstream (agents work only in push workstreams; §3.2).

Exam traps
  • Voice has no Pick mode; the mode is also fixed at creation.
  • A number belongs to one voice workstream, and numbers without inbound enabled are not listed.
  • Do not reuse one ACS resource across environments; numbers cannot be moved afterwards.
  • Voicemail fails when the voice workstream's Channel operating hours toggle is on.
  • Bridged transfer is what keeps recording going; non-bridged transfer allows DTMF but ends recording.

Integrate a non-Microsoft interactive voice response (IVR) system with voice channel

Azure direct routing connects a non-Microsoft IVR, through its Session Border Controller (SBC), to the voice channel and performs a contextual call transfer. Prerequisite knowledge: Azure direct routing, its infrastructure requirements and SBCs.

  1. Set up Azure direct routing and connect the SBC linked to the IVR to the ACS resource that is connected to the application.
  2. Register the number assigned to the IVR with Bring your own number (Channels > Phone numbers > Manage > Advanced > Bring your own number via Azure Direct Routing).
  3. To transfer a call, the IVR issues a SIP INVITE to the ACS resource, which transfers it to the Azure resource connected to the application.
  4. Carry the context in the SIP UUI (User-to-User) header, written param1=value1;param2=value2.
  5. Create context variables whose names match the UUI parameter names exactly: Customer support > Workstreams > the voice workstream > Edit > Advanced settings > Add context variable > Name and Type > Create. The payload then becomes context data for routing and for the representative.
UUI formatExample
Plain text: key/value pairs separated by semicolonsUser-to-User: sipkey1=sipval1;sipkey2=sipval2
Hex with explicit encoding: hex-encode the ASCII payload and append ;encoding=hexUser-to-User: 7369706B6579313D73697076616C313B7369706B6579323D73697076616C32;encoding=hex
Hex with protocol discriminator: hex-encode the payload and append ;pd=4User-to-User: 3530303131323233333434353b363738393b3132;pd=4
  • Direct-routing prerequisites: a certified SBC that answers the INVITE with a SIP status in the 100s (4xx, 5xx and 6xx mean failure); numbers in E.164; the SBC and the DNS server deployed in the same region, with DNS not delegated to a sub domain.
  • Limitation: the call record and transcription of the IVR leg are not available to representatives.
  • Microsoft's own alternative is a Copilot Studio AI agent as the IVR on the voice workstream (§3.2); do not confuse the two.
Exam traps
  • Context travels in the SIP UUI header, not in a custom SIP header, a REST call or the Messaging API.
  • Context variable names must match the UUI parameter names exactly, so policy and PolicyNumber are different variables.
  • Hex payloads need ;encoding=hex or ;pd=4; plain text uses semicolon-separated pairs.
  • The IVR's own number is registered through Bring your own number, and an ACS resource must already be connected.

Manage phone numbers

Start at Customer support > Channels > Manage for Phone numbers. The list shows carrier, calling plan, associated workstream and status: a new number is Ready for setup and becomes Connected once it is on a workstream. Prerequisites: the voice channel installed, an ACS resource connected, and permissions on the secure columns.

SourceHow
Buy a US number in the productAdd ACS number: Country/Region, Number type (Toll-free or Geographic), Calling plans (Receive calls, Make calls or both), SMS plans (None, Send SMS, Send and receive SMS; SMS only on toll-free), Location > Find numbers > Purchase phone number. Purchase within 15 minutes of being allotted the number. Only US numbers can be acquired in this dialog.
Number bought in the Azure portal or outside the USAdvanced > Sync from Azure imports numbers from the ACS resource.
Keep your carrier and numbersAdvanced > Bring your own number via Azure Direct Routing: Add number or Import multiple numbers (CSV columns msdyn_phonenumber, max 15 digits, quotes above 10 digits, no +; msdyn_phoneinboundenabled; msdyn_phoneoutboundenabled; 100 numbers at a time recommended; check Import status). SMS is not supported with direct routing.
Test the channelTrial numbers: up to two and 60 minutes of free calling in total. The first is a toll-free US number callable only from within the US, so make the second a geographic US number for international callers. No ACS connection is needed; select End trial before connecting ACS. Trial numbers cannot be reused or purchased.
  • Attach to a workstream: select the Ready for setup number > Setup workstream > create or pick a voice workstream. A number can be associated with only one voice workstream.
  • Personal numbers give a representative an exclusive number: geographic only; a toll-free number cannot be assigned. Use Setup > Assign to user on a Ready for setup number.
  • Edit: Edit > Save and Close. You cannot upgrade or change plans after the number is connected to a workstream, and granted features cannot be removed, only upgraded (None → Send SMS → Send and receive SMS).
  • Release: first remove the number from workstreams and outbound profiles (disable it if it is a personal number), then Release number. Releasing deletes the number from Dynamics 365. Disconnecting the ACS resource releases all numbers tied to it.
  • Deprecated From September 23, 2026, new ACS customers cannot acquire or port numbers into ACS; existing ACS customers can continue during the retirement period. Bring your own carrier keeps your existing numbers.
Exam traps
  • The 15-minute purchase window: if it lapses, search and purchase again.
  • SMS plans exist only on toll-free ACS numbers, and personal numbers cannot be toll-free.
  • Plans are frozen once a number is connected to a workstream, and a plan feature can never be removed.
  • Release means delete; the Customer Service dialog buys US numbers only, so other regions need Azure purchase plus Sync from Azure.

Configure inbound and outbound calling profiles

Profiles are at Support experience > Productivity > Manage for Outbound and inbound profiles (column Profile type). Inbound profiles enable direct inward dialing (DID) to individual representatives and differ from workstreams, which route calls through queues. DID does not use unified routing, so direct calls are not tracked in unified-routing historical analytics.

GoalUse
Calls routed by queues, rules and skills to whoever is availableVoice workstream + voice queue
Customers dial one representative's own numberInbound profile on a geographic personal number assigned in the user's Omnichannel tab
Representatives place calls from a business numberOutbound profile on a shared (or geographic) number whose calling plan includes Make calls
Customers should see another number as caller IDCaller ID number on the outbound profile; that number must also have an outbound profile
Calls with financial data must not be keptTranscription and recording = None
  • Create: capacity profiles and voice queues must exist first. New profile > name and Profile type > Phone number (one at a time; the outbound list shows only Shared numbers enabled for outbound and not used as personal numbers) > Info page (queue plus one or more capacity profiles) > Behaviors > Save and close.
  • Behaviors: Language (default English - United States), Hold music, Wait music, Call transfer to external phone number (must be on to use call forwarding), Consult with Microsoft Teams user, Transcription and recording, Start setting (default Automatic) and Allow agents to pause and resume (outbound default Yes). Inbound profiles offer a transcription and recording choice or None; outbound profiles offer None, Transcription only or Transcription and recording.
  • Outbound info: the Number label is a dialer label such as Billing and is not a CNAM (caller name delivery is not supported); Caller ID number defaults to (Profile Number). Allow list for countries/regions is an early access feature; representatives with several profiles see only the countries common to all.
  • Default profiles from the first-run experience are the fallback when a representative has no profile; only behavior and templates can be edited, not the profile type, and both share one locale.

Outbound calling setup, in order: (1) the number's calling plan includes Make calls (Phone numbers > Edit number > Calling plans > Make calls > Upgrade); (2) a voice queue (separate inbound and outbound queues are recommended); (3) a capacity profile with users: Work item limit = simultaneous outbound calls, Reset frequency = Immediate for voice, Assignment blocking = Yes to block incoming calls during an outbound call; (4) the outbound profile. A representative who is not in a capacity profile tied to an outbound profile gets no outbound calling features.

Exam traps
  • Profiles are under Support experience > Productivity, not Channels or Workstreams.
  • An inbound profile is DID to one person on a geographic personal number and bypasses unified-routing analytics.
  • The number label is not CNAM; the country allow list is early access.
  • No capacity profile tied to the outbound profile means no dialer for that representative.

Configure call recording, transcription, and real-time translation

Many jurisdictions require every party's consent before PSTN, voice or video calls are recorded, and the organization is responsible for compliance. Copilot Studio AI agents always produce a Copilot Studio conversation transcript; for a DTMF-only agent, speech is ignored and only keypad tones are captured.

  1. Tenant-level audio recording on: Quality Management > Manage (Enable screen and call recording) > Screen and audio recording page. Turning it off at tenant level prevents audio recording whatever the workstream says. (The screen-recording part of that page applies to Contact Center standalone and Customer Service only.)
  2. Allow the audio and mpeg MIME types in Power Platform admin center privacy and security settings.
  3. Event Grid so ACS events reach the app. In the Azure portal create an Event Grid system topic (Topic Type Azure Communication Services, your ACS resource; the Microsoft.EventGrid resource provider must be Registered), then create one event subscription per event type: Incoming Call, Recording File Status Updated, SMS Received and SMS Delivery Report Received. Use Event Schema Event Grid Schema and Endpoint Type Web Hook with the endpoint from Channels > Phone numbers > Advanced > Manage Azure Communication Services; under Additional Features tick Use Microsoft Entra authentication with the same tenant ID and application (client) ID used when you first connected the ACS resource. You must own the app registration, set one webhook at a time, and never change the event type of an existing subscription. Sync can take up to 15 minutes ("Webhook validation handshake failed": recheck the IDs and retry).
  4. Voice workstream > Phone number section > pencil Edit > Voice settings > Behaviors tab > Transcription and recording: choose Transcription or Transcription and recording.
  5. Start setting: Automatic (starts with the call) or Manual (representatives start it; the button reads Resume recording and transcript by default, which is normal).
  6. Set Allow customer service representatives to pause and resume and Allow automatic pause and resume when agent hold and un-hold the customer to Yes if representatives may keep card numbers off the record, then Save.
  • Real-time translation of calls: to see translated voice transcripts you must enable call recording, transcription and real-time translation; the translation setup is the one in §2.1.
  • View: in Copilot Service workspace only: Users > the user > Related tab > Conversations > Closed conversations dashboard > open the conversation. Transcript timestamps are grouped in two-minute intervals. A Power Automate flow can download recordings in bulk.
  • Size and location: a recording can be at most 512 MB (a 20-minute two-party call is about 10,240 KB, its transcript about 40 KB). Data stays in the region where the ACS subscription was acquired; with direct routing it is where the SBC is hosted.
  • Transfers and profiles interact: a non-bridged transfer stops recording, and a profile set to None records nothing.
Exam traps
  • The tenant-level audio toggle beats every workstream setting.
  • Three separate Event Grid subscriptions (incoming call, recording, SMS), and the webhook authentication must reuse the original app and tenant IDs.
  • Translated voice transcripts need recording and transcription first.
  • The MIME types are allowed in Power Platform admin center, and recordings are viewed only in Copilot Service workspace.

Configure agent feedback

The documented feedback configuration for voice is the Customer service representative call quality (feedback) survey on the Voice call experiences page. After a call ends, the representative rates the call; it shows whether the representative had a satisfactory experience beyond technical metrics such as bitrate, jitter and latency, and the data is analysed in Azure logs.

  1. Support experience > Workspaces > Voice call experiences (the survey can also be enabled from Voice settings in voice workstreams).
  2. Switch Customer service representative call quality survey to On.
  3. Set the frequency at which representatives see the survey; optionally switch Set survey duration on and set the period (for example after a telephony change).
  4. Store the data: enable the Call Survey Logs diagnostic setting in Azure Monitor and send it to a Log Analytics workspace, Event Hubs or an Azure storage account; otherwise the survey data is not stored and can be lost.
ACSCallSurvey
| where isempty(AudioIssues) == false
| project audio = split(AudioIssues, ','), CallId, TimeGenerated
| mv-expand audio to typeof(string)
  • The representative rates the call from 1 (imperfect) to 5 (perfect), after every call or at your frequency; ratings 1 to 4 show predefined reasons such as "I couldn't hear any sound" or "Volume was low".
  • Other settings on the same page: Un-hold customer after representative transfer is accepted (off = the representative takes the customer off hold manually) and Allow DTMF to be broadcasted across all participants during a call. Preview External Contact Settings enforce secure recording, transcription and hold behavior when consulting or transferring to external contacts such as payment gateways; it is a production-ready preview.
Who gives feedbackFeature and whereData lives in
Representative rates call qualityCall quality survey: Support experience > Workspaces > Voice call experiencesAzure Monitor logs (ACSCallSurvey)
Customer after the callPost-call survey with a Copilot Studio survey agent: Customer support > Customer settings > Customer feedback > New (CSAT, NPS, CES or Blank template; Enable for Voice Channels), then the voice workstream's Behaviors > Post-call surveyDataverse (customer feedback survey response)
Exam traps
  • Representative survey data goes to Azure Monitor, not Dataverse; with no diagnostic setting it is lost.
  • Do not confuse it with the customer survey (Customer settings > Customer feedback; needs the Omnichannel administrator role). The old post-call survey toggle on the voice workstream's Language tab was deprecated and removed on August 1, 2025.
  • External Contact Settings are a preview feature.

Manage voice calls via the CCaaS SDK API

The CCaaS SDK is a set of APIs that integrate Dynamics 365 Contact Center into third-party CRMs (Embed SDK, namespace Microsoft.CCaaS.EmbedSDK) or into Dynamics environments (Standalone SDK, namespace Microsoft.CCaaS.StandaloneSDK), to extend agent workflows, listen to real-time events and fetch Dataverse data. Its reference lives in Microsoft's GitHub repository microsoft/dynamics-365-contact-center (folder CCaaS SDK APIs), and most modules are labelled Public Preview.

// Embed SDK: send a number from the CRM to the CCaaS dialer (the agent still selects Call)

  • Hold and mute are events you subscribe to, not actions you call.
  • The modules are mostly Public Preview and documented on GitHub, not on Learn.

Skills measured: manage context variables • configure automatic customer identification • close conversations automatically • enable consult with representatives and transfer of conversations • configure sensitive data masking • configure custom presences • configure messages, including templates, formatting, automated messages, and outbound messages • manage active conversation settings • configure the timeline • use custom connectors with the timeline control • configure the channel integration framework • manage conversations • configure feedback by using Copilot Studio • manage file attachments • manage proactive outbound engagement • configure proactive outbound campaigns, including workstreams and triggers • configure dialing methods for proactive outbound campaigns • set up the proactive outbound dashboard • configure Workforce management (WFM) • configure shift management and scheduling • configure forecasting • integrate third-party WFM solutions • design the Dynamics 365 Contact Center setup • use best practices when setting up voice • use best practices for developing AI capabilities • evaluate the total cost of ownership. Build one chat workstream end to end in a trial environment (a context variable, a masking rule, a custom presence, an auto-close override and an outbound SMS configuration), then open a proactive campaign and a WFM schedule once so you know where each setting lives.

Manage context variables

Context variables carry pre-conversation, channel and custom data with a conversation. Routing and classification rules (§4.2), macros, scripts, automated messages and Copilot agents can all read them.

  1. Copilot Service admin center > Customer support > Workstreams > open the workstream.
  2. Advanced settings > Add context variable; in the Edit pane select Add.
  3. Enter the Name and choose the Type: Text or Number.
Limit or ruleValue
Variable nameup to 100 characters
Variable valueup to 4,000 characters; values are case-sensitive, so match exactly
Custom context per chat sessionat most 100 variables
  • Do not rename variables that flows in Azure or Copilot Studio use. Before you change or delete one, check that no unified routing classification or assignment rule depends on it.
  • Unauthenticated live chat: wait for the lcw:ready event, register the provider with setContextProvider, then call startChat(). Keys must equal the logical names of variables on the workstream. A key with no match is created at runtime as String; only primitive values are allowed.
  • Authenticated chat: send the context in the JWT; setContextProvider for authenticated chat has been deprecated since 2021-10-01.
  • Direct Line: send key-value pairs in Activity.ChannelData.ConversationContext when the client starts the conversation.
window.addEventListener("lcw:ready", function () {
  Microsoft.Omnichannel.LiveChatWidget.SDK.setContextProvider(function () {
    return { LoyaltyTier: "Gold", OrderValue: 129.5, IsVip: true };
  });
  Microsoft.Omnichannel.LiveChatWidget.SDK.startChat();
});
The value is...Use
typed by the customera pre-conversation survey question (its name becomes the variable name)
already known by the websitecustom context: setContextProvider, ConversationContext or the JWT
needed inside a Copilot agenta Copilot Studio variable that is Global with External sources can set values

Map a variable into a Copilot Studio agent: Topics > add a topic > Variable management > Set a variable value; the variable name must match the omnichannel name exactly (case-sensitive), Reference = Get value from this node if empty, Usage = Global (any topic can access) plus External sources can set values. Add a time-out for work-classification data and for Dataverse values such as msdyn_CaseId, which can arrive late. Activity.From.Name (the caller's number on voice) can be read only in the Conversation Start topic.

Configure automatic customer identification

The goal is that the representative sees the customer's account or contact (and case) on the Active Conversation page without searching. In the chat widget this is driven by pre-conversation survey questions: the answers are searched in Dataverse. Custom context sent with setContextProvider can also identify a record.

RecordQuestion name (single line of text)Dataverse column searched
AccountName, Email, Phonename, emailaddress1, telephone1
ContactName, Email, Phonefullname, emailaddress1, mobilephone
CaseCaseNumberticketnumber
  • Only records with active status are searched, so custom status codes break identification.
  • If the search finds more than one account, contact or case, nothing is linked. If the identified customer has exactly one active case, it is linked automatically and the representative can change it.
  • Case identification is a Customer Service capability, not Contact Center standalone.
  • Voice: the caller's number is matched against the contact's mobile phone or the account's phone field. To match other fields (for example Home Phone, telephone2), the Contact Center documentation describes extending the voice workstream's record identification rule: a FetchXML rule set (msdyn_recordidentificationrule on msdyn_liveworkstreams) that uses placeholders such as ${msdyn_fromphone}.
  • Identified data feeds the built-in variables msdyn_CustomerId, msdyn_CustomerName, msdyn_CustomerType, msdyn_CaseId and msdyn_CaseTitle that Copilot agents can read.

Close conversations automatically

A scheduler runs every 5 minutes and checks the modifiedon value of the Conversation table (msdyn_ocliveworkitem). It marks conversations that stayed in a state longer than the configured time and moves them on the next run. Monitor, consult and transfer actions make it recalculate. Never edit state or status reason by hand.

ChannelOpenActiveWrap-up
Chat20 min → Closednever auto-closed15 min → Closed
Voice30 days → Closed2 hours → moves to Wrap-up1 day → Closed
SMS, Teams, social, persistent chat30 days30 days (SMS, Teams, social)1 day
  • Waiting state: use the workstream option Auto-close after inactivity. It exists only for persistent chat, SMS, social and Microsoft Teams.
  • Change a default (Power Apps): select the environment > Tables > Channel State Configuration > edit the column Auto close conversation after (needs write privilege on the table).
  • Change a default (Web API): GET [org]/api/data/v9.1/msdyn_occhannelstateconfigurations, then PATCH a row with { "msdyn_autocloseliveworkitemafter": 5 }. The value is in minutes (1 day = 1,440) and msdyn_name names the channel and state, for example "Live Chat - Open".
  • For live chat Wrap-up, the workstream Block capacity for wrap-up value overrides the table value when it is larger.
  • Duration-based auto-close is not supported for records configured for unified routing.

Enable consult with representatives and transfer of conversations

By default representatives can consult other representatives and transfer conversations to queues. The advanced options live in Copilot Service admin center > Channels > Consult and transfer; you need the System administrator or Omnichannel administrator role.

NeedUse
System picks the most eligible representative from a queueConsult to queue: switch on and enter the countdown numbers for voice and messaging channels (how long the system searches). Capacity is blocked by default.
Send the conversation to a named representative with no consultDirect transfer: Transfer settings > turn on transfer to representatives
Hold capacity during a direct consultTick the block-capacity checkbox on the page; for direct consult it is not blocked by default
Wrap-up time after a transferWrap up after transfer; the length is the workstream's Block capacity for wrap up value
Re-run classification and routing with updated contextReroute Preview toggle in Transfer settings (off by default); a representative must first change an attribute such as case Priority, or the conversation may return to the same queue
Show only some queues or representativesFour filtering toggles, all disabled by default (consult to queue, transfer to queue, consult with representative, transfer to representative). Each takes a validated FetchXML query; for queues the primary entity is queue and {queue.queueid} stands for the current conversation's queue, for representatives it is systemuser.
Always show certain queues or external contactsManage pins (Customer settings): pinned items sit on top and representatives cannot unpin them. Pinning does not hide other items.
  • Voice transfer: the Transfer dialog has the tabs Representatives, Queue, Teams and External number, and the customer is put on hold automatically. Use bridged transfers on: the original call continues, recording and transcription carry on, the caller ID is the contact center number and DTMF is not forwarded. Off: a new call that is not recorded, shows the customer's caller ID and forwards DTMF. In enhanced voice (the only voice stack in Contact Center), when you transfer to an external number or Teams user the call ends for the primary representative as soon as that party accepts or rejects it, so use Consult first to confirm they answer. The 8 minutes limit to complete a transfer applies only to the existing (legacy) voice stack.
  • Consult a Teams user: turn on External Microsoft Teams users in the voice workstream's consult and transfer settings. It needs enhanced voice, Teams Phone licensing and Teams-to-Azure Communication Services federation, and it works over VoIP only.
  • Consult with AI agents Preview: a voice-enabled Copilot Studio agent joins a call only through a consult (disclosure, consent, PIN check). Turn it on under Channels > Consult and transfer > Manage, then add agents at Workspaces > Voice call experiences, choosing to pause or continue recording and whether to keep the representative on hold. The agent topic must end with a Transfer Conversation node.

Configure sensitive data masking

A masking rule replaces text that matches a regular expression (credit card, SSN, profanity) with mask characters, # by default, in live messages and in the transcript. Automatic rules apply to chat and asynchronous channels only, and only administrators can edit them.

  1. Copilot Service admin center > Productivity > Manage for Data masking.
  2. Masking rules > New Masking Rule: Name, optional Description, Regular expression.
  3. Check it with Enter test data (the result shows as Masked test data), save, and make sure the rule is Active (ellipsis menu: activate, deactivate, delete).
  • Out-of-the-box rules: Credit Card, Email, SSN. They can be edited or deleted. The limit is 10 rules in total, out-of-the-box ones included.
  • Mask private agent data from the customer: what the representative sends is masked for both the customer and the representative (live chat and async).
  • Mask private customer data from the agent: on live chat both parties see masked text; on async channels only the representative's UI is masked.
  • Voice agents built in Copilot Studio (§3.2) do not use these rules: switch on the Sensitive data toggle in the variable's properties. It needs a provisioned voice channel with inbound calling, a Copilot Studio voice agent in a workstream, and the System administrator and Bot author roles. While sensitive data is collected, recording, transcription and data logging pause, silence is inserted in the recording, and the transcript shows "Entered a confidential section of the conversation".
  • Manual masking lets a representative mask a message in an open conversation (hover over the message > Mask); it works for all digital channels and voice transcripts, but it removes text from voice transcripts not from retained audio recordings. Set up: Productivity > Manage for Data masking > Enable Customer Service Representatives with masking permission to hide messages = Yes; add the Masking Agent Messages and Masking Customer Messages roles to personas in Role Persona Mapping; create a Masked Message text for each workstream language (otherwise the representative gets an error). Encrypt masked messages = Yes plus a Public Key URL (RSA public key, PEM format) keeps an encrypted copy for audit; without it masked messages are deleted for good.
  • Caveats: assigning a sensitive variable to a non-sensitive one makes the latter sensitive; do not enable Log sensitive activity properties for Application Insights; explicit writes of sensitive data to Dataverse are not redacted.

Configure custom presences

Presence tells work distribution whether a representative can receive work. Base status is what routing uses: Available, Busy, Busy-DND, Away, Offline. Presence text is only the label the representative sees. The base statuses that may receive work are the Allowed Presences you pick when you create a workstream.

  • Out-of-the-box statuses cannot be edited or deleted: Available, Away, Busy, Busy - DND, Inactive, Offline. Inactive cannot be selected manually; the system applies it when the missed notifications feature is on and the representative does not respond to an incoming notification.
  • If no default presence is defined, sign-in sets Available.
  • Create: Copilot Service admin center > Productivity (the group is labelled Agent experience or Support experience, depending on the page) > Manage for Custom Presence > New > Name, Presence Text, Base Status, Description > Save. Example: "Away - In Training" with base status Away. Map it logically: a custom presence that looks available but has base status Offline is treated as offline.
  • Stop routing to representatives who ignore notifications: Workspaces > Notifications > Manage > Omnichannel Configuration page > Agent Reject tab > Change agent status to "Do not disturb" after a notification is rejected = Yes. Work still routes to a representative in Do not disturb if that base status is an allowed presence on the workstream.
  • Sync presence to another system: register a webhook with the Plug-in Registration Tool on the msdyn_agentstatus table, synchronous mode, deployment Server; the payload carries msdyn_agentid and msdyn_currentpresenceid. Prerequisites include the Omnichannel agent or Omnichannel Supervisor role, an allow-listed third-party app and middleware.

Configure messages, including templates, formatting, automated messages, and outbound messages

Message templates

Reusable text with placeholders (slugs) replaced at send time. Path: Productivity > Manage for Message templates > New: Name, Channel, Default language, Default text > Save, then add localized text per language in the New message panel. Slugs look like {FullName{Customer}} and {FirstName{Agent}}. Outbound messaging supports templates for SMS and WhatsApp only; a WhatsApp template is built in Twilio Content Template Builder, you reference its Content Template SID (not the template name), and each content template has one language.

Formatting

Productivity > Message formatting > Manage > Markdown settings > Turn on Markdown = Yes > Save & Close. Representatives then type Markdown on chat and social channels (for example Teams, WhatsApp, Facebook, Telegram and Direct Line custom channels): **bold**, _italic_, ~strikethrough~, > blockquote, lists, links and headers of levels 2 to 4. Shift+Enter line breaks are not supported and pasted formatted text may not persist.

Automated messages

System messages sent on events (representative joins, customer waits, conversation ends) for chat, voice, SMS and social. There are two levels: channel level (every instance) and channel instance level (one number or widget).
