Without an adapter, external schedules cannot appear in the representative calendar. Not supported in GCC or sovereign clouds.

Design the Dynamics 365 Contact Center setup

Contact Center is a Copilot-first cloud product that adds omnichannel capabilities to the CRM of your choice. Four composable layers sit on one shared Dataverse data model: self-service (AI agents and conversational IVR, built in Copilot Studio), unified intelligent routing, assisted service (Copilot Service workspace) and operations (analytics, workforce management, AI controls). Two deployment models exist: standalone (a conversation widget inside any CRM, such as Salesforce, ServiceNow or a custom one) and embedded within Dynamics 365 Customer Service (the foundation of Customer Service Premium).

Customer starting pointSolution
Replace both the CRM and the CCaaSCustomer Service Premium
Replace the CRM, keep the CCaaSCustomer Service Enterprise
Replace the CCaaS, keep the CRM (Salesforce, ServiceNow)Contact Center (standalone, embedded widget)
Keep CRM and CCaaS (Genesys, NICE, Five9) and add AICopilot Studio and the Microsoft Contact Center AI overlay
  • Provision channels: Copilot Service admin center > Customer Support > Channels > Manage channels > tick Chat, Voice, SMS, Social, Microsoft Teams > Save. Provisioning runs in the background, boxes are disabled for unlicensed channels, turning off all channels loses earlier configuration, and you need System Administrator on the root business unit.
  • Integration points: Teams Phone (telephony backbone), Dynamics 365 apps, Power Platform (Dataverse, Power BI, Power Automate), Azure (Communication Services, Azure OpenAI) and Copilot Studio for agent authoring. Case features exist only with Customer Service.
  • System requirements: Microsoft Edge or Chrome, third-party cookies not blocked (authentication and presence), at least 4 GB RAM, and voice bandwidth of at least 4 Mbps up and 8 Mbps down (8 and 16 recommended).
  • Design for consolidation: one platform instead of separate IVR, bot, WFM and quality-assurance point solutions.

Use best practices when setting up voice

AreaPractice
HardwareStable wired Ethernet or strong wireless with enough bandwidth (minimum 4 Mbps up and 8 Mbps down; recommended 8 and 16); USB headsets with noise-canceling microphones, not laptop speakers and microphone; test the microphone and speaker, keep the microphone close to the mouth and adjust its sensitivity to remove echo
Network and softwareAllowlist the URLs and IP addresses used for Omnichannel servers (Azure Communication Services firewall guidance); enable telemetry insights (latency within the same region is usually under 150 ms); install the Desktop companion application if representatives are slow to join a call after accepting it
Voice agent (IVR)Put the greeting agent on the workstream, not the queue; play an initial greeting first and look up data afterwards; use Dataverse connectors for Dynamics data and HTTP requests for external data (Power Automate flows add latency because the agent waits for the flow); configure a latency message with a minimum playback time (default 5000 ms) to avoid silence; add a delay activity between messages (default 500 ms); use a system greeting message for a static, uninterruptible message and do not repeat the agent's own greeting
Automated messagesKeep them short; prefer Greeting Message for Async Channels and Voice over "Agent assigned"; deactivate average-wait-time messages unless required

Use best practices for developing AI capabilities

  • Capacity: in a queue shared by an AI agent and representatives, set the agent's capacity higher than all representatives (an agent's capacity is not reduced when it receives a work item) so it picks up first.
  • Escalation: update context variables before escalating so routing rules match, and keep at least one representative in the queue that holds only the AI agent; otherwise an escalated conversation can return to the same queue and never reach a human. Agents are not added to the default queue automatically.
  • Messages: keep message size within 28 KB on all messaging channels (metadata and Direct Line payload included). The variable limits (name 100, value 4,000, case-sensitive) still apply.
  • Responsiveness: greeting agent on the workstream, greet first and look up data later, prefer Dataverse or custom connectors and HTTP requests, and watch Power Automate latency. Voice: latency message (5000 ms default) and delay activity (500 ms default).
  • Sensitive data: mark variables Sensitive in Copilot Studio and do not log sensitive activity properties to Application Insights.
AI maturity levelWhat it means
1. AI assistantCopilot is available to every representative; most organizations start here
2. Digital colleaguesAI agents do specific tasks: intent discovery, knowledge drafting, case closure
3. Agent-operatedHumans set strategy; AI runs the processes with approval points

Prebuilt Contact Center agents: Customer Assist Agent (intent discovery, self-service, real-time assistance, proactive outbound), Quality Assurance Agent (real-time and post-conversation evaluation, coaching) and Service Operations Agent (generally available since July 9, 2026, though the Learn training module still labels it preview; admin configuration, validation and troubleshooting in natural language). The Customer Knowledge Management and Case Management agents belong to Customer Service. Copilot Studio is the authoring platform; Microsoft Contact Center AI overlays Genesys, NICE or Five9 for incremental adoption.

Evaluate the total cost of ownership for a Dynamics 365 Contact Center implementation

Cost has two parts: user-based licences for named users plus consumption charges for AI and telephony. IVR and transcription beyond the included entitlements are a capacity add-on.

LicenceFits
Service agentCopilot assistance in Outlook and Teams for any CRM; no CCaaS channels
Customer Service EnterpriseCRM and case management; keep the existing CCaaS
Dynamics 365 Contact CenterCCaaS for an existing CRM (Salesforce, ServiceNow, custom)
Contact Center Add-onCCaaS on top of existing Customer Service Enterprise licences
Customer Service PremiumFull CRM plus CCaaS bundle, cheaper than buying both
Copilot Credits modelFits
Pay-as-you-go (Azure subscription billing policy, billed monthly)Low or unpredictable volume
Capacity (prepaid) packs (Microsoft 365 admin center)Steady, predictable usage
Pre-purchase plan (Azure portal, one-year prepaid Copilot Credit Commit Units)Larger or variable demand with volume discounts
  • Copilot Credits are the consumption currency for AI agent usage (they replaced "messages" on September 1, 2025). A generative answer costs 2 credits and a classic answer 1 credit on the Copilot Studio rate card (the Learn training unit says classic rule-based topic responses are included in the licence). Capacity is enforced monthly, unused credits do not carry over, and the AI capability stops when the quota runs out.
  • When prepaid and pay-as-you-go are both set up, prepaid capacity is consumed first. The Dynamics 365 environment must be linked to a Power Platform environment; monitor prepaid use in the Power Platform admin center and pay-as-you-go in Azure Cost Management.
  • Estimate credits from monthly self-service interactions, the share that uses generative answers and the escalation rate to humans; the WFM AI credit estimation turns forecast volume into projected credits (planning only).
  • Voice usage is billed per minute and per participant through Azure Communication Services (PSTN inbound and outbound, VOIP, SBC legs, recording). The Teams-originated leg is covered by the Teams licence, supervisor monitoring or consult legs are charged only while joined, and a Teams VOIP consult costs less than a PSTN one. The prices in the docs are illustrative.
  • Each service number needs a free Teams Resource Account licence. The Contact Center licence includes Teams Phone System entitlements for contact center agents (extra Teams Phone licences only if they also need personal calling). PSTN options: Calling Plans, Operator Connect, Direct Routing.
  • Cost levers: retire on-premises telephony hardware (PBX, SBC) and staff, consolidate point-solution licences (IVR, WFM, QA, analytics), cut integration work through the shared Dataverse model. Value levers: reduce case volume, reduce handling time, improve employee experience, improve quality outcomes.
  • Journey: 30-day trial → buy licences (Microsoft 365 admin center) → assign them → create a Power Platform environment with Dataverse → provision Contact Center → enable and configure channels. A trial environment cannot be used for production.
Exam traps
  • Limits that look alike: context variable name 100 characters, value 4,000 characters, 100 custom variables per chat session; data masking allows 10 rules including the out-of-the-box ones; an AI agent message is capped at 28 KB.
  • Voice versus chat: automatic data masking rules and {$variable$} placeholders do not work for voice (voice agents use the Sensitive data toggle). A voice call in Active moves to Wrap-up after 2 hours, it is not closed; a chat in Active is never auto-closed.
  • Presence: the base status drives routing and the presence text is only a label. Inactive is set by the system and cannot be selected.
  • Dial modes: predictive needs at least 10 available representatives and behaves as progressive below that; progressive places one call per available representative; only Preview lets the representative review the record before the call.
  • Names that get swapped: the historical Proactive Outbound dashboard versus the real-time Proactive Engagement report; a timeline "custom connector" is an IRecordSource web resource, not a Power Platform connector; CIF integrates third-party telephony (UI only), not messaging channels.
  • Forecasts are locked: forecast type, interval, entity and data source cannot change after creation; short-term means 15-minute intervals up to 6 weeks (the forecast-scenarios page says up to 84 days).
Confusable pairDifference
Consult to queue, direct transfer, reroute PreviewSystem picks a representative with a countdown; you pick a named representative; routing rules are re-run with updated context
Channel-level and channel-instance automated messagesAll instances of the channel versus one instance; the instance message overwrites the channel one
Message template and automated messageReusable outbound SMS or WhatsApp text with slugs such as {FullName{Customer}} versus system-event text with {AgentName}, {QueueName} and {$variable$}
Data masking rule and Sensitive data toggleRegular expression on chat and async text versus a Copilot Studio voice variable that pauses recording
CIF 1.0 and CIF 2.0Single-session apps, one provider, right panel versus multisession apps, several providers, left panel
Forecast scenario, capacity plan, shift planVolume and handle time versus staffing (service level, shrinkage) versus schedules and bookings
Customer Service Premium, Enterprise and Contact CenterCRM plus CCaaS bundle versus CRM only versus CCaaS only

sections.title: 3.1 Configure agent assist capabilities in Dynamics 365 Contact Center
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure Copilot summaries • Configure the Ask a question feature • Configure knowledge sources for Copilot in Dynamics 365 Customer Service • Extend Copilot capabilities with prompt plugins and tools • Interpret the Copilot analytics report • Create a smart assist bot. Practise in a trial environment: opt in, switch on the three conversation-summary triggers, add one automated filter, publish a knowledge article, open the Copilot analytics report, and register a smart assist bot on a workstream.

Configure Copilot summaries

Prerequisites: the System Administrator role, Copilot available in your region (or cross-region data movement allowed in Power Platform admin center), and Opt in on the Copilot settings or Summaries page (opting out erases the training data). Summarizing cases and conversations is generally available in North America only and Preview in the other supported regions. Admin path: Copilot Service admin center > Support experience > Productivity > Summaries > Manage (or Operations > Insights > Summaries).

SummaryApplies toSwitch it on / key limits
Case summaryCustomer Service onlyTurn on Ask a question first, then Make case summaries available to representatives. Needs at least 50 tokens (about 38 English words) in the fields Copilot reads. Specify information to exclude: up to 10 email addresses and 3 disclaimers, headers or footers (for example a notification sender).
Conversation summaryContact Center standalone and Customer Service; chat and transcribed voiceThree triggers: When a representative joins a conversation (also fires for a collaborator or a transfer), When a conversation ends, On demand (representative selects Summarize conversation).
Custom record summaryAny table, such as accounts or work ordersAdd new summary in Custom record summaries, copy the Developer summary ID, then add the Copilot case summary control to the form.
  • Create case button: under When a conversation ends tick Allow customer service representatives to create case with a button in the summary. The summary also appears on the Summary tab of the closed conversation. AI agent conversations are not included automatically.
  • Conversation format (Live conversation summaries > Manage format): Paragraph or Structured. Structured defaults are Root cause, Customer issue, Troubleshooting steps, Outcome and Error code; use Add new info (title plus instructions), reorder, Reset to default info, and Remove information from the summary that can't be found.
  • Case and custom-record wizard (Manage data edits the default case summary): Specify record type → Specify data → Include related record summary → Manage summary format. Data rows: 1-to-1 up to 10 selections; 1-to-many up to 6 selections and 3 related entities; at least one 1-to-1 row for case summaries and at least one of the first seven default fields enabled. Email Content and Conversation Summary cannot be modified; Product needs prvReadProduct. Structured case format allows up to 5 custom headers (defaults Issue, Troubleshooting steps, Outcome, Error code, Root cause). Description and verbosity (Small, Medium, Large) are editable only on the default case summary.
Exam traps
  • A case with only a short title and a few words produces no summary: the 50-token minimum (about 38 words) is not a setting you can lower.
  • The Create case checkbox sits under the When a conversation ends setting. The usage page also lists the button on summaries of open conversations (generated automatically or with Summarize conversation) when the administrator turned it on and case management is configured.
  • Case summaries and custom record summaries are Customer Service features; Contact Center standalone gets conversation summaries.

Configure the Ask a question feature

Two admin centers are involved. Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Copilot (under Dynamics 365 Customer Service) > pick the environment > Edit setting > Enable AI-powered Copilot features. This is required for Customer Service Hub and custom apps, and it is where data movement and data sharing live. Copilot Service admin center is where you opt in and choose experiences: Support experience > Productivity > Copilot settings > Manage, then tick Copilot help pane - Ask a Question and/or Copilot immersive (preview).

QuestionAnswer
Who gets Copilot in Copilot Service workspace?Whoever has the feature in their experience profile; default profiles include it. To limit features, create a custom profile with only the needed Copilot features and assign it.
Who gets it in Customer Service Hub?All representatives once the feature is on.
Which role can use Copilot?Only Customer Service Representative by default. Custom roles need the listed Copilot table privileges and Miscellaneous privileges > prvIntelligenceUsage.

Behaviour is tuned on the Customer Support agent (Copilot settings > Agents within Copilot > Customer Support). Tabs: Overview, Immersive settings, Email settings, Prompts, Extend agent. On Overview, Instructions hold up to 5,000 characters of tone, escalation or terminology guidance, and Deterministic response returns repeatable output for validation and testing. The side pane needs Allow enhanced features; immersive always has them. Organisation prompts (Prompts tab) have Prompt text, In guide, Alias, Filter, Entity, Scope, and Instructions for Copilot up to 10,000 characters. Let representatives translate responses using Copilot enables translation. The Admin Management agent is Preview.

Filter (Manage filters)Visible to reps?Applied how
PresetNo, background onlyAlways, to knowledge articles
RepresentativeYes, but only with Filter status onReps select or clear it in the help pane
AutomatedOnly if Allow representatives to view or change this filter is onFrom the record the rep is working on; Use untagged content if the field value is null falls back to untagged articles

Filters apply to Ask a question and Draft a response; up to 5 per category; field types String, Whole Number, Option Set, Two Options Set. Turning on the view/change toggle prompts you to create a matching representative filter.

Exam traps
  • Custom apps and Customer Service Hub see no Copilot until Enable AI-powered Copilot features is on for the environment; in Copilot Service workspace the experience profile decides.
  • Instructions apply only when the Dynamics 365 knowledge base is the source; they are ignored for Copilot Studio sources.
  • A custom role with all Copilot tables but without prvIntelligenceUsage still cannot use Copilot.

Configure knowledge sources for Copilot in Dynamics 365 Customer Service

Which source serves which feature is the most tested rule:

FeatureKnowledge baseTrusted webpages (external web)Copilot Studio knowledge
Ask a questionYesNoYes
Write an emailYesYesNo
  • Knowledge base: off by default. Customer Support > Overview > Knowledge sources > tick Include a knowledge base or another type of knowledge source > Use your organization's knowledge base as knowledge source; the number of articles in use is shown. Knowledge management must be configured; an article must be the latest version, in state Published, and tagged with the same language as the user interface. Copilot reads only the content attribute and refreshes the content every day. Without the knowledge base, reps can still draft emails with Suggest a call, Request more information, Empathize with feedback and custom prompts.
  • Trusted webpages (Email settings tab): up to 5 domains, searched two levels down; Bing Search must be enabled in Power Platform admin center (plus cross-region data movement outside North America). Used for email and chat drafts only. The page cautions that the Bing Search API is deprecated, so results might not work as expected.
  • Copilot Studio knowledge: added to the managed Customer Service Copilot Bot from the Extend agent tab (for example SharePoint or a public website); see the next topic.
  • Verbatim answers: set on the article, not in Copilot settings. Add the doNotSummarize keyword to the content, or select a section and use the Verbatim icon, then save and publish. Applies to Ask a question only; Check sources opens the article view-only with the verbatim text highlighted.
Exam traps
  • A published article is ignored if a newer version exists or if its language differs from the UI language.
  • Trusted webpages never feed Ask a question, and Copilot Studio knowledge never feeds Write an email.
  • Marking text verbatim does not change email or chat drafting; those keep the normal generation behaviour.

Extend Copilot capabilities with prompt plugins and tools

The current page, Extend Copilot with Copilot Studio, is a production-ready Preview (supplemental terms apply). It states that, as of April 2026, extensibility for Copilot is managed mainly in Copilot Studio instead of Copilot Service admin center. Prerequisites: System Administrator or Customer Service administrator, a Copilot Studio licence in the tenant (Copilot credits), and Copilot enabled in Customer Service. It is not available in GCC M or GCC H.

  1. Copilot Service admin center > Productivity > Copilot settings > Manage > Agent within Copilot > Customer Support > Settings > Extend agent tab.
  2. Tick Extend agent with Copilot Studio and Save. Optionally select the plus icon to add custom context (entity, data field and a description the orchestrator uses).
  3. Select the Copilot Studio link to open the managed agent Customer Service Copilot Bot and add knowledge, tools, agents and topics.

Runtime order: is extensibility enabled → send the request and context to the Copilot Studio agent → show a confident answer → otherwise fall back to the configured knowledge sources. Rephrasing, summarizing and translating take priority over extensibility.

Tool type (agent > Tools > Add a tool)Use it to
Connector (prebuilt or custom)Call a service through Power Platform connectors, for example update an account address
Agent flow / PromptRun a multi-action flow / run a single-turn model prompt that can reference knowledge
REST API / Model Context Protocol / Computer useCall chosen API endpoints / use an MCP server's tools, for example account information / drive a screen-based system

With generative orchestration (default) the agent picks tools itself; in classic mode tools run only when a topic calls them. Limits: you cannot update the agent model, its instructions, managed topics named msdyn_*, or custom connectors that use OAuth (prefer Maker Authentication). Existing plugins and knowledge keep working; to change anything beyond the connection or tool description, create a new tool and remove the old one.

Legacy plugin model (still in the Learn training, marked Preview): prompt plugin (AI Builder prompt with a unique description), custom connector plugin (Power Automate custom connector) and certified connector plugin (for example Salesforce or DocuSign). Path: Support experience > Productivity > Plugins for generative AI (Preview) > Manage > Turn on; access is All agents who have Copilot or Specific user roles; Publish changes can take up to 15 minutes. One action per plugin. User authentication = Admin or Agent (each rep signs in; for sensitive data).

Exam traps
  • The Plugins for generative AI page is the earlier route (still taught in training); current documentation manages extensibility mainly in Copilot Studio through the Extend agent tab.
  • Copilot Studio extensibility cannot change the managed agent's model or instructions, or topics named msdyn_*.
  • To give a tool extra Dynamics 365 data such as a customer name, add custom context in Copilot Service admin center; default context covers only the current record, role and session metadata.

Interpret the Copilot analytics report

Enable: first opt in to the Copilot help pane and Copilot summaries. Then Copilot Service admin center > Insights > Manage for Copilot analytics > tick Enable Copilot analytics > save. Optional checkboxes add interactions on cases, emails and conversations. Provisioning can take up to 24 hours. View: Copilot Service workspace > Copilot analytics. By default System Administrator and Supervisor can open it; other roles need Read on the Copilot Analytics entity msdyn_dataanalyticsreport_copilot. Not available in Contact Center embedded. Filters: Duration (day, week, month) and Time zone. Raw data is in msdyn_copilotinteraction, msdyn_copilotinteractiondata, msdyn_copilottranscript and msdyn_copilottranscriptdata for custom reports.

GroupMetricMeaning
UsageDaily active usersUnique reps who used Copilot at least once in the last day
UsageTotal Copilot AI responsesAll responses Copilot provided
UsageNumber of responses used / percentageTimes response text was copied / share of responses copied
Productivity: ConversationsTotal conversations; number and percentage using CopilotEngaged conversations while Copilot was available; excludes email and voice; only ended conversations are listed for the using-Copilot count
Productivity: ConversationsAvg conversation handle time; Conversation throughputStart to end; conversations completed per day, each shown with and without Copilot
SatisfactionAgent ratingsCount of positive and negative ratings of Copilot responses

Reading it: many daily active users with a low percentage of responses used means reps try Copilot but do not apply the output; review knowledge sources, instructions and filters. Compare handle time and throughput with and without Copilot for the business case, and review weekly during rollout and monthly once stable.

Exam traps
  • "Responses used" counts copied text, not thumbs-up ratings (those are Agent ratings).
  • The conversation metrics leave out email and voice, so they cannot show the impact on calls.
  • Any role other than System Administrator and Supervisor needs Read on the Copilot Analytics entity before it can open the report.

Create a smart assist bot

Smart assist shows real-time next-best-step cards in the productivity pane (enabled by default) on chat, SMS, Facebook and similar channels, but not the Entity Records channel. It applies to Customer Service and Contact Center standalone, and cards appear only after the representative sends a message. A smart assist agent is a custom Azure Bot Service bot: Microsoft Copilot (Copilot Studio) agents are not supported and the End conversation command is not supported. Case and knowledge suggestions through smart assist have been unsupported since June 2, 2025; use Copilot instead.

  1. Build and register: register the bot in Azure Bot Service as a User-Assigned Managed Identity, set the messaging endpoint, register an app in Microsoft Entra ID, and add the Omnichannel channel in the Azure portal. A GitHub sample (smart-assist-bot) shows knowledge article recommendations.
  2. Create the agent user: Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > New app user, top-level business unit, role Omnichannel agent (add Customer Service Manager or Customer Service Representative if the bot searches knowledge), add the bot's app. Then Copilot Service admin center > User management > Users > APPLICATION USER form: User type = Bot application user and the Bot Application ID.
  3. Add to the workstream: Customer support > Workstreams > your workstream > Advanced settings > Smart assist bots > Add bot > Add from existing > select the agent user > Add. Several bots can be added.
NeedUse
Own logic or non-Microsoft AI that recommends actions to repsSmart assist bot (Azure Bot Service)
Knowledge answers and summaries for repsCopilot Ask a question
Customer-facing self-service (voice agents: §3.2)Copilot Studio AI agent in the workstream's AI agent section
Exam traps
  • A Copilot Studio agent cannot be a smart assist agent, and a smart assist bot is not added in the workstream's AI agent section.
  • The agent user needs the Omnichannel agent role, and the app user must be created in the web client with the bot's application ID.
  • No cards appear until the representative has sent a message, even when everything is configured.

Sources: Enable Copilot case and conversation summaries · Manage case and custom record summary · Customize conversation summaries · Manage Copilot features · Enable features in Copilot · Verbatim responses · Extend Copilot with Copilot Studio · Add tools to custom agents · Extend Copilot with plugins and measure its impact · Manage analytics for Copilot · View Copilot analytics report · Smart assist · Integrate an Azure agent

sections.title: 3.2 Configure voice agents
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure IVR with voice agents by using generative AI or classic orchestration • Manage variables in Copilot Studio • Secure the Dynamics 365 Contact Center voice channel • Configure compliant call recording in Copilot Studio • Configure SIP header transfers • Configure the Real-time Speech agent • Configure dual-tone multi-frequency (DTMF), natural language understanding (NLU) and speech-based IVR • Configure Copilot Studio voice triggers • Implement best practices for configuring voice agents • Configure multilingual voice agents. Practise by building a basic voice agent with a DTMF PIN question, a consent topic and a SIP X-header transfer, then a real-time agent on a second voice workstream. Learn documents the Real-time Speech agent as real-time voice agents (speech-to-speech).

Configure IVR with voice agents by using generative AI or classic orchestration

An IVR agent is a Copilot Studio agent with voice enabled that answers calls on a Dynamics 365 voice workstream. In Settings > Voice > Enable voice you choose Basic (topics and classic orchestration) or Real-time (generative orchestration; see the real-time topic below). The orchestration switch is Settings > Generative AI > Orchestration, where No means classic.

Classic orchestrationGenerative AI orchestration
How it answersMatches the caller's words to topics by trigger phrases and keywordsAI chooses actions, knowledge or topics and reacts to event triggers such as start handoff
Best forKeypad menus, PIN capture, fixed compliance flows (deterministic)Open-ended requests and varied phrasing
Voice typeBasic voiceReal-time voice
  1. Acquire phone numbers (Azure Communication Services) or bring your own carrier.
  2. Create a voice workstream with its routing rules.
  3. Set up the voice channel in that workstream and link the number.
  4. Create the agent (Copilot Studio, or Copilot Service admin center and finish in Copilot Studio), enable voice, then Channels > Telephony > Turn on telephony, select Dynamics 365 Customer Service > Connect, and publish. Turn Telephony on first, then connect.
  5. Add the published agent to the voice workstream.
  • Rules: one agent per workstream; agents receive conversations only in push-based workstreams; agents created in Copilot Service admin center work with enhanced voice workstreams only (create classic agents for non-migrated voice workstreams in Copilot Studio). You need the CCI Admin role to open the agent in Copilot Studio plus the Omnichannel administrator role; usage is billed in Copilot credits.
  • Platform limits: basic voice runs only in standard environments (Get new features early must be off). Only Dynamics 365 Customer Service supports voice agents; Genesys, LivePerson, Salesforce and ServiceNow support chat-based agents only.
  • Call limit: a bot-handled call lasts at most one hour and is disconnected unless it ends or escalates; the limit stops applying after a transfer to a representative or external number.
Fallback action (workstream > Bot > Edit)What the caller gets
Prompt and hang-upDefault message, then the call ends
Prompt and transfer to external numberDefault message, then a transfer to the number in External phone number (E.164: + country code)
Prompt and escalateDefault message, then a representative
Wait Music and EscalateWait music, then a representative

The Fallback calls metric (Omnichannel historical bot dashboard and real-time analytics) counts calls the customer started that could not be connected because of system or network problems.

Exam traps
  • Turn Telephony on before connecting to Dynamics 365; the order matters when the channel is reconnected.
  • Classic orchestration is the No answer to the generative AI orchestration question, and keypad-driven menus belong there.
  • A second agent cannot be added to the same workstream, and a pull-based workstream cannot hand work to an agent.

Manage variables in Copilot Studio

ScopeFacts
TopicDefault; usable only in the topic that created it
GlobalAll topics during one session. Variable properties > Global (any topic can access); the name gets the Global. prefix and must be unique. Clear variable values resets it (the Reset Conversation system topic uses it). Deleting a global variable leaves Unknown references.
SystemCreated automatically and available in all topics
EnvironmentCreated in Power Platform; read-only in Copilot Studio

Types: String, Boolean, Number, Table, Record, DateTime, Choice, Blank. The first assignment fixes the type.

Receive Contact Center context in the agent:

  1. In the voice workstream: Advanced settings > Add context variable (Name, Type). Names are case-sensitive and at most 100 characters; values at most 4,000; do not rename or delete a variable that is in use.
  2. In Copilot Studio add a dedicated topic (for example Set context variables; no trigger phrases needed) with a Set variable value node.
  3. Create the variable with a name that matches the incoming name exactly; Usage = Global (any topic can access) and External sources can set values.
  4. Reference (⋮) > Get value from this node if empty; optionally set a timeout (use at most 10 seconds, 10,000 ms for Omnichannel variables) and a default value in the node, for example Text("") for an empty string.

If the agent assigns the variable itself, that value wins over the external one. Agents published to the Contact Center channel for IVR do not support timeout values for externally set global variables. Mapping from Contact Center: string → User's entire response, Boolean → Boolean, number → Number.

Voice variableHolds
System.Activity.From.Name / System.Activity.Recipient.NameCaller ID / the number the caller dialled. Copy them into a global variable in the Conversation Start topic.
System.Activity.UserInputTypeWhether the last input was speech or DTMF
System.Conversation.OnlyAllowDTMFBoolean; true makes voice ignore speech
System.Activity.SpeechRecognition.Confidence0 to 1 confidence of the last recognition
System.Conversation.SipUuiHeaderValueSIP UUI value when transferring through a direct routing number
Exam traps
  • Environment variables cannot be edited in Copilot Studio; change them in Power Platform.
  • A Contact Center variable that arrives empty usually has a name that differs in case or spelling, or is not marked Global with External sources can set values.
  • The 10-second timeout advice does not apply to IVR agents on the Contact Center channel, which ignore timeouts.

Secure the Dynamics 365 Contact Center voice channel

RequirementControl
No audio recording anywhereCopilot Service admin center > Quality Management > Enable screen and call recording > Manage > Turn on audio recording. Switching it off overrides every workstream setting.
Record or transcribe calls on a workstreamVoice workstream > phone number Edit > Voice settings > Behaviors > Transcription and recording: Transcription or Transcription and recording; Start setting Automatic or Manual; allow reps to pause and resume; automatic pause on hold
Hide a spoken PIN or card numberSensitive data = On on the variable (Variable properties)
Keep digits out of the speech transcriptDTMF-only agent: speech is ignored and only keypad tones are captured; speech is not stored in the Copilot Studio transcript
Mask card numbers typed in chatData masking rule (regular expression): chat and asynchronous channels only, maximum 10 rules including Credit Card, Email and SSN
Stop spam callersCustomer settings > Blocked numbers > Manage: Pending review and Blocked tabs, Block a number, Auto-block after repeated reports

Recording prerequisites: register Event Grid system topics for Azure Communication Services events and allow the audio and mpeg MIME types in Power Platform admin center (Privacy + security settings). Many jurisdictions require caller consent; meeting the law is your responsibility.

Sensitive variable masking needs the voice channel, inbound calling, a voice agent in a workstream, and the System administrator and Bot author roles. Open Variable properties ({x}) and set Sensitive data to On. At run time the transcript shows "Entered a confidential section of the conversation" and recording, transcription and data logging pause (silence is inserted so the audio length still matches) until "Exited a confidential section" and "Recording and transcription resumed" appear. A sensitive variable assigned to another variable makes that one sensitive. Not redacted: explicit writes to Dataverse, data received from connectors or Power Automate, values passed in transfer nodes or to generative AI or custom Application Insights events, and Contact Center transcripts of digital channels; unflagged variables are never redacted and the first answer might escape redaction. Keep Log sensitive activity properties off.

Other facts: manual masking works for voice transcripts but does not remove text from retained audio. The voice channel is PCI DSS compliant, but capturing credit card data over voice is not yet supported; representatives can pause recording and transcription.

Exam traps
  • Data masking rules never hide spoken digits; use a sensitive variable, DTMF capture or pausing instead.
  • The tenant-level audio switch beats any workstream recording setting.
  • Only variables the maker flags are redacted, and Dataverse writes, connectors and transfer nodes are outside the protection.

Configure compliant call recording in Copilot Studio

Consent-based recording lets a voice-enabled agent ask for permission when the call connects; without consent nothing is recorded or transcribed. It works only for inbound voice workstreams that have a voice-enabled agent, not for outbound calls or workstreams without an agent. Prerequisites: a Copilot Studio licence, the voice channel provisioned, and inbound calling set up.

  1. In Copilot Studio: Settings > Security > Authentication > No authentication, then save.
  2. Channels > Telephony > Turn on telephony; select Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Connect.
  3. Settings > Voice: turn voice on (this page still labels it Optimize for voice; other pages say Enable voice) and keep Increase accuracy with agent data off.
  4. Edit the sample User Consent topic (Topics > Custom), then add Topic management > Go to another topic > User Consent to the Conversation Start system topic. Save and publish.
  5. In Copilot Service admin center: create the inbound voice workstream, set up recording and transcription, and under Transcription and recording turn on Request for User Consent.
Workstream: Request for user consentCopilot Studio consent topicResult
OnOnConsent is offered to all callers
OnOffEvery caller counts as opted in; with recording enabled on the workstream the call is recorded and transcribed
OffOn or OffConsent is never offered
  • No answer to the prompt is treated as implicit consent; a misconfigured topic means the call is recorded by default.
  • Recording starts when the caller connects to the agent. A refusal stops it immediately and no transcript is produced; representatives cannot start, pause or view recording or transcripts, also after escalation, transfers and consults. Transcription-only follows the same model. A transfer to a non-Microsoft party outside Contact Center is not recorded by Microsoft.
  • The consent prompt and answer are kept in Microsoft-managed storage that customers cannot access and are deleted within two hours.
  • For an existing agent, create a custom topic in the code editor and call it from Conversation Start. Abridged excerpt:
kind: AdaptiveDialog
beginDialog:
  kind: OnRedirect
  id: main
  actions:
    - kind: ConditionGroup
      conditions:
        - condition: =Global.AskForConsent = true
          actions:
            - kind: Question
              variable: Global.ConsentResponse
              entity:
                kind: BooleanPrebuiltEntity
            - kind: SendActivity
              activity:
                kind: EventActivity
                name: Sys.ConsentEvent
                value: =Global.ConsentResponse
Exam traps
  • Turning on Request for User Consent does not create a prompt; the agent needs the consent topic called from Conversation Start.
  • Silence counts as consent, and workstream Off wins whatever the topic does.
  • Outbound calls and workstreams without a voice-enabled agent are not supported.

Configure SIP header transfers

Voice agents pass call context in two ways. Both apply to incoming calls and to transfers to external numbers on a direct routing telephony setup, and Copilot Studio supports blind transfer to a PSTN or direct routing number.

SIP UUI (User-to-User)SIP X-headers
PurposeStandard field for extended call dataCustom, flexible context fields
OutboundTransfer conversation node > External phone number transfer > ⋮ > Properties > SIP UUI header: key=value pairs, only letters, numbers, = and ;, no spaces; first 256 characters sent; variables not supported; target must use direct routing (PSTN numbers do not support UUI transfers)Same node > Properties > + Add: names start with X- or x- and are sent as typed; value static or a variable; up to 5 headers, name up to 64, value up to 256 characters; External phone number transfer only
InboundThe IVR sends a SIP INVITE with User-to-User: param1=value1;param2=value2 (plain text, hex with ;encoding=hex, or hex with ;pd=4). Create workstream context variables (voice workstream > Edit > Advanced settings > Add context variable) with names that match the keys exactly.Variable management > Parse value node on Conversation.SipXHeader, Data type From sample data, schema from sample JSON using lowercase x- names, saved to a Global variable. Only the first 5 headers arrive; a missing one is an empty string.
{
  "x-CallID": "",
  "x-AAI-Incoming": ""
}

To integrate a non-Microsoft IVR, set up Azure direct routing with a Session Border Controller linked to Azure Communication Services, register the IVR number with Bring your own carrier, and have the IVR issue the INVITE. Recordings and transcripts of the IVR leg are not available to representatives. X-headers also require Contact Center voice-enabled agents and Copilot Studio.

Exam traps
  • Incoming X-header names must be lowercase x- in the schema even when the sender uses X-; outgoing names are sent exactly as typed.
  • UUI cannot carry variables or spaces and needs direct routing; X-headers can use variables.
  • UUI keys must match workstream context variable names exactly, and only the first five incoming X-headers are read.

Configure the Real-time Speech agent

Real-time voice agents give low-latency, speech-to-speech conversations over voice (DTMF, barge-in and voice activity detection included) and, as a Preview, over digital messaging channels.

  1. Create a new agent. Settings > Voice > Enable voice, then Voice type = Real-time. The choice is one-time: you cannot switch back to a basic agent, so create another agent for that.
  2. Choose the model: GPT-Realtime, GPT-Realtime-Mini Preview or GPT-5-Chat Preview.
  3. Settings > Security > Authentication > No authentication.
  4. Save; on Channels make sure Telephony is on and connected to Dynamics 365 Customer Service; publish; add the agent to a voice workstream (or a messaging channel).
ModelPick it when
GPT-RealtimeLowest latency and natural speech-to-speech conversation
GPT-5-Chat (Preview)A text LLM voice model (speech to text, reasoning, then Microsoft Neural text-to-speech): higher latency, but custom or branded voices, compliance needs and regional flexibility
GPT-Realtime-Mini (Preview)Fast speech interactions with lower latency and resource use

Callers hear the voice chosen in Copilot Studio (Settings > Voice > Select voice); voice profile settings in the workstream do not apply. To match Dynamics system message voices use Alloy, Ash, Echo or Shimmer.

VAD (Settings > Voice > Phone Setup > Speech input > Sensitivity)Use whenSettings
Based on sound (silence), server VADStructured IVR-style turns, short answers, background noiseThreshold 0.6 (range 0.5 to 0.7), prefix padding 300 ms, silence duration 750 ms
Based on sentence context, semantic VADOpen-ended talk, hesitation, filler wordsEagerness: Low, Medium (default), High
  • DTMF (Settings > Voice > Conversation behavior > DTMF) is supported on voice; a DTMF-only experience needs a mapping on every input node.
  • Silence detection (Conversation behavior) is off by default, so the agent waits indefinitely. When on, the default timeout is 7,000 ms; add a reprompt and make the fallback (escalate, hang up) intentional.
  • Design: use topics only where behaviour must be deterministic; static greetings are fastest; disable Conversation Start if the model should greet; give On Error an explicit transfer or end call; only child agents are supported (Preview); evaluation sends text only.
  • Add every secondary language. Localisation strings are not required, but deterministic topic messages need translations; test non-English calls with real callers because only some languages are formally validated.
Exam traps
  • Real-time cannot be reverted to basic, and it requires No authentication.
  • A greeting in the Conversation Start topic plays instead of the model greeting, and silence detection must be turned on explicitly.
  • GPT-5-Chat is the choice for custom voices, not for lowest latency.

Configure dual-tone multi-frequency (DTMF), natural language understanding (NLU) and speech-based IVR

DTMF. Multiple-choice options get keys manually (Assign DTMF keys to options); list-variable and Boolean options are mapped automatically in order from 0 to 9. Multi-digit input works for User's entire response, Number, Phone number, Zip code, Money, Date, Age and similar entities (City, Email, Person name and Street address do not support DTMF). Set the digits as a fixed length ("5") or a range ("2-5"); a wrong length repeats the question. The optional termination key is none, * or # and is not counted. The DTMF global command received trigger takes a single key (properties: key, condition, priority) and is not called when that key answers a multi-digit question or matches an option. An unmapped key triggers the Unknown dial pad press system topic. DTMF caching lets callers type ahead. In the test panel type /DTMFKey 1 because the dial pad is not supported.

Agent-level voice setting (Settings > Voice)Default
DTMF interdigit timeout (wait for the next digit)3,000 ms
DTMF termination timeout (wait for the termination key at maximum length)2,000 ms
Silence detection timeoutNo silence timeout (waits indefinitely)
Utterance end timeout1,500 ms; maximum 3,000 ms
Speech recognition timeout12,000 ms
Speech sensitivity (no node-level override)0.5; lower it for noisy places

At node level, a Question can Use agent setting, Disable for this node or Customize in milliseconds for silence, reprompt up to 2 times, once or never, and set a Fallback action: Hang up (default), Escalate, Set variable to value, Set variable to empty, or Redirect to a topic. In DTMF-only mode the interdigit and silence timers are not supported.

Speech IVR features: Increase accuracy with agent data (works only with trigger phrases, not topic descriptions), barge-in (turn it off for recently updated, compliance or first messages), SSML (<audio>, <break>, <emphasis>, <prosody>, <lang>), latency messages, answering machine detection, and constrained recognition with grammars for alphanumeric strings.

Microsoft Copilot Studio NLUNLU+
Where data is processedWithin Copilot StudioWithin Dynamics 365 (data is exchanged between the two); needs a Dynamics 365 Contact Center licence
BuildChanges are picked up automaticallyAnnotate trigger phrases and entities, then select Train NLU+ model (Topics or Entities page); training is required before you can test or publish
FitGeneral useLarge enterprise agents with many topics, entities and training samples; grammar-based exact matching; the training data also tunes speech recognition

NLU+ setup page: Settings > Generative AI > Orchestration > No, then Language understanding > NLU+ ("More prework, enhanced precision"), then save. The IVR overview words the pairing with orchestration differently, so follow the setup page. Annotate trigger phrases with {Topic.Variable_Name/Entity_item_or_synonym} and keep determiners and prepositions out of entity literals.

Exam traps
  • The DTMF received trigger handles single keys only; a multi-digit answer or a mapped option bypasses it.
  • NLU versus NLU+ is about where processing happens and how the model is built; NLU+ must be trained before testing or publishing.
  • Silence detection has no timeout by default, and Increase accuracy with agent data has no effect when topics are selected by description.

Configure Copilot Studio voice triggers

Voice behaviour hangs on a few triggers and system topics. Enabling voice adds Silence detection, Speech unrecognized and Unknown dial pad press; turning voice off removes them and disables DTMF triggers, which can break an agent whose Telephony channel is on.

Trigger or system topicFires whenNotes
Conversation StartThe call beginsGreeting, consent redirect, copying System.Activity.From.Name to a global variable
DTMF global command receivedA single key is pressed outside a question that uses itKey, condition, priority
Unknown dial pad pressA pressed key has no mappingCustomise the business logic
Silence detectionThe caller gives no inputUse agent setting, Disable for this node, or Customize in milliseconds
Speech unrecognizedSpeech is not recognisedAdded when voice is enabled
Answering Machine DetectionA voicemail answersThe Message node leaves the message; an End conversation node stops further processing
An activity occurs > Activity type End of conversationThe call ends for any reasonOptional condition on Conversation.EndReason
On Talk to representativeThe caller asks for a personTransfer conversation node, Transfer to agent

Post-call actions: Copilot Studio sends an End of conversation activity however the call ends. With no condition, the topic runs for every reason. Add Conversation.EndReason to limit it:

Conversation.EndReasonMeaning
CUSTOMER_HANGUPThe caller disconnects
BLIND_TRANSFERThe agent transfers to an external phone number
CCAAS_TRANSFERThe agent escalates to Dynamics 365 Contact Center

Real-time agents: supported triggers are Conversation Start, On Talk to representative, Reset Conversation, Unknown DTMF key press (voice), agent chooses or user says a phrase, redirected, Silence detection (voice), On Error, and user inactive (digital only). Not supported: Unknown intent, OnSelectIntent, Sign in, a message is received, custom client event, conversation update, invoked, a plan completes, AI response generated.

Exam traps
  • An End of conversation topic without a Conversation.EndReason condition also runs for transfers and escalations, so a CRM update meant only for hang-ups needs CUSTOMER_HANGUP.
  • Real-time agents have no Unknown intent or fallback trigger; rely on the model and an explicit On Error topic.
  • Switching voice off silently disables DTMF triggers.

Implement best practices for configuring voice agents

AreaPractice
Queue and workstream (queue setup: §4.1)When agents and representatives share a queue, set the agent's capacity higher than all representatives; it is not reduced after assignment, so the agent picks up first. Add the agent that greets the customer to the workstream, not the queue, so the routing engine is not involved. Agents are not in the default queue; add them in Copilot Service admin center.
EscalationUpdate context variables before escalating and make the routing rules match. A conversation that comes back to the same queue is not reassigned to the agent that escalated it, so give the agent-only queue a representative to avoid an infinite loop.
LatencyGreet first, then look up data. Prefer Dataverse connectors for Dynamics data and HTTP requests for outside data; Power Automate pauses the agent until the flow ends. Use a latency message with a minimum playback time (default 5,000 ms) and a delay activity between messages (default 500 ms). Use system greeting messages for a static, uninterruptible message before the agent greets; avoid repeating it in the agent greeting.
MessagesKeep each message at or below 28 KB in all messaging channels (metadata included).
Voice designCapture PINs and card numbers by DTMF. Prefer per-question DTMF mapping to a global DTMF-only setting, and avoid informational messages between questions in DTMF-only mode (they can cause empty grammar and telephony errors). Keep barge-in on for long menus, off for compliance and first messages. Customise Fallback and On Error.
Network and clientsWired or stable network, USB headsets with noise-cancelling microphones, allowlist the Contact Center URLs and IP addresses and follow Azure Communication Services firewall guidance. Same-region latency is usually under 150 ms; enable telemetry insights to find delays. Use the desktop companion app when representatives are slow to join calls.
NLU+ and real-timeNLU+: real-world training data, distinct intents and entities. Real-time: static greetings, explicit On Error action, explicit topic and tool descriptions.
Exam traps
  • If representatives have higher capacity than the agent, they receive the work first; the agent must be higher.
  • Putting the greeting agent on the queue instead of the workstream slows the first response.
  • Escalated conversations that return to the agent-only queue loop unless the queue also has a representative.

Configure multilingual voice agents

Workstream patternBehaviour
Several voice channels, each with its own number and primary languageThe agent answers in the channel's language. If that language is not one of the agent's primary or secondary languages, it answers in its primary language.
One channel and number with several languagesThe agent greets in its primary language, the caller picks a language by voice or keypad (for example press 1 for English), and the agent switches.
  1. In Copilot Studio add languages (Settings > Languages > Add language) as primary or secondary and supply translations of topic messages. The primary language cannot be changed after the agent is created.
  2. In the voice workstream add the phone number and set the channel languages, then add the agent in the workstream's Bots section. A warning appears if the channel languages differ from the agent's.
  3. Define language-based routing rules (work classification). For escalation create a voice queue for each language with representatives who speak it, and in the route-to-queues rule set use Conversation.CustomerLanguage as the criterion.
  • Publishing a multilingual voice agent to the Contact Center channel requires No authentication.
  • The transcript is in the language the agent detects and falls back to the channel's primary language if the agent switches to one the channel does not support.
  • Dynamic language switching (generative orchestration): a topic triggered by A message is received runs a prompt that detects the language of Activity.Text, branches on the result and sets the User.Language system variable. That choice persists as an override; /debug clearstate clears it when testing.
  • Metrics: in the Omnichannel historical bot dashboard add the Last Language filter, which is not there by default.

Docs example: English primary with Spanish and French secondary; a German channel is answered in English because the agent does not support German.

Exam traps
  • An unsupported channel language does not fail the call; the agent falls back to its primary language.
  • Routing to a Spanish-speaking representative needs a Spanish queue and a rule on Conversation.CustomerLanguage, not just a Spanish phone number.
  • After testing dynamic language switching, clear the persisted language with /debug clearstate before you test browser-based language detection; a separate test agent avoids the clash.

sections.title: 4.1 Configure queues
sections.html:
Skills measured: create and manage queues • configure queue prioritization • configure overflow and fallback • configure work assignment methods • set up operating hours. Practise by building a messaging queue with a queue priority, operating hours, an overflow condition and an assignment method, then using it as a route-to-queue target and as the fallback queue of a workstream (§4.2).

Create and manage queues

A queue collects work (records such as cases, conversations such as chat or SMS) and distributes it to its member reps through an assignment method. The queue type follows the channel, and routing rules offer only queues of the matching type: a live chat rule lists only messaging queues, a chat can be transferred only to a messaging queue and a case only to a record queue.

TypeRoutes
MessagingLive chat, SMS and social conversations
RecordWork items for records such as cases and emails
VoiceCalls made to the support phone numbers
  1. Copilot Service admin center > Customer support > Queues > Manage for Advanced queues > New.
  2. In Create a queue enter Name, Type and Queue priority (a number), then Create.
  3. Add users, then choose the Assignment method, Overflow management > Set overflow conditions and Operation hours > Set operation hours. The operating hour record must already exist; with none selected the queue is available round the clock.
  • Metrics Threshold > Add Threshold: Service Level Threshold and Short Abandoned Threshold, both entered in seconds, support SLA and short-abandonment reporting per queue.
  • Manage: search, edit, delete, Copy (inherits the settings; the name gets the prefix "Copy of") and Share (permissions on related tables need a custom plug-in). With unified routing on, keep the default Queue form or you cannot create a basic queue in Customer Service Hub.
  • Default queues (system-defined): Default entity queue, Default messaging queue, Default voice queue. All reps with the Omnichannel agent role are members and only the assignment method is editable, so create advanced queues instead; a default queue can still be a workstream's fallback queue.
  • A routed conversation is owned by the root business unit owner until it is assigned. Set msdyn_issetowneridfromqueueoninitenabled to true on msdyn_omnichannelconfiguration to use the queue owner's business unit while it waits.
Scale limitDefault methodsCustom assignment
Users per queue5,0002,000
Users across queues10,00010,000
Work items waiting across queues50,00010,000
Exam traps
  • A queue of the wrong type never appears in a workstream's routing rules or in transfer lists.
  • Default queues cannot be created or reconfigured beyond their assignment method.
  • No operating hour record on a queue means available 24x7, not closed.
  • Channel and routing configuration changes can take up to 15 minutes to take effect.

Configure queue prioritization

Queue priorityPrioritization ruleset
OrdersWork across the queues a rep is subscribed toWork inside one queue
Set inThe Queue priority number on the queueA custom assignment method
RuleThe smaller number is served first (conversation queues 1, case queues 2; premium chat 1, general 2)Ordered rules form priority buckets, each sorted by Order by; unmatched items go to the last bucket in first-in-first-out order; one ruleset per queue
  • Default inside a queue: first in, first out. Chat and voice use creation time, asynchronous channels such as WhatsApp or persistent chat use last interaction time, and records use the time they were routed.
  • Equal queue priority: default first-in-first-out queues serve the oldest item across them; queues with custom prioritization are ordered alphabetically by queue name. Queues on out-of-box methods are served before queues with custom prioritization, so give custom-prioritization queues distinct priorities.
  • Prioritization rules run in every assignment cycle, so a changed case priority applies at the next cycle. Affinity work items skip them and are assigned first.
  • Build a ruleset: queue > Assignment method > Create new > Create work assignment (name) > select it > Edit > prioritization ruleset: Template ruleset (decision rules cannot be modified at queue level), Copy from template or New ruleset > Decision list > Create rule (conditions plus order by).
  • Cross-queue prioritization is limited to 100 queues with default methods and 20 with custom assignment.
  • Preview Dynamic prioritization (natural language playbooks in conversation orchestration) raises a priority score with wait time or on queue transfer, for voice and live chat only. Score 0–100,000, minimum interval 30 seconds, ties first in first out; queues with priority escalation should not have custom prioritization rules.
Exam traps
  • A smaller queue-priority number means higher priority.
  • Queue priority is not the dynamic priority score (0–100,000).
  • Only one prioritization ruleset can exist per queue.

Configure overflow and fallback

With no overflow handling a work item simply waits in the queue. Overflow acts before queueing (checked once, after the route-to-queue rules and before the item enters the queue; with an AI agent, only after it escalates) or after queueing. Prerequisites: unified routing, queues with reps, route-to-queue rules in the workstream for pre-queue overflow, and outbound-capable numbers for Transfer to an external number.

ChannelBefore queueing: conditions → actionsAfter queueing: Waiting time in queue exceeds
VoiceOut of operating hours; Work item limit exceeds; Average wait time (30 seconds–60 minutes) → Assign to queue anyway, Direct callback, End call, Transfer to a different queue, Transfer to an external number, Voicemail1–60 minutes → Direct callback, Transfer to a different queue, Transfer to an external number, Voicemail
MessagingOut of operating hours; Work item limit exceeds → End conversation, Transfer to a different queue, Assign to queue anyway1 minute–2 days → End conversation, Transfer to a different queue
RecordOut of operating hours → Assign to queue anyway, Transfer to a different queue3 minutes–2 days → Transfer to a different queue
  • Set up: Customer support > Queues > Advanced queues > the queue > Overflow handling > Add condition-action pair under Before work items are queued; for queued items choose Edit > When work items are queued. Work item limit exceeds takes 1–100 and the queue position refreshes every 10 seconds.
  • Adding an operating hour record creates the condition Out of operation hours with the action Assign to queue anyway. You cannot edit the condition but you can change the action. Hours set on the channel in the workstream do not affect overflow.
  • When several conditions are true, the operating-hours action runs first, then the others in the order defined. Of several matching queues the first non-overflowing one gets the item. For priority customers use Handle rule-specific overflows (workstream > route-to-queue rule > queue > More commands).
  • Edit the message for End call or End conversation under Customer settings > Automated messages, trigger End conversation due to overflow.
  • Fallback queue: one per workstream, chosen with Create new (add users afterwards) or Choose existing (default: the out-of-box queue for the channel) when you create it, or later on the workstream page. Default assignment is Highest capacity. It receives work after a classification error, a route-to-queue rule error, or when no route-to-queue rule matches, and it overrules overflow: its overflow settings are ignored.
Exam traps
  • Fallback is not overflow: work reaches a fallback queue through errors or unmatched rules, and its overflow settings are ignored.
  • Voicemail, direct callback, End call and external transfer are voice-only actions; messaging queues can end the conversation.
  • The default Out of operation hours action keeps the work in the queue until you change it.
  • Queue overflow rules are evaluated once, before queueing; a conversation-orchestration playbook condition for a queue being out of operating hours is evaluated continuously.

Configure work assignment methods

Set the method on the queue: Customer support > Queues > Advanced queues > the queue > Assignment method.

MethodHow it picks
Highest capacityMost available capacity among reps with the classified skills and an allowed presence; ties by round robin. Workstream skill matching: Exact Match filters on exact skills then orders by capacity; Closest Match orders by closest skill match instead
Advanced round robinMatches skills, presence and capacity; order starts with when the user joined the queue, then follows assignments, kept per queue
Least activeLongest since capacity was last released, plus the workstream Block capacity for wrap-up setting; voice and messaging queues only
No auto assignmentNobody: work stays queued until a rep picks it from the Inbox or a supervisor assigns it from the ongoing conversation dashboard
Create newCustom method with prioritization rulesets and assignment rulesets
  • Assignment ruleset: ordered rules; each has conditions (up to two levels of related records) and an Order by (Least active, Round robin, Unit-based or Profile-based available capacity, Proficiency, Skill count, or a user attribute). The lowest-order rule runs first, and if no rep matches, the next rule relaxes the constraints; no match leaves the item queued. With more than one assignment ruleset, define selection criteria.
  • Condition attributes: System User columns, Presence Status, Capacity, User skills (Exact match, Custom match), Calendar schedule (Is working) and bot attributes. Rollup and calculated fields and fields with field-level security are not supported.
  • A custom method ignores the workstream defaults, so configure presence, capacity and skill matching in its rules. Default methods ignore rep working hours: use Is working, which checks the rep's service scheduling calendar, not the queue's operating hours.
  • Assignment cycle triggers: new work item, presence change, runtime capacity update (a manual one does not), rep added to the queue, and every five minutes for records.
  • Declines: rejecting or letting the notification time out counts. A rep is reconsidered for the same item up to 3 times by default; change it to 1–5 with msdyn_number_of_declines_allowed on msdyn_omnichannelconfiguration (null means 3). After 100 decliners auto assignment skips the item.
  • Push or Pick is the workstream's work distribution mode, fixed at creation (§4.2).
Exam traps
  • Least active is not available for record queues.
  • No auto assignment (queue method) differs from the Pick work distribution mode (workstream setting that cannot be edited).
  • Queue operating hours do not stop auto assignment to off-shift reps; only a custom rule with Calendar schedule Is working does.

Set up operating hours

An operating hour record is a schedule with working hours, holidays and time zones. Create it in Copilot Service admin center > Operations > Calendars > Operating Hours > Manage > New:

  1. General tab: Name, Owner, optional Description, then Save.
  2. Working Hours tab (default 8:00 am–5:00 pm) > New > Working hours: All Day, Calendar (dates are selectable only when All Day is Yes), Time, Repeat, optional end date and Time zone (daylight saving is taken into account). Save.
  3. Holiday: New > Holiday, pick the date or range, give a reason, then save.

Edit an event for This event, This and all following events or All events in the series.

Apply toHow
QueueQueue page > Operation hours > Set operation hours > select the record. No record means 24x7
Chat widget (§2.1)Chat channel settings > chat widget tab > Show widget during operation hours On > Operating hours name; Show widget outside of operation hours shows it outside those hours
SMSBehaviors tab of the channel instance, opened from its workstream
Social channelsConfigured at the queue level
  • Separate schedules can serve reps, AI agents and queues. Messages that customers see or hear outside hours come from automated messages.
  • Queue hours add the default overflow condition Out of operation hours; hours set on a channel in the workstream do not affect overflow.
  • The Calendar entity cannot be moved with export and import; set up work hours manually.
Exam traps
  • The admin center calls the record Operating Hours; the queue field says Operation hours.
  • Closing on a public holiday means adding a Holiday to the record, not a second schedule.
  • Queue hours control queue availability and overflow, not which reps are on shift.
