Skills measured: workstreams, context variables and Copilot Studio agents • work classification rules • engagement agent • skills-based routing • AI-enabled skills-based routing • intent-based routing • preferred representative routing • routing for records • basic routing rule sets • conversation diagnostics. Build a push chat workstream with a Copilot Studio agent, a classification ruleset that attaches a skill and a route-to-queue rule, then open one test conversation with Diagnose.

Configure workstreams, including configuring context variables and associating agents in Copilot Studio

A workstream is the container that enriches, routes and assigns work items. One workstream can serve several channel instances of the same type (for example two chat widgets), and all of them inherit its settings. Types: Messaging (live chat, SMS, social, Microsoft Teams), Record (case, email, activity; unified routing must be enabled) and Voice (calls to support numbers; push only). Inside a workstream the pipeline is intake (records only) → work classification → route-to-queue → assignment by the queue's method.

  1. Copilot Service admin center > Customer support > Workstreams > New workstream. You need the System Administrator role or permission to modify secure columns.
  2. Enter Name, Type, the Channel or Record type (for Chat a Make chats persistent box appears; then also set Keep same representative for entire conversation) and the Work distribution mode: Push (the system alerts representatives) or Pick (representatives take items from the open work items). The mode can't be edited later.
  3. Choose the Fallback queue (Create new, or Choose existing; the out-of-the-box queue of the channel type is preselected), select Create, then configure the channel instance.

Work distribution > See more: Auto-close after inactivity (persistent chat, SMS, social, Teams only); Capacity (Unit based or Profile based); Block capacity for wrap up (Always block is the default, Don't block, or Custom time of 30 seconds to 60 minutes); Allowed presences (leave out Inactive and Do not disturb to stop new work reaching representatives who miss or reject); Default skill matching algorithm; Keep same representative for entire conversation (push only). Advanced settings hold Sessions, Representative notifications, Context variables, Smart assist agents and Quick replies; the templates are covered in §5.1.

Context variables carry pre-conversation, channel and custom data into routing rules, macros and scripts. Add one under Workstreams > (your workstream) > Advanced settings > Add context variable > Add: Name up to 100 characters, Type Text or Number, value up to 4,000 characters. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Don't rename a variable after you create it, and don't change or delete one that a classification or assignment rule uses.

Associate a Copilot Studio agent, in this order:

  1. In Copilot Studio publish the agent, then Channels > Customer engagement hub > Dynamics 365 Customer Service > Connect > View in Omnichannel. You need the OC_Admin and Agent Author roles, the agent and Customer Service in the same environment, and an agent name shorter than 30 characters. Test with the embed code of the Dynamics 365 chat widget; the Copilot Studio embed code breaks handoff.
  2. In the admin center open a push workstream > Bot area > Add bot > choose the agent in the Name list of the Add a bot dialog > Save and close. Roles: Omnichannel administrator, plus CCI Admin to open the agent in Copilot Studio.
  3. To let the agent read a workstream variable: Topics > Add a topic > From blank, add Variable management > Set a variable value and create a variable whose Variable name matches the workstream variable exactly. Under Reference choose Get value from this node if empty; under Usage select Global (any topic can access) and External sources can set values. Add a time-out if a work classification rule sets the value, then Save and publish.
ScenarioUse
Two chat widgets must share routingOne Messaging workstream with both channel instances
An agent must answer before representativesAdd the agent to a push workstream (Bot > Add bot)
A web page or agent value must drive routingWorkstream context variable plus a same-named Copilot Studio global variable
Exam traps
  • Agents receive conversations only in push workstreams, one agent per workstream; Microsoft recommends no agents on record-routing workstreams. The mode is fixed at creation, so a pick workstream with an agent needs a new push workstream.
  • AccountType is not accounttype, and the only types are Text and Number.
  • Agents created in the admin center work with enhanced voice workstreams only; classic agents aren't supported there.

Configure work classification rules

Classification is optional: it adds detail (attributes, skills, a capacity profile) to the work item before a queue is chosen. You need the CSR Manager or Omnichannel administrator role. Path: workstream > Routing rules > Work classification (optional) > Create Ruleset > Create new; pick the Rule type (Logical rules or Machine learning model); start from a Template ruleset (linked; its rules can't be edited in the workstream), Copy from template (an editable copy) or New ruleset; then Create Rule > Conditions > Output.

LimitValue
Rulesets per workstream / rule items per ruleset10 / 100
Output attributes per rule itemUp to 5
Condition depth on related recordsUp to 2 levels
Route-to-queue rulesets per workstream1

Evaluation. Classification rulesets run first, in listed order. Inside a ruleset the first rule item whose conditions match runs its output, then evaluation moves to the next ruleset. A value set earlier (Priority = High) can be a condition later (Severity = Critical). The route-to-queue ruleset runs last and evaluates all of its rule items.

  • Skill attachment rules are logical rules: Conditions > Add row > Skills, Output = skills. The rating model chosen for the skill must equal the one on the representative's skill, and one skill must never use two rating models. Re-routing appends skills. Capacity-profile rules use Output = Capacity profile. ML rules use a published intelligent skill finder model; sentiment-based rulesets are marked preview.
  • Template rulesets (Routing > Templates > Template ruleset; types Assignment, Prioritization, Work Classification) must be published and can be assigned to at most 10 workstreams or queues (5 if they use context variables). Template context variables get the _template suffix.
  • Route-to-queue rules pick the queue; no rule or no match sends the item to the fallback queue. Hit-all (default) evaluates every rule plus queue overflow; if several rules match and no queue overflows, the first rule's queue wins. Hit-first stops at the first match and ignores overflow. Percentage allocation (Add queue + Work allocation percentage) takes up to five queues that must total 100.
NeedUse
Add priority, skills or a capacity profileWork classification ruleset
Choose the queue, or split work across vendorsRoute-to-queue ruleset (percentage allocation)
Choose the representativeAssignment method of the queue

Configure the engagement agent

The product articles on workstreams and agents don't use the term "engagement agent". The Learn training module for this exam uses it for a Copilot Studio agent associated with a workstream that handles self-service (answers questions, collects context, tries to resolve) before a representative joins. Documentation calls it a Copilot agent or AI agent; Contact Center also ships pre-built agents such as Customer Assist Agent, listed with Quality Assurance Agent and Service Operations Agent under Contact Center Agents. The setup is optional but valuable: it deflects routine inquiries without using representative capacity, gathers context before handoff and feeds context variables to classification.

  1. In Copilot Studio connect the agent to Dynamics 365 Customer Service, define an escalation topic that hands off to a representative, and publish. The decision to escalate lives in the agent, not in the admin center.
  2. Add the agent to a push workstream (Bot > Add bot > Save and close). One workstream takes one agent; one agent can serve several workstreams.
  3. Make the agent update the context variables before it escalates so that classification and route-to-queue rules can match.
Best practiceReason
Put the greeting agent on the workstream, not the queueThe routing engine isn't engaged, so the agent engages faster
In a queue shared with representatives give the agent higher capacity than every representativeAn agent's capacity isn't reduced by assignments, so it picks up first
Add agents to queues manuallyUnlike representatives they aren't in a default queue
Add a representative to the queue that has the agent onlyAn escalation that returns to the same queue is not given back to the same agent; this prevents an endless loop
  • The representative sees the full agent transcript. Message size is limited to 28 KB in all messaging channels.
  • An unescalated agent conversation closes when the customer abandons it and after 30 minutes of inactivity. Voice does not listen for closeOmnichannelConversation; end the call with an explicit end-of-conversation message.
  • Sources differ on sequence: the workstreams article says classification rules run and the item is then routed to the agent, while the training module has the agent first and classification after escalation, and says an unavailable or failing agent is skipped. Remember the principle (rules need the agent's variables), not a fixed order.
Exam traps
  • Classification is optional and its first-match rule applies per ruleset; route-to-queue is the stage that evaluates every rule item.
  • A skill attached with the wrong rating model breaks assignment even though the rule matched.
  • The agent belongs on the workstream; adding it only to a queue engages routing first and is slower.
  • The escalation topic is built in Copilot Studio. A conversation that escalates back into the same queue isn't given to the same agent again; the documented fix is a representative in the agent-only queue.

Configure skills-based routing

Skill-based routing is enabled by default. The documented setup has seven steps, and the order is testable: (1) create a rating model; (2) create skill types and skills; (3) assign representatives to skills; (4) set exact or closest match as the workstream default; (5) choose a skill-classification method (logical rules, or an intelligent skill finder model plus ML rules); (6) choose an out-of-the-box or custom assignment method on the queue; (7) enable skill control for the representative.

  • Rating model: Operations > Insights > Skill-based routing > Manage > Rating Model > New Rating Model. Recommended range: minimum 1, maximum 10. Mixed rating models are normalised, but one model across all skills is recommended.
  • Skill types are the option set Bookable Resource Characteristic Type (Settings > Advanced Settings > Customizations > Customize the system > Option Sets), for example Language, and must exist before a skill such as Spanish. Skills hub: Customer support > User management > Skills hub > Manage shows skills, skill types, proficiency scales (positive minimum and maximum values, level names) and skill finder models. Only the classic experience needs representatives to be bookable resources.
  • Enable update skill control: User management > Skill-based routing > Manage > Skill based routing tab > Enable update skill control = Yes. The control is available for messaging by default; for records add it to the form. Skills that representatives correct also feed model retraining.
Default skill matching algorithmBehaviour
Exact MatchKeeps representatives whose rating is greater than or equal to the required value, then orders them by the queue's method (highest capacity, round robin or most idle). If nobody qualifies the work remains unassigned in the queue.
Closest MatchOrders everyone by closeness: exact-qualified first, then over-qualified, then under-qualified. If nobody has any required skill the conversation might go to a representative without them. Use it when speed matters more than fit.

The list also offers None. Whichever you pick, the workstream setting works only with out-of-the-box assignment methods (Highest capacity, Advanced round robin, Least active). A queue with a custom assignment method ignores it: write the conditions yourself, for example User skills > Exact match > All skills (or one skill type) with an Order by such as Nearest proficiency, Most proficient, Skill count, Round robin or Capacity. Closest match in a custom method is an order-by: Proficiency > Nearest Proficient. Least active exists for voice and messaging queues only and is the default for a new voice or messaging queue.

Exam traps
  • Picking Exact or Closest on the workstream does nothing until skill attachment rules (or an intelligent skill finder model) put skills on the work item.
  • A custom assignment method overrides the workstream algorithm; the setting is not a global switch.
  • Exact Match waits; Closest Match may hand work to someone who lacks every required skill.
  • Use the same rating model on the rule and on the representative's skill, or assignment won't behave as expected.

Configure AI-enabled skills-based routing

The intelligent skill finder (ISF) predicts the skills a new work item needs, so you don't write declarative skill rules. It depends on a custom AI Builder category classification model trained on Dataverse data. AI Builder must be available in your region, and the article lists enabling AI Builder preview models as a prerequisite.

  1. Operations > Insights > Intelligent skill finder > Manage > New. Enter a name on the Configuration tab and set Data criteria: Attributes (required), optional Filters and Date range. Attribute values are merged in the order you add them into the training string.
  2. Save, then Load training data; review and edit the tags.
  3. Select Input data and Approve. At least 50 approved records are required to train.
  4. Train model and confirm; when the status shows training completed, select the rows and Publish model.
  5. In the workstream: Work classification > Create Ruleset > Rule type: Machine learning model > Select skill identification model, then Add attribute under Input attributes (Attributes or Related Entities). Skill is the fixed output and can't be edited or deleted.
SituationUse
Plenty of labelled history in DataverseTrain the ISF model from Load training data
New organisation or no skill dataImport Excel on the Training data tab
Fixed rule such as "Platinum customers need the Premium skill"Logical skill attachment rule
Accuracy has driftedRetrain with skills that representatives updated (Enable update skill control)
  • Excel import: upload msdyn_ocsitrainingdata.csv first and msdyn_ocsitdskill.csv second, one file at a time, in the sample format. The model name must match the Training record column, each input string must be 5,000 characters or fewer, and duplicates aren't allowed.
  • Test: Power Apps > AI models > your model > Quick test; detailed metrics come from the vertical ellipsis, and predicted tags appear under Suggested tags and confidence.
  • Models move only between environments of the same type: a model trained in test works in another test environment, not in production.
Exam traps
  • You can't train below 50 approved records, and approving comes before training and publishing.
  • The CSV order matters: training data first, skill mapping second.
  • ISF is a classification rule type (Machine learning model), not an assignment method.
  • The article carries no Preview tag, but it requires AI Builder preview models to be enabled and AI Builder to be available in your region.

Configure intent-based routing

Preview The current article is titled Configure intent-driven routing (preview). It is prerelease documentation, a "production-ready preview" under supplemental terms of use, and it says intent-driven routing replaces the intent-based routing experience; intent group to user group mappings no longer apply. The exam still says "intent-based routing". Intent is now a native routing attribute: use Intent, Intent group and Line of business as conditions in classification and route-to-queue rules, and skill-based assignment then picks the representative. The preview supports live chat, voice and case (a case's intent is determined when it is routed).

PrerequisiteDetail
Customer Intent Agent onCustomer support > Intent > Turn on Customer Intent Agent; needs a pay-as-you-go plan plus the Intent Manager and CSR Manager roles
Intent discovery set upThe first run analyses up to two months of history, then it runs daily
Live chatCopilot agent in the messaging workstream with intent-based suggestions configured
VoiceVoice agent in the voice workstream
  1. The Copilot agent in the workstream detects the intent, asks follow-up questions and, on escalation, persists the intent fields to the work item. Unified routing does not determine intent for live chat or voice.
  2. A classification rule reads the fields and attaches skills, priority or other attributes (intent cancel-order attaches the cancellations skill).
  3. A route-to-queue rule uses the same fields (Line of business Billing plus Intent group Refund requests goes to Billing Tier 2); the skill engine then assigns the best qualified representative. Existing queues, skills, capacity profiles and assignment strategies keep working.

Lines of business partition intents and intent groups. Add them (Intent > Manage for Add Line of business (Optional)) only if the feature should apply to selected workstreams and queues; without them it applies to the whole organisation. You can create one case rule and one conversation rule per line of business, and chat rules should name the workstream.

Exam traps
  • Intent-driven routing is Preview, and the old intent-to-user-group mapping is obsolete.
  • Intent rules depend on three prerequisites: the Customer Intent Agent turned on, intent discovery set up, and the Copilot or voice agent added to the workstream.
  • Intent is a routing attribute, not a replacement for skills: assignment still uses skills and the queue strategy.

Configure preferred representative routing

Preferred representative routing sends work from a specific contact to that customer's preferred representatives or relationship manager. The article is now titled "Configure routing to preferred or previously engaged representatives". Roles: CSR Manager (Customer Service) or Omnichannel Administrator (Contact Center) with access to the Contact table; a custom role also needs the msdyn_preferredagent and msdyn_preferredagentcustomeridentity tables. Representatives mapped to a contact must be members of the queue that the work is routed to.

  1. Admin center > Routing > Manage next to Preferred representative routing.
  2. Turn on Enable preferred representative routing.
  3. Choose who gets the item when the preferred representative is unavailable: Next best representative based on assignment logic (use for live chat and voice) or No one. Let the work remain unassigned in the queue (use for asynchronous channels).
  4. In the Preferred representatives matrix: Add a contact > Select a contact > Add user; reorder with Move up and Move down; Save and close.
RuleDetail
Who can have preferred representativesContacts only; 1 to 3 representatives per contact, tried in the listed order
What is checkedAn available representative whose presence matches an allowed presence of the workstream. Capacity, skills and assignment rules are skipped
Where it worksPush-based workstreams only
Contact with no preferred representativeAlways routed by the queue's normal assignment method, whatever fallback you chose

How the contact is identified: case → Customer field; email, phone, fax, letter and appointment → Regarding field; chat → authenticated users automatically, unauthenticated users through a pre-conversation question named Name; voice → authenticated by phone number; other channels → social profiles. A section on assigning to a previously engaged or preferred expert with conversation orchestration playbooks is marked Preview (prerelease documentation).

Exam traps
  • A full or unskilled preferred representative still gets the item if the presence is allowed: capacity and skills are not checked.
  • Accounts can't have preferred representatives, a contact can have at most three, and every representative must be in the queue.
  • Pick workstreams don't use the feature. For asynchronous channels choose No one: the item stays in the queue until a representative picks it up or you assign it manually.

Configure routing for records

Unified routing can route cases, emails, activities and custom tables. Prerequisites: unified routing enabled (Routing > Manage unified routing > Manage > Unified routing = Yes > Save; it is off by default when only Customer Service is installed, and enabling it imports a solution, so test in a development environment first); the table enabled for queues; the System Administrator role; users set up as bookable resources.

  1. Enable the table for queues: Power Apps > Tables > table > Properties > Advanced options > Can be added to a queue. It can't be disabled afterwards. Clear When the rows are created or assigned, move them to the owner's default queue, or records aren't distributed automatically.
  2. Admin center > Customer support > Routing > Manage for Record routing > Add > Add a record type dialog > pick the type > Add.
  3. Create a Record workstream (Name, Work distribution mode, Type = Record, Record type).
  4. Create intake rules: workstream > Intake rules > Create rule. Conditions reach two levels of related records; map the rule to a workstream or to an active basic routing rule; reorder in the Decision list (See more).
  5. Add work classification and route-to-queue rules, then set Capacity, Allowed presences and the default skill matching algorithm (Exact Match or Closest Match for records).

Trigger routing. For a case the Route Case field decides: it defaults to No for cases created in the user interface (routing isn't triggered) and to Yes for cases created programmatically. For other records build a Power Automate flow: Dataverse trigger When a row is added, modified or deleted (Change type Create, a table such as Email Messages, Scope Organization), then Perform an unbound action with the action name msdyn_ApplyRoutingRuleEntityRecord and Target emails(<id>).

Symptom or needCause or use
Cases stopped routing after unified routing was enabledThe active basic routing rule doesn't route records until intake rules exist
A custom table must be routedCan be added to a queue → Record routing > Add → Record workstream → intake rule → flow action
Keep a basic rule set for some casesIntake rule mapped to the active basic routing rule
Assignment stops and the conversation is closedThe representative lacks permission on the work item
Exam traps
  • Intake rules choose the workstream (or a basic rule set); they are not routing rules, and the queue is still chosen by route-to-queue rules.
  • Can be added to a queue can't be turned off again, and the owner's-default-queue option blocks automatic distribution.
  • Don't add agents to record workstreams; record notifications appear only in Copilot Service workspace.

Configure basic routing rule sets

Basic routing rule sets route cases to a queue, user or team. Microsoft recommends unified routing for automatic record routing; basic rule sets suit simple case routing that needs no skills, capacity or multichannel logic. You need the Customer Service Manager, System Administrator or System Customizer role (or equivalent).

  1. Admin center > Routing > Manage for Basic routing rule sets > New.
  2. On the General tab enter Name and Description, then Save, which reveals the Rule Items section.
  3. New Rule Item: name it, define Rule Criteria (Add Row, Add Group, Add related entity) and under Action > Route to pick a queue or a user/team; Save & Close.
  4. Order the rule items, then Activate the rule set.
  • Evaluation: rule items run top to bottom; the first one that is true routes the case and stops evaluation, otherwise the next item is tried.
  • Without unified routing only one rule set can be active: activating another deactivates the current one. Deactivate a rule set before you edit it.
  • Apply: Save & Route when you create a case, or in Customer Service Hub select cases in My Active Cases > Apply Routing Rule. To skip routing during a bulk import add a Route Case column with the value No; programmatically set RouteCase to No.
  • Criteria limits (Unified Interface): no time value for Date and Time, one level of related entity, no related entity inside an and/or group, no multi-select option sets, no in or not in on text and no not-on on dates, lookups only equal, not equal, null and not null, no One-to-Many or Many-to-Many.
  • ALM: rule sets are solution-aware, but the queues, users and teams they point to are not, so re-map each rule item after an import; deactivate and remove the active layer before an import or upgrade. In a custom app add the Routing Rule Sets entity as a site map subarea.
SituationUse
Simple, case-only routing without skillsBasic routing rule set
Skills, capacity, classification or several channelsUnified routing with a Record workstream
Unified routing on, but some cases keep a basic rule setIntake rule mapped to the active basic routing rule
Exam traps
  • The first rule item that is true wins; item order is the whole design.
  • Activating a second rule set silently deactivates the first (unified routing off).
  • Queues, users and teams aren't solution-aware, so a rule set imported to production still points nowhere until you re-map it.

Diagnose unified routing by using conversation diagnostics

Deprecated The older Routing > Routing diagnostics page (Turn on routing diagnostics, data stored in Dataverse) is marked deprecated as of May 9, 2024; the Deprecations article lists removal on March 31, 2026 and recommends conversation diagnostics in Azure Application Insights. Conversation diagnostics logs each conversation lifecycle event, and the data appears in Application Insights within 15 minutes of routing.

PrerequisiteDetail
AzureContributor or higher to set it up; at least Read to query Application Insights
Power PlatformPower Platform administrator or System Administrator for tasks such as exporting data
EnvironmentA Managed environment; no export in GCC, GCC High or DoD
  1. Provision an Application Insights resource in Azure and copy the App ID from JSON View.
  2. Admin center > Operations > Insights > Observability settings > Conversation lifecycle diagnostics > Manage. Tick the two confirmation boxes, enter the Application Insights ID, select Provision and copy the 3P Application Name. The guided setup creates the app and a federated identity credential and sets an environment variable.
  3. In Azure open that app > API permissions: the Application Insights Read permission must show Granted; otherwise select Grant admin consent.
  4. On the Application Insights resource open Access control (IAM) and assign the Monitoring Reader role to the app.
  5. Back in the admin center select Test connection.

Use it. In Copilot Service workspace open Conversations, select a conversation and choose Diagnose on the command bar. The new tab shows channel, queue, distribution mode and events; select a Classification or Route to queue event to see the applied condition, the condition that wasn't evaluated, the final output and the assignment details. For a case use Cases > Diagnose: each routing attempt creates its own conversation, and the intake rules of that attempt can be reviewed.

QuestionLook at the subscenario
Why this queue, or why the fallback queue?RouteToQueue, Classification (and Intake for records)
Why unassigned, or why this representative?Assignment snapshot: CSRConfiguration, QueueConfiguration, AssignmentRuleset, CSRStatusandCapacityDetails, plus CSRAssignment
Who rejected or ignored it?CSRRejected, CSRNotificationTimeout, ConversationAutoRejected
Did an agent handle it first?CopilotAgentAssignedToConversation, CopilotAgentEscalationToCSR

For bulk analysis query the Traces table in Application Insights Logs. The documented fallback-queue sample, shortened:

Traces
| extend customDim = parse_json(customDimensions)
| extend scenario = tostring(customDim["powerplatform.analytics.scenario"]),
         subscenario = tostring(customDim["powerplatform.analytics.subscenario"]),
         conversationId = tostring(customDim["powerplatform.analytics.resource.id"]),
         queueResult = parse_json(tostring(customDim["omnichannel.result"])).DisplayName
| where scenario == "ConversationDiagnosticsScenario"
| where subscenario == "RouteToQueue" and queueResult == "Fallback queue name"
| project timestamp, conversationId, queueResult
Exam traps
  • Routing diagnostics (Routing > Routing diagnostics) is the deprecated feature; Diagnose in Copilot Service workspace backed by Application Insights is the current one.
  • Monitoring Reader goes to the 3P app; Contributor or higher is what you need in Azure to run the setup.
  • The environment must be Managed, and sovereign clouds can't export the data.
  • No data right after a test chat is normal: allow up to 15 minutes.

sections.title: 5.1 Configure experience profiles
sections.html:
Skills measured: create experience profiles • application tab templates • agent inbox and custom views • session templates • notification templates. Practise: build a custom profile with an inbox view, a session template that opens an extra tab and a notification template with one added field, then assign the profile by security role.

Create experience profiles

An experience profile gives representatives and supervisors a targeted Copilot Service workspace: specific session templates, channels, productivity tools and the inbox. A representative without a custom profile gets the default profile. The out-of-the-box profiles, such as Omnichannel for Customer Service - default profile, Customer Service workspace - default profile and Customer Service workspace + channels - default profile, can't be deleted or modified, can't be set as default and can't get roles or a rank.

Roles. Creating profiles needs the App Profile Manager Administrator role plus the Basic User role. Out of the box, Customer Service Representative and CSR Manager carry the App Profile User privileges; in Contact Center the Omnichannel administrator carries the App Profile Manager Administrator privileges and the Omnichannel agent and supervisor roles carry App Profile User. Give the Administrator role manually to whoever builds profiles, templates, productivity tools and channel providers.

  1. Admin center > Support experience > Workspaces > Experience profiles > New: Name, Unique name (format <prefix>_<name>) and Description > Create.
  2. Open the profile and configure it: Users > Add Users; Add entity session template; Productivity pane On (default mode expanded or collapsed, plus toggles for Copilot, Knowledge search, Agent scripts, Join a Teams call, Teams chats, Smart assist, Case handling time, Screen Recording and Timeout Rules); Inbox > Edit; Channel providers > Edit (the All active channels toggle and third-party voice providers).
  3. Decide how users receive the profile (table below). Copilot features are available in the out-of-the-box profiles by default; enable them in a custom profile.
Assignment method (shown by Search by user)How it is set
DefaultThe out-of-the-box profile, or the single custom profile marked Set as default. It doesn't apply to users who have a specific profile. Only one default exists: use Remove Default before choosing another. Setting a default removes its roles.
Role-basedSet rank and roles maps security roles to the profile. A user with several roles gets the profile with the higher rank (rank 1 beats rank 2 in the documented example). Team membership isn't used.
DirectUsers > Add Users on the profile

Profiles can be added to solutions and imported; profiles that come from a managed solution show a lock icon and can't be edited. The admin center refuses two profiles with the same rank and two defaults, but an import from different environments can create them; resolve the conflict in the source environments.

Exam traps
  • You can't edit the out-of-the-box profile to add a tool: create a custom profile.
  • Assigning by team doesn't work; use security roles with a rank, or add users directly.
  • The default profile never overrides a profile that was assigned by role or directly.
  • Creating profiles needs two roles: App Profile Manager Administrator and Basic User.

Configure application tab templates

An application tab template defines which application a tab opens in a Copilot Service workspace session. Every session has at least one anchor tab that can't be closed or customized, and the Home session can't be closed or customized. Out-of-the-box templates can't be customized. The article applies to Customer Service and Contact Center standalone only, and you need the System Administrator role.

  1. Admin center > Support experience > Workspaces > Manage for Application tab templates > New.
  2. General tab: Name (not shown to representatives), Unique name (<prefix>_<name>; prefix alphanumeric, 3 to 8 characters, underscore required; the light bulb > Apply validates it), Title (shown to representatives), Page type, Description > Save.
  3. Enter the Value of each parameter the page type shows, then Save. After you edit the template, save again so the Parameters section refreshes.
  4. Add the template to a session template as the anchor tab or an additional tab.
Page typeKey parameters
DashboarddashboardId (required)
Entity listentityName (required), viewId
Entity recordentityName (required), entityId, formId, validateRecord; in create mode also data (JSON prefill)
SearchsearchText (required), searchType (0 relevance, 1 categorized)
Third-party websiteurl (required, https), data; the site must allow iframe hosting
Web resourcewebresourceName (required), data
Customname of the custom page (required), entityName, recordId
ControlFor internal use only

Slugs and OData fill parameters at runtime from the anchor record: {anchor.<attribute>} such as {anchor.incidentid} or {anchor._customerid_value}, and {$odata.<entity>.<attribute>.?<query>}. For the Entity record type, an entityId that matches no record opens the form in create mode; set validateRecord to true to open the form only for an existing record (if the parameter is missing, add it with the unique name new_tabtemplateparam_validateRecord).

Exam traps
  • A third-party tab that says the site "refused to connect" points to a site that doesn't allow iframe hosting; it isn't a template error.
  • Control is internal; custom pages use the Custom type, files and HTML use Web resource.
  • The Name is hidden from representatives; the Title is what they see.
  • An application tab template does nothing until a session template uses it.

Configure the agent inbox, including creating custom views

The inbox (the article is titled "Configure the inbox") shows each representative's assigned cases, conversations and records in one place. It supports live chat, asynchronous chat (SMS, persistent chat, Facebook, WeChat, LINE, WhatsApp, Teams), case, email, task, voice (voicemail) and records routed by unified routing. The inbox can be configured for custom experience profiles only, and channel providers must have All active channels set to On to use and configure the chat setting.

  1. Admin center > Support experience > Workspaces > Experience profiles > Manage > open the custom profile.
  2. On the Inbox card turn the inbox on (Settings icon > Inbox toggle, or Enable Inbox on the Inbox page) and select Edit.
  3. Select + Add to open Add a new view: Name, Representative visibility (Show or Hide the view from representatives) and Record type. Several record types make a multi-entity view of cases, chats, emails and voicemails together.
  4. For each record type choose Simple (ready-made filters) or Advanced (the condition builder), then Save.
Record typeSimple settings
EmailSent to me • assigned to me • in my team(s) • in my queue(s) • in a shared mailbox
Chat and VoicemailAssigned • Unassigned • Resolved
CaseAssigned to me • in my team(s) • in my queue(s)
Unified routing enabled recordsAssigned • Open • Closed (open and save a migrated view again to get read/unread support)
  • Out-of-the-box views: Cases, Assigned Conversations, Resolved Conversations, Unassigned Conversations. Views refresh automatically every five minutes, and representatives can refresh manually.
  • Custom sort: profile > Inbox > Edit > Edit view pane > Sort (entity, attributes, order). Your own entity: Inbox settings > Inbox record types > +Add. Custom card: Inbox record types > select an attribute > rearrange or add with + > Save and close.
  • Channel-focused inbox: Edit inbox > Incoming work items tab. Choose Add to inbox if customer service representative is currently in inbox; otherwise open in a new session tab, Add to inbox, or Open in a new session tab, then Save and close and clear the cache or refresh. It applies to all users and profiles in the organisation and to every conversation type except voice, which always opens in a new session with a card added to the inbox.
  • The Deprecations article lists the Omnichannel agent and supervisor dashboard experiences in Copilot Service workspace for deprecation on December 1, 2025, with support ending December 1, 2026, and recommends the inbox plus the Omnichannel real-time analytics report.
Exam traps
  • There is no inbox setting for the out-of-the-box profiles; create a custom profile first.
  • Hide in Representative visibility removes the view from representatives; it doesn't merge views.
  • A multi-entity view comes from several Record type values in one view, not from several views.
  • Voice never follows the channel-focused inbox option; it always opens a new session.

Configure session templates

A session starts when a representative accepts a conversation or opens a record. A session template defines the application that opens as the anchor tab (can't be closed), the additional application tabs, and the default mode of the communication panel; scripts can be attached. Out-of-the-box templates can't be customized: Case entity session - default template is the out-of-the-box template for Copilot Service workspace, and generic ones cover Chat, Voice call, Custom messaging, Entity records, Facebook, LINE, SMS, Teams, Twitter, WeChat and WhatsApp. Channel Integration Framework must be enabled to load generic templates with the createSession API.

  1. Create the application tab templates you want to use.
  2. Admin center > Support experience > Workspaces > Manage for Session templates > New, complete the General tab (table below) and Save.
  3. Additional Tab > Add Existing Application Tab Template > search > Add. Representatives can't close these tabs.
  4. Scripts tab: scripts must already be configured; set Enable build expression to Yes and build an expression that makes a script the default for this template. Save.
  5. Associate it: workstream > Advanced settings > Sessions > Edit > Default template, or on an experience profile with Add entity session template.
FieldWhat to know
Unique Name<prefix>_<name>; prefix alphanumeric, 3 to 8 characters, underscore required
TypeEntity (then pick an entity; the list shows user-owned entities only) or Generic (assignable to any channel)
TitleShown to representatives; supports slugs such as {customerName}
Communication panel modeDocked (expanded), Minimized or Hidden; for entity routing (case) sessions the panel is hidden
Session IconGeneric type only; a deployed web resource, no slugs, no GIF files
Anchor tabShown only when Type is Generic; opens by default and can't be closed
Exam traps
  • The Anchor tab field and the Session Icon exist only for the Generic type.
  • A session template that isn't associated with a workstream (or profile) is never used.
  • Session templates and experience profiles are different objects: a profile only links entity session templates.
  • The Name is internal; representatives see the Title.

Configure notification template

A notification alerts a representative or supervisor to an incoming conversation, escalation, transfer or consult, showing the customer, a countdown and the Accept and Reject buttons. A notification template defines what is displayed. Out-of-the-box templates can't be customized (for example Chat - incoming authenticated - default; each channel has consult, authenticated, unauthenticated and transfer variants). The authenticated template is used when the customer's record exists in Dynamics 365; otherwise the unauthenticated template applies.

  1. Admin center > Support experience > Workspaces > Manage for Notifications > Templates tab > New Notification Template; complete the General tab and Save.
  2. In Notification Fields select Add Existing Notification Field > New: Name (internal), Field header (what representatives read) and Value (a slug such as {customerName}). Return to the template, Add the field and Save; repeat for more fields.
  3. Associate the template: workstream > Advanced settings > Customer service representative notifications > Edit and choose a template for each type: Incoming unauthenticated, Incoming authenticated, Consult, Transfer, Supervisor assign, Returning Conversation (persistent chat workstreams only).
SettingWhat to know
Title / IconTitle is shown to representatives; Icon is a web resource path (an SVG icon isn't shown in desktop notifications)
Show CountdownShows or hides the timer; the timer runs and the notification disappears at the timeout either way
Countdown (seconds)Default 120; below 5 seconds no desktop notification appears
Autoassign work items PreviewDefault No. When Yes, Accept becomes Open and the Reject button is disabled
Autoaccept voice/chat calls PreviewShown only when autoassign is on; default No
Show desktop notificationsAlways Preview or When app is in background; default Never
  • Slugs use curly braces. Built in: {customerName}, {caseId}, {caseTitle}, {queueId}, {visitorLanguage}, {visitorDevice}, {entityRoutingLogicalName}, {customerEntityName} and {customerRecordId}; these nine names are reserved, so don't reuse them for custom context variables. Also valid: {msdyn_WorkstreamId}, any pre-chat question name and any workstream context variable. Macros and scripts use ${customerName} instead.
  • For record routing don't offer a reject option: the record is assigned to the routed representative anyway.
  • Desktop notifications need browser permission (Edge or Chrome) and don't work in incognito mode, with Windows focus assist on, or in legacy Microsoft Edge; also enable Windows and site notifications and the service worker.
Exam traps
  • Templates use {slug}; ${slug} is the macro and script syntax.
  • Creating the template is under Workspaces > Notifications; the workstream only selects a template per notification type.
  • The countdown is in seconds; with fewer than 5 the desktop alert doesn't show.
  • The notification-templates article marks autoassign and autoaccept as in preview, but the dedicated automatic-assignment article has no Preview label, so Microsoft's pages disagree; the Reject button disappears when autoassign is on.

sections.title: 5.2 Configure productivity tools
sections.html:
Skills measured: enable custom productivity panels • configure scripts, including slugs • create macros • enable Teams collaboration • extend the productivity panel by using the app profile manager JavaScript API reference • extend the customer service representative experience by using the Omnichannel JavaScript API. Practise: in a test environment build a script with a default-script expression, a macro that creates a case and links it to a chat, and a custom pane tool, then call the Microsoft.Apm and Microsoft.Omnichannel methods from a custom page.

Enable custom productivity panels

The productivity pane of Copilot Service workspace holds macros, scripts, smart assist, Teams and custom productivity tools. A custom tool is a Power Apps custom page or a Power Apps component framework (PCF) control. You can create several and switch each one on per experience profile (§5.1). The articles apply to Customer Service and Contact Center standalone only; the pane isn't available in Omnichannel for Customer Service on Unified Service Desk.

Roles. The administrator needs Productivity tools administrator; representatives and supervisors need Productivity tools user. The custom page or PCF control must already be built.

  1. Copilot Service admin center > Support experience > Productivity > Manage for Productivity tools > New (New Pane tool configuration).
  2. Enter Name, Unique Name, Type (Control and then Control Name, or Custom Page and then Custom Page Name), an optional Icon (a web resource), Global = Yes (the tool is available across sessions, including the home session), and optionally Description and Learn More Link. Save.
  3. Support experience > Workspaces > Manage for Experience profiles > open the profile > Edit for Productivity pane > enable the custom tool > save.
ScenarioUse
Only the Tier 2 team should see the toolCreate the pane tool once; enable it only in the Tier 2 experience profile.
Tool must be available in every session, including homeGlobal = Yes on the pane tool configuration.
Tool needs the open case or customerPlan for it: hosted tools aren't contextually bound to the session and have no mechanism to read the session context.
A custom security role can't open the paneGrant Read on App profile, Application tab template, Notification field, Notification template, Pane tab configuration, Pane tool configuration and Productivity pane configuration.
Exam traps
  • You create the tool under Productivity, but you make it available to users under Workspaces > Experience profiles > Productivity pane.
  • Productivity tools administrator builds tools, Productivity tools user uses them. Don't swap the roles.
  • Type decides which name field you fill: Control Name for a PCF control, Custom Page Name for a custom page.

Configure scripts, including slugs

Scripts give representatives step-by-step, company-approved guidance during a session. The same two roles apply: Productivity tools administrator builds, Productivity tools user uses.

  1. Support experience > Productivity > Manage for Scripts > New: Name, Unique Name (<prefix>_<name>; prefix alphanumeric, 3 to 8 characters, underscore required), Language (only languages enabled in Dataverse appear), Description > Save.
  2. Script steps > New Script step (quick create): Name (shown to the representative; slugs allowed), Unique Name, Owner, Script, Order, Action Type and the field that matches it > Save and Close > Save.
  3. Support experience > Workspaces > Session templates > open the template (for example Chat - Default Session) > Scripts tab > Add Existing script > select > Add > Save. The script now loads for sessions of that type, and representatives can switch among the scripts available.
Action TypeField that appearsWhat the step is
Text instructionText instruction (text; slugs and OData queries allowed)Guidance the representative reads and performs
MacroTarget macro (lookup)A step tied to an existing macro
ScriptTarget script (lookup)A step tied to another script

Default script by condition

On the same Scripts tab of the session template set Enable build expression to Yes and select Build Expression. In the Expression builder select the Condition step and build the condition; under If true choose Add an action > Customer Service tab > Set default script > pick the script; repeat for If false; Save and close. When a representative accepts a conversation, the script control shows the matching default. Conditions use automation-dictionary slugs.

Slugs

A slug is a replacement parameter the system fills at run time from context (channel provider, user actions, Dataverse). The format depends on where you type it:

WhereFormatExample
Templates: session title, notification title and fields, application tab template parameters{slug}{caseId}
Macros, scripts and the default-script expression${slug}${customerName}
Session connector actions${$session.<slug>}${$session.visitorDevice}
Omnichannel connector actions${$oc.<slug>}${$oc.customerName}
OData query (a Dataverse value){$odata.<entityName>.<entityAttributeName>.<?options>}; the macro examples prefix it with $${$odata.contact.emailaddress1.?$filter=contactid eq '{anchor._customerid_value}'}
  • Macro and script slugs: ${customerName}, ${caseId}, ${caseTitle}, ${LiveWorkItemId}, ${queueId}, ${visitorLanguage}, ${visitorDevice}, ${entityRoutingLogicalName}, ${customerEntityName}, ${customerRecordId}, plus one slug per pre-conversation survey question, named after the question.
  • For data from the anchor record in Copilot Service workspace only ${anchor.<attribute_name>} is supported, for example ${anchor.ticketnumber}. Session.CurrentTab and Session.AnchorTab parameters (EntityName, EntityId) work in macros only.
  • Session context: a case session fills from the anchor tab record; a conversation session from the channel provider; records in additional tabs aren't in the context. Static text can be mixed with slugs.
  • The reconnect link slug {ReconnectUrl{ReconnectID}} is used in quick replies.
Exam traps
  • Templates use {slug}; macros and scripts use ${slug}. A few doc examples (a macro static value, a script step name) are written with single braces, so rely on the format rule from the automation dictionary article.
  • A script loads for representatives only after it is associated with a session template on the Scripts tab.
  • The default script is set by Enable build expression on the session template, not on the workstream or the experience profile.
  • Target macro and Target script appear only for the matching Action Type.

Create macros

A macro is a set of sequential actions that runs on demand and can be reused across sessions through session-context slugs. Design needs Productivity tools administrator or System Administrator; running needs Productivity tools user or Customer Service representative.

  1. Support experience > Productivity > Manage for Macros > New.
  2. Enter a name and description, then always begin with the Start macro execution step.
  3. Add actions from the four connectors below.

Triggers: a representative runs it from the productivity pane, code calls Microsoft.ProductivityMacros.runMacro(macroName) (returns a promise), or a script step uses the Macro action type.

ConnectorUse it for
Productivity automationModel-driven app work: open and update records, open views, resolve cases, search knowledge, clone records, set focus to another script, open email templates, autofill form fields, set and get session-context variables, and Execute JavaScript (Web Resource Name plus Custom Macro Function) to reach non-Microsoft pages
Session connectorSession and tabs: get a tab ID, refresh a tab, pass a tab ID, set focus on a tab, open a tab template, refresh session context
Omnichannel connectorLink record to the conversation, Unlink record from the conversation, Send knowledge base article link in chat
Flow connectorTrigger a Power Automate flow
  • Create a case from a conversation: Open a new form to create a record > Save the record > Link record to the conversation (Entity record ID, Entity primary name, Entity logical name). Switching conversations while it runs can give unexpected results.
  • Lookups need three separate attributes: the related record ID, the record type and the record name (for example regardingobjectid, regardingobjectidtype, regardingobjectidname).
  • Autofill form fields doesn't save to Dataverse until the form autosaves; add Save the record or Update existing record. Resolving a case by macro doesn't refresh the tab automatically; add the Session connector actions Get the current tab and Refresh the tab.
  • Send knowledge base article link in chat must follow Search knowledge base for the populated phrase, with Use an external portal set to Yes.
Exam traps
  • Every macro must begin with the Start macro execution step.
  • Linking or unlinking a record to the live chat belongs to the Omnichannel connector, not to Productivity automation (open and update records) or the Session connector (tabs).
  • A lookup needs the related record ID, type and name as three separate attributes.
  • Records in additional tabs don't feed the session context; only the anchor tab (case) or the channel provider (conversation) does.

Enable Teams collaboration

Teams collaboration in the productivity pane covers embedded Teams chat (chats connected to records), Join a Teams call and suggested contacts. It applies to Customer Service and Contact Center standalone only. Customer support swarming (preview) is documented as deprecated and no longer supported; embedded Teams chat is the recommended replacement.

  1. Teams chat is on by default in Copilot Service workspace and Customer Service Hub; other apps need manual enabling.
  2. Support experience > Collaboration > Embedded chat using Teams > Manage > turn on Turn on Microsoft Teams chats inside Dynamics 365 > Turn on for all Dynamics 365 apps (including apps added later) or Turn on for selected Dynamics 365 apps > Save.
  3. A custom model-driven app: add the settings page to its sitemap in the Power Apps app designer (subarea, Type = URL, /main.aspx?pagetype=control&controlName=MscrmControls.TeamsCollaborationAdmin.TeamsCollaborationAdmin) and publish.
  4. A custom experience profile: with the toggle set to Yes use Turn on for specific multisession users > Manage, open the profile and enable its productivity pane features. Users need permissions equal to the Productivity tools user role.
  • Microsoft Graph permissions: Chat.ReadWrite.All (chats and recent messages), Directory.Read.All (team and channel names), Presence.Read.All (presence), User.Read.All (names and licences of suggested participants), User.ReadBasic.All (photos). Dynamics 365 stores only the record ID to chat ID mapping.
  • Connected record types out of the box: case, account, contact, knowledge article, email. Add record types adds more; Include a note shows a context card from the first five fields of the chosen view (default views: Case introduction message for case, Quick find for the other standard types).
  • Disconnecting chats: the settings Record owner can disconnect chats and Chat connector can disconnect chat, or the role privilege Disconnect Teams chat from Dynamics 365 record (Business management > Miscellaneous Privileges).
  • Join a Teams call: Collaboration > Join a Teams call > Manage; on by default for Contact Center profiles in Copilot Service workspace; needs Power Platform admin center > Settings > Product > Collaboration > End users can join Teams meetings from appointments on, and outbound email to invite customers by email.

Suggested contacts. Both modes start on the Microsoft Teams collaboration and chat page with Turn on the linking of Dynamics 365 records to Microsoft Teams channels set to Yes; you then pick the record type under Connect Teams chat to Dynamics 365 records.

Suggested contactsAI-basedRules-based
Record typesCase (Customer Service) or ConversationAny record type connected to chats; most types offer only this mode (case offers both)
PrerequisitesAI suggestions for similar cases enabled; tenant permission for the enhanced Teams integrationToggle per record type
SetupSelect Case or Conversation > Suggest contacts > AI-based suggested contacts; first-time preprocessing takes 24 hoursSuggest contacts > Rules-based suggested contacts > Add new rule; reorder, disable or delete; users see suggestions in your order; 10 rules per record type
LogicSimilar cases resolved, similarity, recency, average resolution timeRelational (a user on the record or on up to 10 chained related entities) or Custom (a custom action with EntityLogicalName, Recordid, optional CustomActionInputs in and CustomActionSuggestedUsers out)

Optional on the AI page: Turn on Enhanced Microsoft Teams Integration (pin records and views to a channel) and Enable Confidential Labels.

Exam traps
  • The default profile gets Teams chat automatically; a custom profile must be enabled under Turn on for specific multisession users.
  • Two toggle labels appear in the docs for the same Microsoft Teams collaboration and chat page: one in the chat article, the other in the suggested-contacts articles.
  • AI-based contacts need AI similar-case suggestions first and 24 hours of preprocessing; rules-based is capped at 10 rules per record type.
  • Join a Teams call has a prerequisite outside the Collaboration page: the Power Platform admin center setting End users can join Teams meetings from appointments.

Extend the productivity panel by using the app profile manager JavaScript API reference

The Microsoft.Apm namespace manages sessions, tabs and session context in Copilot Service workspace. The caller needs the App Profile user or Productivity tools user role. The reference keeps the old app profile manager name; you now manage profiles as experience profiles in the admin center.

AreaMethodsProperties and events
SessionsgetFocusedSession, getAllSessions, getSession, createSession, canCreateSession, close, focus, requestFocus (notification indicator on a session not in focus)sessionId, isDefault (home session), canClose, title
TabsgetFocusedTab, getAllTabs, getTab, createTab (in the focused session), canCreateTab, closeTab, focusTab, refreshTabtabId, canClose, title
ContextupdateContext: add, change or remove slug values that macros use later 
Events ON_SESSION_SWITCH (previousSessionId, newSessionId), ON_SESSION_CLOSED
// open a case session; the caller's profile must contain this session template
var x = new Map();
x.set("parametersStr", '[["entityName","incident"],["entityId","<case-guid>"]]');
Microsoft.Apm.createSession({ templateName: "case_entity_session_default_template", sessionContext: x, isFocused: false });

// make a slug value available to macros that run later
Microsoft.Apm.getFocusedSession().updateContext({ "customerName": "Contoso" });

// listen for session switches (Broadcast Channel API, same origin)
let topic = Microsoft.Apm.getEventPublisherTopic("ON_SESSION_SWITCH");
let sub = new BroadcastChannel(topic);
sub.onmessage = (e) => console.log(e.data.previousSessionId, e.data.newSessionId);
  • createSession input: templateName (the template's unique name), sessionContext (Map<string,string>), optional isFocused and shouldRestore; it returns the session ID. The user must belong to a profile that contains the session template.
  • updateContext takes JSON, returns nothing; read values back with getContext().

Extend the customer service representative experience by using the Omnichannel JavaScript API

The Microsoft.Omnichannel namespace has six methods for the Contact Center SDK; each returns a promise.

MethodDoesRules
getConversationId()GUID of the current ongoing conversation in the session 
getConversations(input, correlationId)Lists msdyn_ocliveworkitem records for an agentInput JSON attributes, agentId, status, orderBy, createdBeforeDays; only agentId is required
openConversation(conversationId, lastsessionId, liveworkstreamId)Opens a conversation as a sessionThe last two are optional
linkToConversation(entityLogicalName, recordId, conversationId)Links an account, contact or incidentDatabase link only; the caller refreshes the UI; one customer and one case at a time, a new link overrides; active conversations only; conversationId optional (focused conversation)
unlinkFromConversation(entityLogicalName, recordId, conversationId)Unlinks a linked customer or case 
sendMessageToConversation(message, toSendBox, conversationId)Sends a string or valid rich-object JSONThe conversation must be assigned to the signed-in representative; toSendBox defaults to the send box, false sends straight to the chat
Microsoft.Omnichannel.linkToConversation("incident", "<case-guid>", "<conversation-guid>")
  .then(() => Microsoft.Apm.refreshTab("<tab-id>"), (err) => console.log(err));
NeedNamespace
Create, focus or close sessions and tabs, refresh a tab, share slug valuesMicrosoft.Apm
List, open, link, unlink or message conversationsMicrosoft.Omnichannel
Run a macro from codeMicrosoft.ProductivityMacros.runMacro(macroName)
Exam traps
  • linkToConversation only writes the link; refresh the tab yourself with Microsoft.Apm.refreshTab.
  • A conversation holds one account or contact and one case; linking another overrides the first, and closed conversations can't be linked.
  • getConversations fails without agentId; sendMessageToConversation needs a conversation assigned to the signed-in representative.
  • createSession works only if the caller's profile holds the session template; createTab acts on the focused session.
  • updateContext only sets slug values for macros invoked later.

Sources: Productivity tools · Custom productivity tools · Manage scripts · Automation dictionary · Macros · Productivity automation actions · Omnichannel actions · Teams chat · AI-suggested contacts · Rules-based contacts · Join a Teams call · App profile manager API · Omnichannel API · linkToConversation · Deprecations in Customer Service

sections.title: 5.3 Create and administer knowledge management
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure internal knowledge search capabilities • Integrate and search external knowledge sources • Configure tables for knowledge management • Configure the Customer Knowledge Management agent • Integrate knowledge into portals. Practise by turning on each toggle on the Knowledge page of Copilot Service admin center in a trial environment, adding one external and one integrated search provider, and running the Customer Knowledge Management Agent prerequisites once.

Configure internal knowledge search capabilities

Everything starts on the Knowledge page: Copilot Service admin center (CSAC) > Support experience > Knowledge. You need the System Administrator or System Customizer role (or equivalent) and must be a Microsoft 365 tenant administrator. Set KnowledgeArticle privileges alongside the Basic User role; for this table the security boundary is the environment, not the individual user.

Setting (General settings unless noted)Use it when…
Set search mode as allmulti-word searches return articles that match only one word. The default is searchMode=any; all requires Dataverse search. A concept article calls the same feature Knowledge search logic
Enable suggest as you typereps want a flyout of matching article titles (matched text highlighted) while they type
Show recently viewed knowledge articlesreps reuse articles across similar cases without searching again; choose 1 to 8 articles
Enable Kb preview mode from global search optionreps should preview an article directly from global search
Origins allowlist > Add origin linksauthors embed iframe links. An origin is protocol + domain or IP + optional port: https://www.contoso.com allows https://www.contoso.com/about but not https://contoso.com/about
Filters page: Enable search filtersresults must be limited by field value. Yes by default; Allow customer service representative to personalize lets reps save their own; per filter use the ellipsis > Preselects or Visibility
  • Filter fields must be option set, multiselect option set, lookup, two choices or date and time columns. While the CSAC filters are on, filter configurations made in Power Apps are deactivated. To filter on a custom column, add it to the Quick Find view columns. With Dataverse search, selecting the Archived, Discarded or Expired values of the Status filter returns nothing unless you delete the Archived, Discarded, Expired and Is Latest Version criteria in Quick Find Knowledge Article > Edit Filter Criteria.
  • Search engine: Dataverse search is on by default in production environments except those that use their own encryption key; otherwise knowledge search falls back to SQL Server full-text search.
  • Operators work in either mode: + AND, | OR, - NOT (before the keyword), * wildcard at the start or end of a keyword, double quotes for an exact phrase.
  • Where reps search: multi-session Copilot Service workspace uses the app side pane control (add the record type, see the tables topic; the side pane itself is set in the experience profile, §5.1). The Knowledge Search form component (Power Apps > table > Forms > + Component > Related Data > Knowledge Search) is for single-session apps or automatic search on non-anchor tabs.
  • Duplicate detection rules are not supported on the Knowledge Article table, and the embedded knowledge search control in the web client is deprecated (use the Knowledge Settings page in Unified Interface).

Integrate and search external knowledge sources

External search provider (federated)Integrated search provider (ingested)
Use forCross-Organizational Search (another organization; URL identified automatically, data crosses regions if it is in another geography), SharePoint (URL in the same Microsoft organization), Microsoft Graph connector (unique connection ID; when Microsoft Search indexes your external data)Third-party sources such as enterprise websites based on the site map protocol
ResultLinks per provider: 3 articles each plus Show more; the Search results display count no longer applies once one provider existsArticles are ingested into Dataverse on a refresh schedule and behave like internal articles (searchable, filterable)
PathKnowledge > External search providers > Manage > New > General (name, owner) > Details (Select organization, Search Type) > SaveKnowledge > Integrated search providers > Manage > Set up integrated search (first time) > New
SecurityCustom roles need Read, Create, Append and AppendTo on Knowledge Federated Article and Knowledge Federated Article Incident; in Microsoft Cloud for Sovereignty, GCC onlyProvisioning needs prvReadconnector (Basic) and, at Global level, prvReadWorkflow, prvWriteWorkflow and create, read, write and delete on msdyn_knowledgeconfiguration

Adding an integrated provider (if provisioning fails, turn on the cloud flow Integrated Search API trigger in make.powerapps.com > Solutions > Default Solution > Cloud flows):

  1. Provider info: name, description, authorization check box.
  2. Authentication and testing: Root URL, Site map URL (the site's /robots.txt shows it) and Language filter for ingestion.
  3. Knowledge article schema: Field Mapping or JSON Schema; the method cannot be changed after saving. Mandatory targets: Content, External Reference Id (unique) and Title; operation types Regex, Direct, Constant, RegexUrl.
  4. Refresh Schedule: Refresh frequency (No refresh pauses ingestion) and Lookback period; review the Summary.
  5. Save and close gives Inactive/Validated; Save as draft gives Inactive/Draft, and a draft cannot run ingestion.
  • Site map rules: every article url needs a lastmod tag; site map files are served as application/xml or text/xml; static websites only (script-rendered content is unsupported); root URL, site map URL and language filters must form a unique combination.
  • Ingestion: Trial ingestion (Inactive/Validated; No of records, maximum 1,000; check Crawl failures on the Insights tab) and then Activate; Time-range based ingestion (Active/Ingestion Ready; a range of 60 days from the From date). Deactivating stops ingestion and ingested articles leave search results; edits apply at the next ingestion.
  • Filter by source: Filters > Select filter type > Integrated Search Dataprovider Id > Add > pick the provider (needs Dataverse search; with a custom layer on the Quick Find view add msdyn_integratedsearchproviderid to View columns and Find columns). Set as preselected filter makes it a default.
  • These providers extend the representative knowledge search; Copilot's own knowledge sources are configured separately (§3.1).

Configure tables for knowledge management

Table or relationshipPurpose
KnowledgeArticleThe article (HTML content). Creating one also creates an internal root article that holds all versions and translations. New articles start in Draft as major version 1, minor 0. ArticlePublicNumber is the ID shown to customers and stays the same across versions and translations
KnowledgeArticleIncidentIntersect table that links articles to cases (Incident), which are enabled by default
msdyn_<Entity_Name>_knowledgearticleMany-to-many relationship and intersect table created automatically when you enable knowledge for another table, for example msdyn_account_knowledgearticle
LanguageLocaleLanguages for translations (more than 150); the GUIDs are identical in every organization
entityanalyticsconfigEntity Analytics Config: the docs recommend adding the mapped tables here (with Track changes on) before historical article creation
  • Lifecycle (statecode): 0 Draft, 1 Approved, 2 Scheduled, 3 Published, 4 Expired, 5 Archived, 6 Discarded. It is a lifecycle stage, not confidentiality: users with Read and Write can open drafts.
  • Versions and translations: CreateKnowledgeArticleVersion (IsMajor true or false) keeps RootArticleId and PreviousArticleContentId; CreateKnowledgeArticleTranslation copies title, content, description and keywords into a new record in the language you choose.
  • Enable another table: Knowledge > Record types > Manage > Add > Select record type > Save and Close. Then edit it to open Knowledge settings: Automatic search (Turn on automatic search, Provide search results using a field), Actions (link or unlink, copy URL, link and email URL, link and send content) and Email recipient (Customer or Lookup attribute types, Account or Contact lookups). Case is on by default; Conversation is present when add-ons such as Chat, Digital messaging or Voice are purchased.
  • Categories: Knowledge > Categories > Manage; roles Customer Service Manager, System Administrator or System Customizer; fields Title, Description, Display Order, Parent Category and Category Number (visible after the first save). Categories are hierarchical (View Hierarchy).
  • Article templates: Knowledge > Article templates > Manage opens the Article Templates System Views page, where you create templates that give authors consistent language and messaging.
  • The legacy KbArticle, KbArticleComment and KbArticleTemplate tables have been inaccessible since December 1, 2020; use KnowledgeArticle.

Configure the Customer Knowledge Management agent

The Customer Knowledge Management (CKM) agent autonomously turns cases and case-related conversations, emails and notes into knowledge articles. Prerequisites: case or conversation tables (or a custom case table), knowledge management configured, Copilot allowed to use the internal knowledge base, pay-as-you-go set up, and flow connections for Dataverse and Copilot Studio. Then:

  1. CSAC > Support experience > Knowledge > Customer Knowledge Management Agent > Manage.
  2. Step 1: Connection References > Setup connections > Update connection references to use your connector.
  3. Step 2: Power Automate Flows > Enable.
  4. When every tile shows Ready, select Publish in Step 3: Copilot Studio Agent.

Manual fallback (make.powerapps.com > Default Solution): connection references Microsoft Dataverse CustomerServiceKnowledgeHarvest and Microsoft Copilot Studio CustomerServiceKnowledgeHarvest, three harvesting cloud flows (names are localized), and the Copilot Studio agent CustomerServiceKnowledgeHarvest published.

ModeHow it works
Real-time creation (Case and Conversations tabs)Fires when a rep resolves a case or closes a conversation. The agent compares the content with existing articles and creates one only if there is a gap. Manage rules (rule name, condition name, conditions) limit which records qualify
Creation from historical cases or conversationsSelect the option, Manage rules (optionally one custom article template per rule), Save, Save the settings page, then Start. A long-running job that cannot be stopped and processes up to 100,000 cases or conversations, so run it in batches; follow View creation process log.
  • Attributes: up to 10 one-to-one and 6 one-to-many attributes feed an article. Defaults cover the case title and description, product, subject, incident resolution, email content, conversation summary and case notes. You can remap, disable or delete all except Title and Description. Articles default to the Issue, Cause, Resolution template.
  • Compliance: set a default compliance state such as Pending so reviewers mark articles compliant first; Noncompliant articles cannot be published. The agent removes personal data from case data but may miss some.
  • Publishing: choose Automatically publish compliant articles as soon as they're created with the audience Internal target audiences (reps and Copilot) or Internal and external target audiences (external portals). Without auto publishing, set up the review draft experience: in-app notifications, rep permission to edit articles, and Timeline plus Timeline highlights on the case. Reps then open the resolved case's Timeline > Suggested actions > Review draft > Mark as reviewed.
  • Insights: with Record user interactions with AI… on (under User experience data), supervisors get the Overall performance report on the Knowledge analytics dashboard.
  • Preview Custom record types (up to five; they need a Trigger Harvesting command bar button that runs Msdyn.KnowledgeHarvest.triggerHarvest) and Automatically update existing articles (new minor version) are labelled production-ready preview; the rep-side drafts-from-cases article is titled preview too. The agent itself carries no preview label.

Integrate knowledge into portals

The portal is a Power Pages site. Only Published, unexpired articles are found there, and iframe links outside the origins allowlist show an error to portal users.

GoalConfigure
Reps share a public linkCSAC > Knowledge > Portals > Manage > Support portal connection: Use an external portal = Yes and URL format https://<support portal URL>/kb/{kbnum} ({kbnum} becomes the article number). Create the portal on your domain first
Use knowledge article attachments instead of notes attachmentsSame page > Sync knowledge article attachments to portal > Sync attachments to the portal = Yes
Show and search attachments on the sitePower Pages site setting KnowledgeManagement/DisplayNotes = true; authors use the article editor's attachment function, not Notes
Tiered visibilityContent access levels: Default, Registered Users and Premium Users exist out of the box (Default maps to the Anonymous Users and Authenticated Users web roles). Create more under Power Pages > Security > Content Access Levels, assign them to articles and to contacts, accounts or web roles, and set site setting KnowledgeManagement/ContentAccessLevel/Enabled = true (default false). Unauthorized users see "Article Unavailable"
Browse by topic and ratePower Pages > Settings > Service Management > Knowledge Base Management > Categories > New (blank parent = top level); associate with Associate Category in Customer Service Hub; Enable Ratings on the inline editor's Options tab
  • Assigning levels: in Customer Service Hub, add the form Portal Knowledge Article for Interactive experience to the Knowledge Article table, then use Content Access Levels (lock icon). Translations and new versions copy the levels, and users also inherit levels from a parent contact, account or web role.
  • Portal search: Lucene.Net search, Progressive search, Dataverse search and Faceted search. Facets are Record Type, Modified date, Rating and Products; counts are exact below 100 and show + above 100. The Customer Service article still links to "Configure Dataverse search in portals (preview)", but that link now opens the Power Pages Search overview, which has no preview label: new sites (website version 9.4.4.xx and later) use Dataverse search, Lucene .NET search is deprecated, and an existing site switches by setting Search/EnableDataverseSearch to true.
  • Copilot agent on the portal: needs Dataverse search (a system administrator enables it), articles published to the portal and a Copilot agent with a topic. Set the Microsoft Dataverse and Content Conversion connection references in make.powerapps.com, turn on the Search Dynamics 365 knowledge article flow, then use the Search Dynamics 365 knowledge articles action (or the Power Automate flow template). By default it searches external published articles: statecode eq 3 and isinternal eq false; a Filter (text) input adds conditions.
Exam traps
  • Search mode: the default is any; Set search mode as all (called Knowledge search logic in the search-concepts article) needs Dataverse search. Suggest as you type matches titles only, and recently viewed articles top out at 8, not 10.
  • External or integrated? External providers federate (SharePoint, another organization, Graph connector by connection ID) and show 3 links per provider; only integrated providers ingest static, site map websites (with lastmod) into Dataverse. The tile once called Search Providers is now External search providers.
  • Locked choices: Field Mapping versus JSON Schema cannot be changed after saving; a Draft provider cannot ingest; a trial run is capped at 1,000 records and a time-range run at 60 days.
  • Draft is not security: statecode 0 is a lifecycle stage, and Scheduled is 2. Enabling another table creates msdyn_<Entity_Name>_knowledgearticle; only cases use KnowledgeArticleIncident.
  • CKM agent: Publish in Step 3 comes last, after the connection references and flows are Ready. Historical creation cannot be stopped (up to 100,000 records), Noncompliant articles cannot be published, and custom record types and automatic updates are preview.
  • Portals: content access levels do nothing until the site setting is true (the Customer Service search article spells the name with a space; the Power Pages article has none), and attachments need KnowledgeManagement/DisplayNotes. A Copilot agent searches only published, external articles by default.
