sections.title: 6.1 Configure the Dynamics 365 Contact Center supervisor experience
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure supervisor settings • Configure the Quality Evaluation agent • Configure access to analytics and dashboards • Perform supervisor actions for conversations • Configure the supervisor app. Practise by setting the four supervisor toggles, giving a test user the Omnichannel supervisor role, running one bulk action in All ongoing conversations, publishing the Quality Evaluation agent and building a custom analytics security role.

Configure supervisor settings

Supervisor actions are gated twice: an organization setting turns each action on, and a security role makes someone a supervisor. Open Copilot Service admin center (CSAC) > Operations > Insights > Ongoing conversation insights > Manage; the Omnichannel Configuration.Supervisor Settings page opens. Set a toggle to Yes to allow the action and to No to disable it.

ToggleLets supervisors…
Supervisor Monitorwatch how representatives handle live conversations, and join them
Supervisor Assignassign conversations to representatives
Supervisor Transfertransfer conversations from one representative to another
Force Closeend voice calls and conversations on the voice and messaging channels (the name has no "Supervisor" prefix)
  • Roles: Basic User for everyone, plus Omnichannel supervisor for supervisor tasks (role assignment is covered in §1.3). The Omnichannel API access role must not be assigned to a supervisor or representative; check it first when Assign fails.
  • Decision rule: to use an action a supervisor needs both the matching toggle set to Yes and the supervisor role. The Omnichannel Ongoing Conversations dashboard needs the Omnichannel supervisor role; in Unified Service Desk the user must also be added to the supervisor configuration for the dashboard to appear on the home session tab.
  • Monitoring features are subject to employment and privacy law, must not be used to make decisions about employees, and may require notifying customers and obtaining their consent.
  • The Omnichannel intraday insights reports are documented as deprecated; use the real-time analytics reports instead.

Configure the Quality Evaluation agent

Quality evaluation uses a supervisor-defined framework to score interactions autonomously: evaluation criteria (questions, answers, scoring, guidance) → evaluation plans (which interactions, when, with which criteria; bulk evaluations) → evaluations (scores, summaries, recommended actions). On-demand evaluation needs no plan. It covers cases and closed and active conversations; evaluation for emails is Preview.

Prerequisites: the three Quality roles, connection references, Copilot credits (set up through pay-as-you-go), Enable AI agents for the environment in the Power Platform admin center, and consent for potential data movement across regions.

RoleCan
Quality Administratorconfigure the agent; create criteria and plans; complete or assign evaluations
Quality Managercreate criteria and plans; complete or assign evaluations
Quality Evaluatorcomplete or assign evaluations
  1. CSAC > Customer Support > Quality management > Quality evaluation > Manage.
  2. Prerequisites tiles: Step 1: Connection References (Manage connections > Update connection references to use your connector), Step 2: Power Automate Flows (enable any flow that is off), then Publish in Step 3: Copilot Studio Agent once all tiles show Ready.
  3. Enablement by record type: Case, Conversation or Email; tick Enable bulk evaluations for bulk case evaluation. In Specify data, Email needs the Description field; Add data allows up to 10 one-to-one and 6 one-to-many data types beyond the defaults.
  4. Evaluation criteria score: Enable scoring for criteria > Turn on (it cannot be turned off afterwards), choose the threshold value out of 100, Save.
Item (Copilot Service workspace)Rules
Evaluation criteriaBuilt-in Support quality and Closed Conversations Default Criteria are prefilled, published and read-only. Answer types: Yes/No, Multi-select, Single-select, Descriptive. Section weights total 100%; each question scores 0 to 100. The language is fixed once saved. A critical question needs an answer marked Mark as fail. Save, then Publish
Evaluation method (plan or on demand)AI agent: every question has AI response enabled; no manual editing. AI assisted: at least one AI-enabled question; assigned to a team or user. Manual: no AI. Evaluations fail when the criteria lack AI-enabled questions for the chosen mode
Evaluation planRecord type Conversations (frequency Trigger on Closed conversations, Recurring daily, or Once) or Cases (recurring daily with Sampling: Absolute Number of 1 or more, or Percentage; Top or Bottom; Sample by Representative; or a trigger on resolved cases). Active plans cannot be edited: pause first; record type and criteria never change. A batch run handles up to 20,000 records
On-demand evaluationRequest from the case grid (up to 20 cases) or from closed conversations
  • Historical analytics: CSAC > Insights > Quality evaluation agent analytics > Manage > Enable Quality Evaluation Agent historical Analytics.
  • Do not confuse: Quality and coaching (CSAC > Customer Support > Quality and coaching) is a separate, Contact Center-only skill that needs the Omnichannel Administrator role and consumption-based billing and uses a quality library of indicators and guardrails. Governance (Customer Service only) and screen and call recording are other Quality Management Agent skills.

Configure access to analytics and dashboards

Two separate steps: enable a report family in CSAC, then grant access with roles. By default only System Administrator or supervisor-role users open analytics; give anyone else access by assigning a security role in the Power Platform admin center (customizing the reports is §6.2).

DashboardGrant Read on this table
Omnichannel real-time analyticsmsdyn_dataanalyticsreport_oc_rt
Omnichannel historical analyticsmsdyn_dataanalyticsreport_oc
Real-time analytics for record routingmsdyn_dataanalyticsreport_ur_recordrouting_rt
Customer Service historical analyticsmsdyn_dataanalyticsreport_csrmanager
Copilot analyticsmsdyn_dataanalyticsreport_copilot
Knowledge analyticsmsdyn_dataanalyticsreport_ksinsights
  1. Power Platform admin center > the environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > New role.
  2. Enter the name and business unit and set Member's privilege inheritance; Save.
  3. Open the role, use the Custom Tables dropdown and grant Read (Permission Settings) on the tables above. A custom role also needs Read on the tables that the historical and real-time analytics use.
NeedDo
Everything for a supervisorAssign the supervisor role
One dashboard only (for example a quality analyst)Custom role with Read on that dashboard's table
Users save report bookmarksCreate, Read, Write and Delete on the Report Bookmark custom table
Users edit reportsThe Analytics Report Author role
  • Enable (CSAC > Operations > Insights): Real-time Analytics > Manage > Enable Omnichannel real-time analytics (on by default; options for voice, intent and bot); Omnichannel historical analytics > Manage > Enable Omnichannel historical analytics report first, then the add-on dashboards, with metrics appearing 24 hours later; Customer Service historical analytics > Manage > Enable Customer Service historical analytics report.
  • Defaults: real-time reports are on for System Administrator, Omnichannel Administrator, Omnichannel Supervisor, Analytics Reports author and CSR manager. Configuring Omnichannel historical analytics needs System Administrator, Omnichannel Administrator, Omnichannel Supervisor or CSR Manager.

Perform supervisor actions for conversations

Supervisors act from the Ongoing conversation report of the Omnichannel real-time analytics dashboard in Copilot Service workspace, for digital messaging, chat and voice only, after the matching toggles are Yes (§2.3 covers the same view from the channel side).

ActionAllowed when
Monitor and joinDigital conversations in Active or Wrap-up; voice only in Active (the ongoing conversation report article also lists conversations in a waiting state); never a conversation assigned to you. Joining lets you message both the rep and the customer
AssignThe conversation is Open and not assigned. You can override the rep's presence and capacity (the units exceeded are shown); the target is a rep or a queue
TransferActive or Waiting on messaging channels (Live Chat, SMS, WhatsApp); not after the conversation switches to elevated voice or video; between representatives only, never AI agents. The first rep becomes a consultant and the transfer completes when the second rep acknowledges the notification by selecting Accept or Reject
Force closeVoice calls and messaging conversations; the status becomes Closed
  • Voice (Omnichannel Supervisor role): Monitor without being seen; Consult sends private messages hidden from the customer and does not affect your capacity; Join call (barge) notifies the rep.
  • Bulk actions: Copilot Service workspace > Conversations > All ongoing conversations, up to 1,000 conversations at once, Omnichannel Supervisor role. Assign (open live and persistent chats, to a queue), Force Close (persistent and live chats that are open, active, wrap-up or waiting), Message Customer (open persistent chats then move to Waiting) and Notify CSR. Messages are limited to 1,000 characters and outcomes appear in Action History.
  • Notify CSR also needs the supervisor role with prvSendAppNotification at Organization level, and reps with the Omnichannel agent role plus prvReadAppNotification and Read. Only administrators can delete items.
  • Assign fails although the toggle is Yes → look for the Omnichannel API access role on the supervisor.

Configure the supervisor app

The study guide names no page for this bullet, so know the supervisor surfaces the documentation describes and their status.

SurfaceStatus and requirements
Copilot Service workspace (Service analytics, Conversations)Generally available. Roles Basic User + Omnichannel supervisor; the supervisor toggles apply; a customized workspace app needs the real-time report page added in App Designer (§6.2)
Real-time streaming analytics supervisor experience PreviewProduction-ready preview, Dynamics 365 Contact Center only. Needs Omnichannel for Contact Center configured, the Omnichannel Supervisor role, and channels that generate live data
Workforce Engagement Management app PreviewStandalone app that combines workforce and quality management; does not replace Copilot Service workspace; needs the Workforce Management for Customer Service package (Power Platform admin center) and a role that makes the app visible
  • Access: the streaming experience is a separate web page at portal.<geo>.contactcenterai.powerplatform.com/experience/supervisor (first-release environments use portal.<geo>.fre.contactcenterai.powerplatform.com/experience/supervisor), chosen by environment type and region. It is event-driven rather than a scheduled-refresh dashboard.
  • Six views: Wallboard (consolidated metrics; trend indicators refresh every five minutes), Assisted Service (trends and service metrics), Queues (backlog, wait times, service level, abandon rate), Representatives (presence, workload, update queue membership, reset presence, 24 hours of presence history), Conversations (tabs All, Ongoing, Closed; bulk Assign to a representative, Transfer to another queue or representative, Force close; search by subject, customer or representative) and Self Service (containment, escalation, intents, languages).
  • Filters: Period, Channel, Business Unit (applies to every tab; All business units is organization-wide) and Queues; Representative exists only in the Representatives view. Live metrics (active conversations, queue backlog, online representatives, longest wait) ignore Period; aggregated metrics (service level, abandon rate, average speed to answer) follow it.
  • Thresholds: Normal, At risk (amber) and Critical (red); See details shows ranges, definitions and trendlines (not on the Wallboard). The display language follows the user-level locale, then the organization locale, then the browser locale.
Exam traps
  • Two gates: a supervisor needs the matching toggle (Supervisor Monitor, Supervisor Assign, Supervisor Transfer or Force Close) and the Omnichannel supervisor role. The toggles sit under Operations > Insights > Ongoing conversation insights, and the Omnichannel API access role must not be on the supervisor.
  • State rules: voice monitoring is Active only (digital also allows Wrap-up); Assign needs Open and unassigned; Transfer never targets an AI agent and is blocked after a switch to elevated voice or video; bulk actions cap at 1,000 conversations.
  • Quality evaluation: scoring cannot be turned off once enabled; AI agent mode needs every question AI-enabled while AI assisted needs at least one; email evaluation is preview; Publish in Step 3 works only when Steps 1 and 2 are Ready.
  • Similar names: Quality evaluation (Customer Support > Quality management) is not the Quality and coaching skill (Contact Center only, Omnichannel Administrator role). The preview roles pages write Quality Admin where the evaluation page says Quality Administrator.
  • Analytics: enabling a report (CSAC toggle) is not granting access (security role). A custom role needs Read on the matching msdyn_dataanalyticsreport_* table from the Custom Tables dropdown, bookmarks need Create, Read, Write and Delete on Report Bookmark, editing needs Analytics Report Author, and Omnichannel historical data takes 24 hours to appear.
  • Supervisor app: real-time streaming analytics is preview, Contact Center only and opened through a regional URL; its live metrics ignore the Period filter.

Sources: Enable supervisor access · Monitor, assign, transfer and end conversations · Monitor voice calls · All ongoing conversations · Assign roles · Ongoing Conversations dashboard access · Manage quality evaluation · Evaluation criteria · Evaluation plan · On-demand evaluation · Connection references · Quality evaluation historical analytics · Quality and coaching skill · Quality Management Agent overview · Configure analytics and insights dashboards · Real-time analytics reports · Omnichannel historical analytics · Real-time streaming analytics (preview) · Streaming Conversations view · Streaming Representatives view · Workforce Engagement Management app (preview)

sections.title: 6.2 Customize analytics and reporting
sections.html:
Skills measured: customize the key performance indicators (KPIs) in the analytics reports by using the embedded Power BI editor • embed out-of-the-box reports in the Copilot Service workspace app • customize historical and real-time analytics reports by using Power BI • extend historical and real-time analytics reports by using Power BI Desktop • configure conversation diagnostics in Application Insights • configure and embed telemetry and analytics from Application Insights. Practise: edit and publish a visual in Omnichannel real-time analytics, add a report page to a customized workspace app, provision a data model in a test tenant, and connect a test Application Insights resource.

Customize the KPIs in the analytics reports by using the embedded Power BI editor

The embedded Power BI editor changes how an out-of-the-box report presents data, from inside Copilot Service workspace. It works on Customer Service historical analytics, Omnichannel historical analytics, Omnichannel real-time analytics and Real-time analytics for record routing. Unified routing and knowledge analytics reports can't be customized. No license is needed to customize the first three reports, and the author needs the Analytics Report Author role (System Administrator already has it).

  1. In Copilot Service workspace open the report and select Edit report.
  2. Use Visualizations (for example show Incoming conversations as a table instead of a bar chart), Data (every KPI, measure, dimension and attribute in the model, not only those displayed, such as Participation Mode in FactSessionParticipant) and Filters (Advanced filtering; the Or option combines several queue conditions).
  3. Select Save, then Publish. After publishing, the customization is visible to all users in the organization. Resume editing continues after a publish.
  4. To undo everything: Edit report > Checkout default report > Reset (permanent).
ItemRule
Report sizeNo more than 20 metrics or tiles per report; add pages and link to them instead.
Data modelFacts (FactConversation: Average handle time; FactAgent: agent metrics) split by dimensions (DimQueue > Queue Name). Microsoft model updates don't overwrite your customizations; a renamed field may need reselecting.
Move between organizationsEdit > Export (Download export) and Import (Upload), or the APIs msdyn_ExportVisualCustomReport and msdyn_ImportVisualCustomReport. Published customizations only; the target must be the same or a higher version and have the out-of-the-box feature enabled; an import replaces existing customizations.
Personal viewsReport filters (applied to a report group) and bookmarks; no editing needed.
NeedUse
Table instead of bar chart, another existing KPI, a page for one teamEmbedded Power BI editor
New metric, different calculation logic, custom tablesData model customization with Power BI Desktop (below)
Development to productionExport and import (published only)
Exam traps
  • Save is not enough: nobody else sees the change until you Publish, and then everyone sees it. Use bookmarks for a personal view.
  • Reset permanently removes your customizations.
  • Knowledge analytics and unified routing analytics can't be edited in the embedded editor.
  • The embedded editor needs no license; model customization does (below).

Embed out-of-the-box reports in the Copilot Service workspace app

The reports appear in the standard Copilot Service workspace navigation. If you customized the app, you add each report as a page in the app designer. Enable the report in Copilot Service admin center first (§6.1: Operations > Insights); the app designer only adds navigation.

  1. Apps > Copilot Service workspace tile > More Options (ellipsis) > Open in App Designer.
  2. New > Dataverse Table > Select existing table > Omnichannel historical analytics.
  3. Select Show in navigation > Add.
  4. Navigation > the new page > Settings: Title; Icon = Use web resource with msdyn_/Analytics/imgs/OmnichannelReportIcon.svg; ID OCReportsSubArea.
  5. Advanced Settings: SKU = All, On premise, Live and SPLA; Client = Web; Outlook shortcut = Offline availability.
  6. Save, then Publish.
Page typeShowsDetails
Dataverse TableAn out-of-the-box reportAn existing table named after the report. Each report article lists its own icon and ID; real-time analytics uses the table Omnichannel Realtime analytics.
URLCustomized (Power BI data model) reports[Organization Url]/main.aspx?pagetype=control&controlName=MscrmControls.Analytics.ModernReportingControl&data={"featureIds":"..."}, Title Customized Reports, icon msdyn_/Analytics/imgs/CustomizedReportsIcon.svg, ID CustomizedReportsSubArea, Outlook shortcut = Pass parameters and Offline availability.

Keep the report state when a representative switches session tabs (customized app): app designer > Pages > Navigation > the report view (for example Omnichannel real-time analytics) > Settings > Display options > Content type = Table > Table = Omnichannel Realtime analytics > Save and Publish. Repeat for each report.

Exam traps
  • Dataverse Table pages are for the out-of-the-box reports; only the customized Power BI reports use a URL page.
  • Turning a report on in the admin center doesn't add it to a customized app; the app designer step does.
  • The Power BI template app route (Customer Service Analytics for Dynamics 365) is documented as Deprecated.

Customize historical and real-time analytics reports by using Power BI

Data model customization (embedded Power BI extensibility) goes beyond visuals: you can edit the out-of-the-box data model, add metrics, bring in Dataverse entities or other sources, publish to a Microsoft Fabric workspace you choose, add the reports to the workspace site map and refresh automatically. It needs a paid Power BI service; licensing applies to report users and authors.

Prerequisites: enable at least one historical report (Customer Service historical, Omnichannel historical or Knowledge analytics) for historical customization, and Omnichannel real-time analytics for real-time customization. A Microsoft Entra ID security group that contains the Dynamics 365 Analytics service account (Dynamics CCA Data Analytics if the first isn't available); Power BI grants permissions to groups, not to individual service principals. In the Fabric admin portal enable, for the organization or that group: Create workspaces, Service principals can call Fabric public APIs, Service principals can create workspaces, connections, and deployment pipelines, Allow DirectQuery connections to Power BI semantic models, Allow XMLA endpoints and Analyze in Excel with on-premises semantic models and Embed content in apps.

Enable: Copilot Service admin center > Operations > Insights > Report settings > Embedded Power BI extensibility - Historical data model customization (or Real-time) > Manage > Enable embedded Power BI data model customization = On.

StepTaskKey facts
1Select a Microsoft Fabric workspaceCreate new workspace or pick one (then the enabling admin must be its workspace admin); Save starts provisioning. The choice applies to the customer workspace; one workspace can serve historical and real-time.
2Provision the data modelsUp to 24 hours; Refresh checks status; needs the security group.
3Grant permissionsYou must be Workspace Administrator on both workspaces. Data model: Share with Allow recipients to build content with the data associated with this semantic model for authors and viewers. Report workspace: Contributor for authors, Viewer for other readers, Member for supervisors who view the embedded report.
4Embed customized reports (optional)Add report > name > Select Power BI report > Add > Save; maximum 40 reports. The site map is shared by historical and real-time; edit or delete a report only from the page that added it.
  • Managed workspace: Microsoft provisions it (Omnichannel Managed Workspace for real-time, Customer Service Managed Workspace for historical, each with a GUID suffix). Treat the dataset as read-only: changes are overwritten by updates. Historical data refreshes daily from Azure Data Lake (last two years processed); real-time uses TDS connectors.
  • Customer workspace: copies of the out-of-the-box reports (up to three historical, one real-time), created once and never updated. Update the semantic model manually, then refresh and redeploy custom reports.
  • Not available: knowledge analytics and unified routing analytics can't be customized; supervisor actions (assign, transfer, monitor, force close) aren't available in model-customized reports.
  • Automatic page refresh is for real-time reports only: enable it in the Fabric admin portal; download the real-time report; Visualizations > Format page > Page refresh On > Refresh type = Auto page refresh > fixed interval of 5 or 10 seconds > Publish to the customized workspace.
  • Monitoring: Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app (Compute, Timepoint, Item Detail) and Performance Analyzer.
Exam traps
  • The order is workspace, provision, permissions, embed; embedding is optional.
  • Supervisors need Member to see an embedded report; Contributor is for authors, Viewer for other readers.
  • Provisioning fails without the Entra security group that holds the Dynamics 365 Analytics service account.
  • Auto refresh: real-time only, fixed interval of 5 or 10 seconds.

Extend historical and real-time analytics reports by using Power BI Desktop

With data model customization enabled and the Power BI permissions granted, build on the managed-workspace dataset instead of recreating metrics.

  • New report: Power BI Desktop > File > New > Get data > Power BI semantic models > choose the historical or real-time data model from the managed workspace > Connect > build > File > Publish.
  • Existing report: Power BI service > report in your workspace > File > Download this file > a copy with a live connection to data online > Get data > Power BI semantic models > the managed-workspace dataset > edit > Publish. To edit the out-of-the-box copy, download it from the customer workspace.
NeedDo
A variant or different logic on existing entities (150-second service level; handle time that includes consult time)Right-click the entity (for example FactConversation) > New measure > DAX > save > use it in a visual > publish.
Extra attributes, custom entities or other applications' dataModeling > Make changes to this model > Add a local model (a DirectQuery link to the Dynamics model, giving a composite model) > Connect to your data > Submit > Dataverse (more Dynamics attributes) or another source > Transform data > Manage relationship > DAX > publish.
Rename an existing columnRequires a new local model.
Service level (150 seconds) =
DIVIDE (
    SUMX ( FactConversation,
        IF ( FactConversation[ConversationFirstWaitTimeInSeconds] <= 150
             && FactConversation[IsAgentAccepted]
             && NOT FactConversation[DirectionCode], 1, 0 ) ),
    SUMX ( FactConversation,
        IF ( FactConversation[IsAgentAccepted]
             && NOT FactConversation[DirectionCode], 1, 0 ) ),
    BLANK ()
)

Set the format to Percentage and replace the Service level (60 seconds) tile on the Summary Report page. In the documented title example, a local model reads the Dataverse system user table (named UserTitle) and a relationship links DimAgent to it by agent ID. Pull only the data you need; Import or DirectQuery mode is your choice, and DirectQuery suits real-time reports. Don't use hidden out-of-the-box fact or dimension fields, which can change or be removed.

Exam traps
  • Pick the dataset from the managed workspace, and download existing reports with a live connection.
  • A new measure on existing fields needs only DAX; extra tables or columns need a local model.
  • Don't edit the managed dataset: it is overwritten by updates.
  • Composite models depend on the DirectQuery and XMLA tenant settings.

Configure conversation diagnostics in Application Insights

Conversation diagnostics logs each lifecycle event of a conversation to Azure Application Insights. Export isn't available in sovereign clouds (GCC, GCC High, DoD). Prerequisites: Contributor or higher on the Azure services to set up; at least Read to query Application Insights; Power Platform administrator or System Administrator; the environment must be a managed environment.

Guided setup: Copilot Service admin center > Operations > Insights > Observability settings > Conversation lifecycle diagnostics > Manage.

  1. Provision Application Insights in Azure; copy the App ID (Overview > JSON View); select I've provisioned Application Insights and have the connection string ready.
  2. Connect Application Insights with your org: confirm the resource is connected to your environment and select Application Insights is connected to my organization.
  3. Provide Application Insights ID and provision resources: enter the App ID > Provision > copy the 3P Application Name. The guided setup creates the app and federated identity credential, sets the environment variable and validates the connection. In Azure check API permissions: Application Insights Read must be Granted (otherwise Grant admin consent).
  4. Assign the Monitoring Reader role to the 3P app: Azure portal > the Application Insights resource > Access control (IAM).
  5. Select Test connection.
  • Data export connection (Power Platform admin center): Manage > Data export > App Insights tab > New data export > export package name > Dynamics Customer Service > the environment (managed only) > subscription, resource group and Application Insights instance > Create. Only one Customer Service export configuration per environment. The articles don't spell out how this and the guided setup relate; know both.
  • View: Copilot Service workspace > Conversations > select one > Diagnose (channel, queue, distribution mode and events; select a Classification or Route to queue event to see the applied condition, the condition that wasn't evaluated and the final output). For a case use Cases > Diagnose to review routing attempts (§4.2).
  • Cost: Application Insights bills ingested data (Basic and Analytic log plans). Averages: 7 KB per routed work item with one classification, one route-to-queue and one assignment ruleset, 2 KB per ruleset with one rule, 1 KB per extra rule; 500 items a day is about 4.88 MB.
Traces
| extend customDim = parse_json(customDimensions)
| extend conversationId = tostring(customDim["powerplatform.analytics.resource.id"]),
         subscenario = tostring(customDim["powerplatform.analytics.subscenario"])
| where tostring(customDim["powerplatform.analytics.scenario"]) == "ConversationDiagnosticsScenario"
| project timestamp, conversationId, subscenario
Exam traps
  • A non-managed environment can't be used; Contributor sets it up, Read only queries it.
  • The data export is created in the Power Platform admin center (one per environment); the guided setup lives in Copilot Service admin center.
  • The 3P app needs the Monitoring Reader role on the resource and a Granted Application Insights Read permission.
  • Events land in the Traces table; the subscenario value names the lifecycle stage. The older routing diagnostics tab is documented as deprecated.

Configure and embed telemetry and analytics from Application Insights

The Diagnose dashboard surfaces Application Insights telemetry in Copilot Service workspace so supervisors needn't write KQL. Open Omnichannel Realtime analytics or Real-time analytics for record routing and select Diagnose on the command bar; a new session tab shows the Debug page. Roles: Omnichannel supervisor or CSR Manager for the Omnichannel real-time dashboard, CSR Manager for record routing. The real-time dashboard must be enabled, and data needs about 24 hours to sync fully.

  1. System administrator: configure Application Insights, conversation diagnostics and the connection (previous section).
  2. Put the Application Insights ID in the environment variable's Default Value and Current Value.
  3. Register an app (copy the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID) and add a federated identity credential: Issuer https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/v2.0, Type Explicit subject identifier, Audience api://AzureADTokenExchange, Name the app name, Value the plug-in subject. If msdyn_GetAppInsightsTelemetry fails, read its failed response in the browser Network tab to correct the value.
  4. Assign Monitoring Reader to the app.
  5. Update the managed identity record with the app's applicationid and tenantid (a PATCH to /api/data/v9.0/managedidentities(<id>) from the browser console).
  6. Power Apps > Default Solution (or your solution) > Objects > Setting > Setting definition > Enable Application Insights Dashboard > Yes in Default value and Setting environment value > save.
Capability or limitDetail
Trends and timelineConversations over 24 hours or a custom range by channel and queue; full conversation timeline
AssignmentAssignment time (P95); View by time to assign; View by assignment events; non-assignment reasons; service representative skills, capacity and presence; raw events
LimitsOut-of-the-box assignment methods only (presence, capacity, skills checks); up to 15 minutes of delay; transfer and consult conversations aren't supported

For custom dashboards, use the Export option to combine Application Insights data with other data sets, or run KQL and Azure Data Explorer dashboards (the docs have sample queries for fallback queues, overflow, rejected assignments and transfers).

Exam traps
  • Diagnose exists twice: on Conversations (one conversation's events) and on Omnichannel Realtime analytics (the Debug dashboard).
  • The dashboard also needs the Enable Application Insights Dashboard setting (both value fields), the app, credential, role and managed identity record; the data export alone isn't enough.
  • Transfer and consult conversations, and custom (non-out-of-the-box) assignment methods, aren't diagnosed.
  • The guided setup page says it creates the app, credential and environment variable, while the Enable Diagnose dashboard page lists them as prerequisites; the docs don't reconcile the two, so know both lists.

sections.title: Study habits that work
sections.html:
• Build, then read. Do the task in the product first, then read the section to see what you missed.
  • Memorize exact names: menu paths, settings, limits, roles and (for code) object, method and attribute names.
  • Practise the decision, not just the definition. For every feature write "choose it when / do not choose it when".
  • Keep a trap log. Every missed question becomes one line: what I picked and why it was wrong.
  • Use the Missed filter in Quick drill until it is empty, then re-take the full exam.
  • Read documentation dated 2026. Features were renamed and moved between preview and GA recently.

sections.title: Exam-day plan
sections.html:
The week before

  • Take the full timed practice exam twice, a few days apart; fix every skill rated below 4.
  • Skim the cheat sheets and your trap log — do not start new topics.
  • Run the exam sandbox (aka.ms/examdemo) once so flagging, the review screen and the case-study layout are familiar.
  • Online exam? Run Pearson VUE's system test, clear your desk and room and have government ID ready. Test center? Confirm the address and arrival time.
  • Re-check the official study guide in case Microsoft revised the skills list.

During the exam

TopicApproach
PacingWith 40–60 questions in 120 minutes you have roughly 2.0–3.0 minutes per question. Do not spend more than about 3 minutes on one item in the first pass.
First passAnswer what you know, flag what you do not. Answer every question before time runs out — an unanswered item cannot earn credit.
EliminationCross out answers that use retired, renamed or wrong-direction features. Many questions have two plausible options — look for the deciding constraint (GA versus Preview, required role, prerequisite, order of steps).
Multi-selectCount how many answers are requested ("Select TWO"); each must be independently correct.
Configuration itemsCheck the exact setting, scope, role or sequence the requirement names before choosing between similar options.
Case studiesSkim the questions first, then read the scenario for the requirements and constraints that matter. Re-read the exhibit instead of relying on memory. Breaks are allowed in case studies, but you cannot return to questions seen before the break.
Microsoft Learn buttonOn associate and expert exams Microsoft Learn opens in a split screen (no extra time; Q&A, practice assessments and your profile are blocked). Use it only to confirm one detail with Ctrl+F; if you cannot find it in about 90 seconds, make your best choice and flag it.
BreaksThe clock keeps running during a break, and after a break you cannot go back to earlier questions. You cannot break in the middle of a lab or a problem/solution question set. Use the restroom before you start.
ReviewUse the review screen for flagged items. Change an answer only if you can name the specific fact that makes your first choice wrong.
